538567|2026-03.headline: Gulf Oil Q4 FY26 posted record quarter: 45,000 KL lubricant volume (+14%), EBITDA INR 135 crore, FY26 revenue above INR 4,000 crore.
538567|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly volume, revenue and EBITDA for Q4 FY26, with lubricant volume up about 14% and revenue up about 14%. FY26 lubricant volume grew 10.5% to 1,68,000 KL, and consolidated revenue crossed INR 4,000 crore for the first time. Margin pressure is building from the Middle East crisis and rupee depreciation, with crude moving from about USD 65-70 in February to USD 90-120 in March onward. Management is prioritising supply security and per-litre price pass-through, and is holding its 12-14% EBITDA margin band as the target. The Board recommended a record FY26 dividend of INR 51 per share, including a INR 30 final.

segments.name: Passenger car motor oils
segments.commentary: Delivered double-digit growth in Q4; management wants to grow faster here given lower market share.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth in Q4; all vehicle categories reported positive growth in FY26.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Robust double-digit growth in Q4.

segments.name: OEM franchisee workshops / B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Strong double-digit growth across 40+ OEM partnerships (management cites 50-55 OEMs); industrial growing consistently at double digits.

segments.name: Tirex (EV charging subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Crossed INR 100 crore revenue in FY26; holds at least 35-40% share of new bus DC charger orders; supplies MG Motors and VinFast for AC chargers. Stake raised from 51% to 65% for INR 38 crore; new plant due Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Lubricant volume growth targeted at 2-3x industry; industry growth assumed about 3-4% (Systematix cited 8-9% industry).
EBITDA margin band of 12-14% to be protected; management said 14-16% is a challenge in the current environment.
Chennai capacity expansion expected Q3 FY27 and Silvassa expansion Q4 FY27; management said timelines are on track.
Distribution growth target of 10-15% in both urban and rural areas.
Tirex new plant expected to be operational in Q3 FY27; funding via a mix of equity and borrowings.
Margins may move toward the lower or higher end of the band as realisations rise sharply.
capex_capacity: Chennai plant capacity expansion on track; expected to come on stream first, targeted by Q3 FY27.
Silvassa plant expansion on track; civil work under way, targeted by Q4 FY27.
Tirex building a new plant, expected to be running in Q3 FY27; funded by equity and borrowings plus working capital.
Tirex stake raised from 51% to 65% in FY26 for INR 38 crore.
Base oil stock held at 45-60 days (normal 45 days), raised by 10-15 days for supply security.
demand_pricing: Demand robust across segments; March-end saw extra demand partly from supply-security buying by OEMs and channel. Management says Jan-Feb also grew double digit.
Management said the channel stocking effect was real but not the whole story, with demand continuing into April-May.
Multiple price increases taken in response to crude and input costs; management says input costs now reprice in 1-2 weeks versus about 2 months earlier.
Base oil sourced mainly from South Korea and Singapore refiners; allocation of 80-90% received from some refiners. No major supply disruption so far.
Management says price increases are being passed through per litre, though percentage margin may fluctuate.
Management declined to quantify Castrol's like-for-like price premium, and said it cannot know Castrol's base oil procurement advantage.

Data centre cooling: two products (PAO-based synthetic and mineral-based) developed and made in India; material compatibility tests done, data-centre trials next. Management says volume will be small.

qa_highlights.question: What strategic levers are prioritised for FY27 in lubricants, OEM partnerships and EV-ready fluids?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing segment-wise focus under 'Unlock 2.0' (accelerate, premiumise, transform), with digital initiatives, mechanic outreach and EV fluids for more than 30 OEMs. It aims to grow margins through premium products.

qa_highlights.question: What capital allocation and risk framework applies to dividends, R&D, hedging and liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Global R&D is funded by Gulf globally, so no direct P&L hit in India. Payout was lifted from 30-40% three to four years ago to c.72% for FY26, as cash builds and M&A and Tirex funding are still ahead.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Chennai and Silvassa expansions on schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Chennai is expected by Q3 and Silvassa by Q4 FY27; civil work at Silvassa is progressing.

qa_highlights.question: Are base oil availability and price rises hitting margins in Q1-Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to hold the 12-14% margin band and has cost levers. Supply has held so far, but a prolonged crisis could squeeze refiner supply chains. Prices are being raised repeatedly.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 volume driven by channel stocking or sustainable demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said double-digit growth ran through the year, with March-end boosted by supply-security buying from OEMs and distributors. Demand remains good into April-May.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook and revenue timing for data-centre cooling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume will be low and timing depends on which data centres are targeted; no revenue timing given.

risks_watch: Crude and base oil price volatility: crude moved from USD 65-70 to USD 90-120; margin band of 12-14% at risk if pass-through lags.
Supply: about 50% of base oil is imported from Korea, Singapore and the Middle East; a prolonged crisis could tighten refiner allocations (currently 80-90%).
Rupee depreciation keeping input costs elevated.
Tirex: bus-segment growth below expectation; new plant and working capital needs require funding via equity and borrowings.
Data-centre cooling products: commercial timing and volume undisclosed; management says volume will be small.
Brand and pricing: management declined to quantify Castrol's premium; the gap in EBITDA margin versus the market leader remains wide.
538567|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volume and demand, with a strong Q4 and FY26 record. Cautious on margins and supply, with management repeatedly calling the situation volatile and declining to quantify the Castrol premium or the price hike.
key_quotes: Extremely delighted to share with you that Q4 has been a record quarter for us in terms of our volumes, revenues and EBITDA.
And I think all the actions are being taken to ensure supplies to our customers and consumers because our customers should not suffer.
I think ensuring supply security is the most critical part, and pricing is the secondary thing.
So overall, we have been a cash generating company.
We are a growth company.

538567|2026-06.headline: Gulf Oil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR 1,320 crore and EBITDA 35% to INR 170 crore, with lubes volume up 17% to 48,000 KL.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever; no YoY figure stated
Inventory up INR 108 crore QoQ per analyst; management attributed to valuation rise, not gains

segments.name: B2C (retail/channel)
segments.commentary: Grew double digits; PCMO (passenger car) led, with gains in agriculture, commercial vehicles and motorcycles. Around 55% of sales mix.

segments.name: OEM
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth; agriculture (Mahindra, Swaraj) in franchisee workshops and motorcycles (Bajaj) led. Around 45% B2B combined with B2B.

segments.name: B2B (industry, infra, mining)
segments.commentary: Growth across customer base with new customer acquisitions in infra; combined B2B share about 45% of sales. Marine also grew double digit.

segments.name: AdBlue
segments.commentary: 40,000 KL in Q1; top-3 supplier in India; low realisation with single-digit margin, guided to mid-single-digit margin going forward.

segments.name: Tirex (EV DC/AC chargers)
segments.commentary: Q1 subdued as e-bus depot orders slowed; management expects H1 revenue positive with most growth in Q2 and Q3. Holds 8-10% share in DC charger business per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume growth partly anticipatory buying, and how will it normalise in Q2-Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply security drove some stocking; industry grew 3-4%, and Gulf expects to keep 2-3x industry growth. Monsoon quarter Jul-Sep is seasonally softer for B2C, but OEM buying continues.

qa_highlights.question: Has EBITDA margin guidance of 12-14% been revisited given per-litre EBITDA rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish said percentage margins are diluted in inflation; per-litre margin is the priority. The 12-14% band is still intact on a long-term basis, with 14-16% targeted via premiumisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any inventory gain in margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The company uses weighted-average costing and does not play on inventory; pass-through is immediate in theory, with timing lags.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on base oil supply and cost into July-August?
qa_highlights.answer: Base oil has not eased with crude; Hormuz is still almost shut. Company has long-term refiner tie-ups plus spot sourcing and 30-45 days base oil inventory; prices reviewed monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Operating expense fall of ~190 bps as share of revenue: drivers, and A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said A&P is still around 3% of revenue, not cut significantly; savings came from fixed-cost absorption and other optimisation. Absolute A&P in rupees not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Tirex: CPO plans and competitive landscape?
qa_highlights.answer: Tirex is not in CPO business; it manufactures chargers for charge point manufacturers. CPO entry evaluated at an appropriate time, not near term.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided at 2-3x industry growth (industry ~3-4%), i.e., roughly double-digit volume growth; management says Q1 17% growth was higher than normal.
EBITDA margin band of 12-14% reiterated on a long-term basis; per-litre EBITDA is the primary focus during inflation; medium-term move to 14-16% band linked to premiumisation.
Full price-increase reflection expected in Q2 or Q3 as pipeline inventory clears; B2C pricing takes 1-2 months to fully flow through.
Silvassa and Chennai capacity expansion (70% increase) phased: Chennai on track for Q3 (December), Silvassa augmented production by FY-end (March 2027).
EV business guided at INR 300-400 crore in 3-4 years, dependent on e-bus tenders materialising over next 1-2 years.
Monsoon quarter (Jul-Sep) expected to be seasonally softer for B2C but management expects a positive, good-growth quarter; July described as normal.
capex_capacity: Silvassa and Chennai expansion, announced as 70% capacity increase; phased commissioning in Q3 and Q4. Chennai on track (by December); Silvassa augmented output expected by financial year end.
Tirex moving to a new, upgraded plant to increase capacity; management says capacity should cover INR 300-400 crore revenue ambition.
Base oil inventory held for at least 30-45 days; Silvassa plant operating normally with no production impact from local flooding.
demand_pricing: Q1 volume growth 17% YoY vs industry ~3-4%; management attributes part of growth to customers securing supply amid Hormuz disruption (pre-buying/stocking).

Pricing: B2C saw close to three price increases from end-March/April, roughly monthly; B2B repriced in 2-3 staggered stages via formula and negotiation. Another retail price increase effective 1 July.
Base oil prices: crude fell from above $100 to below $85, but base oil prices have not fallen similarly; some grades (Group III, high-end) still rising; others softened in the last month.

Competition: management reports no change in pricing discipline or promotional intensity; price increases industry-wide described as unprecedented. Management states Gulf is taking some pricing leadership in certain B2C products.
Management says it has not seen demand destruction yet; elasticity risk noted at a certain price point, especially motorcycles.
risks_watch: Strait of Hormuz disruption and base oil availability; Group III and high-end base oil prices still rising.
Full price pass-through lag: Q2/Q3 margin depends on pricing actions and possible B2C price rollbacks as costs ease.
Demand elasticity and down-trading in B2C if unprecedented price increases persist, especially motorcycles.
Monsoon-season softness in Jul-Sep; sustainability of 17% volume growth after supply-security stocking.
Tirex execution: e-bus tender timing and H1/Q2 revenue ramp; EV revenue target depends on tenders in next 1-2 years.
Inventory built up (about INR 108-109 crore per analyst) and its valuation effect on reported margins.
key_quotes: We've been able to keep the margin at 13%, which is within the guided range.
So, we would term it as a volume-led profitable growth for the quarter is what we have been able to achieve with a lot of emphasis on the supply security.
We would say Strait of Hormuz is still like almost shut. So it's very difficult to say how the things will move.
Gulf has done very well. We've been able to get whatever we gauge.

538567|2026-09.headline: Gulf Oil Q2 FY27 core lubricant volume up 16% to 47,000 KL, revenue up 44%, EBITDA up 37%, margin 11.8% just below 12-14% band.
538567|2026-09.overview: Gulf Oil reported Q2 FY27 volume growth of about 16% (core lubes 47,000 KL vs 40,500 KL) and revenue growth of 44%, with EBITDA up 37% YoY. EBITDA margin was 11.8%, close to the guided 12-14% band, and management said per-litre margins were protected despite input cost inflation from crude and base oil. Working capital rose in absolute terms on higher prices, though days stayed within the 95-105 day band. A fire at Valsad cost about 4-5 days of production, which is insured.

vs INR 321 crore in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Lubricants - B2C (channel)
segments.commentary: B2C grew about 2x the market in H1 per management; outlets grew 16% YoY. Management targets at least 2x market growth going forward.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue of INR 33 crore+, up 78% YoY. Capacity to rise to 3,000 chargers by end of this year; the Chennai/plant expansion targeted for the coming quarter.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27: management expects the industry to grow about 3-4% and Gulf to grow 2x-3x that, implying close to double-digit volume growth in H2. Agri demand is currently weak.
Margin: medium-term trajectory back to 14-16% EBITDA margin, but management said this is not a 1-2 quarter story; focus is on per-litre margin protection.
Pricing: base oil has not yet shown the recent crude rally ($100 to $115); if crude sustains, price hikes segment-wise may follow in about 40-50 days. Base oil inventory held for 45-60 days.
Working capital: management said the current level is near peak if prices hold; incremental H2 cash generation should flow to cash flow rather than working capital.

Capex: Chennai expansion on track for completion by end of the quarter. Silvassa expansion may slip 1-2 months into Q1 FY28 (earlier target March 2027). Total expansion capex now about INR 60-62 crore (from INR 55 crore).

demand_pricing: Volume growth driven by OEM, franchisee workshops and B2B industrial; supply security was a focus given input supply challenges.

Price increases taken in calibrated fashion: 3 price increases taken in channel (B2C) so far; OEM contracts have quarterly price variation clauses, with monthly variations during the last 6 months; B2B requires negotiation and takes longer.

538635|2026-03.headline: Snowman Logistics Q4 FY26 call: West Asia disruption keeps volumes subdued; FY26 double-stack share averaged 40%, Q4 at 42%, with margins pressured by start-up warehouses and domestic ramp-up costs.
538635|2026-03.overview: Management described volumes as still subdued in Q4 and April due to the West Asia conflict, with import cargo from US, Europe and Middle East and export food cargo hit. Snowman's EBITDA and EBIT per TEU and margins fell year on year and quarter on quarter, which management attributed to start-up warehouses (Kolkata, Krishnapatnam) with high power costs, DG running costs, stabling and empty haulage costs, one-time 5PL import procurement, and domestic ramp-up upfront costs. Management reiterated a INR1,000 crore revenue target for Snowman (15% blended EBITDA margin, about INR150 crore EBITDA) but said it may slip about a year, with FY29 seen as more realistic. Capex guidance for FY27 is about INR50 crore, and gross debt at Gateway is expected to keep declining.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise about 12% to 13% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of headcount additions ahead of Ankleshwar and domestic scale-up, plus retention bonuses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Snowman gross and EBITDA margins fall and COGS rise about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Start-up warehouse costs (Kolkata, Krishnapatnam), DG power costs, stabling and empty haulage costs, upfront domestic costs, and one-time 5PL import procurement. Management said COGS relates to trading, which grew 23%.

qa_highlights.question: Capex in FY26 and FY27 guidance?

qa_highlights.answer: FY27 principal repayments about INR30 crore; lease rent about INR40 crore for the year, charged to P&L, with no separate lease principal repayment.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt trajectory and use of cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt to keep declining; capex plans (rakes, EVs, solar, reach stackers, warehouses, Indore and Jaipur) absorb cash; dividends to continue; no near-term stake increase in Snowman.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15% rail growth achievable given historical 4% to 5% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rail grew about 10% last year, exceeding market growth, and cited new ICDs (Ankleshwar, Indore, Jaipur) and domestic volumes as drivers.

qa_highlights.answer: Owns about 250 to 260 vehicles and leases about 200; plans to add vehicles; a transport management system going live within about a month for trip-level profitability tracking.

538635|2026-06.headline: Snowman guides 10-15% top-line growth for FY27 despite war-driven volume dip; Gateway ICD volumes stagnant, DFC-JNPT link now complete.
538635|2026-06.overview: Joint Gateway Distriparks and Snowman Logistics call covering Q1 FY27. Management attributed the volume softness to the West Asia conflict (since April), which cut imports sharply in April-May, and to July weather disruptions at ports; market share is described as intact while the underlying market has de-grown. Snowman pricing rose 5-7% on average across warehousing customers, and management guided 10-15% top-line growth across all segments. Rail EBITDA was pressured by lower double-stacking (39% vs 40-42% earlier), higher underframe and empty running, and wage and fuel inflation, with relief expected from Q2. Management reported no specific Q1 financial figures in the call.

financial_highlights.change: reached after special dividend paid earlier this year
about 95% are customs bonds to government authorities

segments.commentary: Market share intact but market de-grew in operating regions; JNPT exposure about 5% of rail volume. Rail EBITDA per TEU fell on lower double-stacking, higher empty running and underframe usage, and wage and fuel costs.

segments.name: Snowman warehousing
segments.commentary: Pricing up 5-7% on average; about 24,000 additional pallets expected by end of FY27 (Pune first, then Patna).

segments.name: Snowman 5PL
segments.commentary: Service margin typically 5-6%; no new 5PL customer added in Q1, with new names possibly by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: CFS (Gateway)
segments.commentary: Volumes improved and a pricing increase taken to offset fuel and wage hikes; margin uplift possible in Q2. Management is not actively pursuing a sale.

segments.name: Domestic transport (Snowman)
segments.commentary: Around 500 containers a month currently, with scope to scale as network expands.

Gateway land bank about 475 acres across India, mostly freehold; Garhi land (85-90 acres) indicated at INR 25-30 crore per acre on outright purchase basis.
Ankleshwar is expected to be a new EXIM location, currently served by one ICD estimated at about 5,000 TEU, with a 3-4 year ramp to a similar scale.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict since April cut imports sharply in April-May; imports improved from June-July, but July volumes were hit by weather-related port and double-stacking restrictions at Mundra and JNPT.
Management said June and July trends were similar to Q1 and declined to give specific monthly figures, citing listed-company restrictions.
Shipping lines reportedly prefer single-dip over double-dip on the West Coast, which could shift some volume to JNPT; management described this as early, exploratory.
JNPT is about 6 rail slabs more expensive than Mundra for North-bound rail haulage; industry talk of special haulage relief is unconfirmed.
Warehousing market shifting from unorganised to organised; competitive intensity described as ongoing, with CONCOR the largest rail competitor.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gateway's ICD market share holding given the stagnant volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share is intact and the market itself has de-graded due to the war; double-digit growth for the year is still expected once the situation clears.

qa_highlights.question: How much MAT credit supports the low cash tax rate, and when does full tax apply?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kartik Aiyer said the company will pay at 18.88% for at least 7-8 years, using accumulated MAT credit; management noted cash tax rose only INR 1-2 crore YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why has rail EBITDA per TEU weakened, and what is the fix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower import share, lower double-stacking, higher underframe and empty running, port imbalance at Mundra and Pipavav, and steep wage hikes (Haryana up 35%); recovery expected as volumes return, with fuel impact visible in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the JNPT exposure and the economics of shifting to it?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPT is about 5% of rail volume; on current pricing it is more expensive for North-bound customers but yields higher revenue and slightly higher EBITDA per TEU for Gateway due to distance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the CFS business and its land?
qa_highlights.answer: A sale was explored about 1.5 years ago without a satisfactory valuation; no active process now, though management is open to a good offer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value of the land bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a formal valuation; cited Garhi (85-90 acres) at INR 25-30 crore per acre on outright purchase, with total land of about 475 acres.

538635|2026-09.headline: Snowman Logistics Q2 FY27 call: pallets stored up ~10% YoY, ~23,000 pallets being added, FY27 EBITDA seen crossing INR100 crore; PAT remains thin.
538635|2026-09.overview: This was a joint Gateway Distriparks and Snowman Logistics Q2 FY27 call, with Snowman questions covering warehousing, 5PL, capex and margins. Management said pallets stored rose close to 10% YoY, with warehousing revenue growing about 10-11%, while utilisation held at 85% against a targeted 88-89%. 5PL grew only 1-2% as one major customer declined and another grew, and no new 5PL customer was added this fiscal. Management said Snowman is on track to cross INR100 crore EBITDA this year but gave no firm PAT trajectory, citing reinvestment-driven interest and depreciation. On the Gateway side, management guided to a 100,000 TEU-per-quarter rail-volume floor and double-digit growth for next year, with Western DFC and JNPT linkage still unproven for volume shifts.

Analyst-cited figures, not disputed by management

segments.commentary: Growth of 1-2% in Q2; no new customer added this fiscal, with a few deals near closure. Scope expanded for one major customer to pan-India; management is avoiding low or negative margin business.

segments.commentary: Rail volumes recovered about 11% QoQ; management targets at least 100,000 rail TEUs per quarter. Ankleshwar MMLP EXIM permissions are in place and volumes are minimal so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is Snowman's PAT likely to grow meaningfully and when does profitability improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reinvestment keeps interest and depreciation high, so PAT may grow modestly; focus is on operating cash flow and EBITDA, with Snowman on track to cross INR100 crore EBITDA this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why are warehousing margins falling over the long term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 5PL mix, park-and-pay spot business at under 10% margin, build-to-suit at lower margin, and minimum wage, PF and gratuity changes not yet passed through. Utilisation at 85% versus a targeted 88-89% also cut margins by about 2-3%.

qa_highlights.question: How much could DFC and JNPT linkage lift Gateway volumes and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to size; road-to-rail shift of about 10,000-15,000 TEU per month is possible, but shipping line routing decisions at JNPT are the main driver.

qa_highlights.question: Is Indian Railways likely to cut tariffs post-JNPT DFC linkage?
qa_highlights.answer: Representations have been made for tariff rationalisation to compete with Mundra and Pipavav, but management said it is too early to comment and expects incremental JNPT rail volume in a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: What are Snowman's capex plans and how is expansion funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is through both build-to-suit and owned capacity, with about 23,000 pallets under construction and 20-odd thousand under discussion; no capex quantum was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jaipur ICD status?
qa_highlights.answer: All final arguments are complete and the order is reserved; if favourable, construction starts and operations take up to 18 months.

Jaipur ICD outcome depends on a reserved court order with no timeline.

538666|2026-03.headline: Sharda Cropchem FY26 PAT rose 124% to INR 681 crores on record revenue of INR 5,268 crores; FY27 revenue guided at 10-15%.
538666|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 13% YoY to INR 2,065 crores, with EBITDA up 75% to INR 513 crores and PAT up 57% to INR 319 crores. Gross margin expanded 750 bps to 37.3%, aided by a sharp rise in FX contribution (+11.7% in Q4). For FY26, revenue rose 22% to INR 5,268 crores, EBITDA rose 69% to INR 1,040 crores (19.7% margin), and PAT rose 124% to INR 681 crores. The company remains debt-free with INR 702 crores of cash and liquid investments. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-15%, gross margin around 35% plus or minus a few points, and EBITDA margin of 18-20%.

538666|2026-06.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs.1,074 crore and EBITDA 25% to Rs.178 crore, but reported PAT of Rs.88 crore was cushioned by lower forex gains.
538666|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs.1,074 crore, with volume down 1.6% and forex contributing 12.7 points. EBITDA margin expanded 220 bps to 16.6% and gross margin rose 120 bps to 36.7%, driven by mix in NAFTA, LATAM and rest of world. Europe revenue softened as distributors cut stock after an unusual heatwave, though Europe gross margin improved to 44.2%. Forex gain fell to Rs.7.5 crore from Rs.73.1 crore, so reported PBT and PAT looked weaker, while management said PBT before forex grew 16% to Rs.111 crore. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 10-15% revenue growth and about 35% gross margin.

segments.commentary: Largest market; revenue softened as distributors cut stock after heatwave. Gross margin 44.2% vs 42.9% in Q1 FY26. Management said restocking has largely normalised.

segments.name: NAFTA
segments.commentary: Gross margin 32.8% vs 25.9% a year ago; growth strong and margins improved this quarter.

segments.name: LATAM
segments.commentary: Among the strongest growth engines this quarter, but gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0% a year ago.

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.commentary: Gross margin 30.8% vs 26.8% in Q1 FY26; growth reported as good with better profitability.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 10-15% maintained; volume growth expected at about 5-10%.
FY27 gross margin guided at 35% to 37% (management, in Q&A), and EBITDA margin in the 18-20% range.
Effective tax rate on annualised basis expected at 18-20%, with Q1 running higher.
Amortisation expected to be about Rs.370-375 crore annualised for FY27 vs about Rs.325 crore last year.
Management expects Europe volumes to recover to prior-year levels and the next three quarters to be better than Q1; last month of Q2 said to be better than Q1.
Registration investment of about Rs.450-500 crore per year; FY27 spend to rise further.

Q1 capex was elevated by heavy data compensation payments, which management says will not repeat.
Total product registrations at 30 June 2026 were 3,016 (3,011 at 31 March 2026), with 1,027 applications pending.
Registrations by region: Europe 1,682 (up 3), NAFTA 325 (up 2), LATAM 760 (flat), rest of world 249 (flat).
demand_pricing: Volume declined 1.6% YoY; forex added 12.7 points and product mix subtracted 2.1 points.
Management said prices are improving sequentially after a severe decline about two years ago.
Europe revenue fell on distributor destocking linked to heatwave; management attributes this to weather, not molecules.
LATAM and NAFTA growth may partly reflect customer pre-buying ahead of season, per analyst; management said there is no strong trend.
Sourcing is 100% contract manufacturing, mainly from China, and all purchases are in US dollars.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the 9% revenue growth into volume, forex and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume -1.6%, forex +12.7%, product mix -2.1%, total +9%. Management said the mix impact is concentrated in Europe and should improve next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.7.5 crore forex gain and its accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly unrealised, from repricing foreign-currency receivables and payables at each balance sheet date. Q1 FY26 had a Rs.73 crore unrealised gain from a roughly 10% EUR/USD move. EBITDA excludes forex.

qa_highlights.question: Has Europe restocking normalised and what is FY27 EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restocking has improved and is largely normal, and guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex Rs.273 crore in Q1 vs Rs.500 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance not revised; Q1 included heavy data compensation spend that is not expected to recur. Full year could be Rs.480-550 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report PAT excluding forex for like-to-like comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO pointed to the investor presentation, which gives PBT and EBIT excluding forex. He said more clarity will be provided in future presentations.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the NAFTA and LATAM gross margin, and do margins hold for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe mix and price increases drove margins, LATAM volumes grew but margins dipped, and it expects Europe and NAFTA margins to stay in the same range.

Capex range wide (Rs.480-550 crore) with no firm guidance revision.

538666|2026-09.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR1,052 crore and PAT 23% to INR92 crore, despite a 5.1% volume decline.
538666|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 13% YoY to INR1,052 crore, driven by price, forex and mix (18.3% contribution) offsetting a 5.1% volume decline. EBITDA rose 18% to INR164 crore at a 15.6% margin, and gross margin expanded 140 bps to 35.9%. NAFTA (about 30% growth) and LATAM (agrochemical revenue up over 80%) offset a softer Europe, which management attributed to weather-led distributor caution. Management maintained FY27 revenue growth guidance of 10–15% and EBITDA margin of 18–20%. The company remains debt-free with INR846 crore of cash and liquid investments.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY; agrochemical +6% to INR1,755 crore, non-agro +40% to INR371 crore

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Largest market; saw slight moderation after an exceptionally strong FY26 as distributors restocked cautiously amid heat and drought. Q2 Europe gross margin about 41%. Management expects recovery in H2, the seasonally stronger period.

segments.name: NAFTA
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 30% YoY with significantly better margins; Q2 gross margin about 40%. Management says the margin gains are sustainable, citing good demand and lower availability.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Q2 gross margin about 31%.

segments.name: Non-agrochemical
segments.commentary: Revenue INR212 crore in Q2 (+68% YoY) and INR371 crore in H1 (+40%), driven mainly by conveyor and rubber belts. Margins fell in Q2 on higher transportation costs for conveyor belts.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 10–15%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 18–20%, supported by better product mix and H2 operating leverage.
Gross margin in H2 expected to hold or improve from Q2 level of 35.9%, per management.
Management said H2 EBITDA margin could be above 20% if the low end of 18% for the year is assumed.
FY27 planned capex of INR550–600 crore for product registrations; INR419 crore already spent in H1 per analyst's reading of the call.
Amortisation to stay elevated in H2 as capitalised registration intangibles are amortised over 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q2 revenue growth between forex, realisation and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated 18.3% from price, forex and mix with a 5.1% volume decline. It did not provide the split between realisation and forex and offered to follow up offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did registrations rise about 50 while the pipeline fell about 120 over 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there were no withdrawals; some registrations were discontinued and new ones came in. He linked the increase in H1 capex to US data compensation. Regional registration and pipeline numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Will Europe margins return to the earlier high profitability levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said European profitability is likely to improve.

qa_highlights.question: Is an H2 EBITDA margin above 20% achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it can be.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving non-agro growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly conveyor and rubber belts, driven by customers restocking after supply uncertainty and transport disruptions. Management did not say how long the trend will last.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation and amortisation up, and does it lead revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said higher amortisation (5-year life) will continue in H2 and is tied to new registrations that should lift future revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin fall in H2 given oil and commodity pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 gross margins are expected to hold or go up.

Registration timing is unpredictable (regulatory delays, new test requirements, US data compensation arbitration), so capex phasing could shift.
Analysts questioned the registration count versus the pipeline, which the management did not fully answer.
Volume decline continued in H1 (-3.5%); management expects normalisation in H2 but gave no volume guidance.
NAFTA margin sustainability depends on tight availability and demand, which may not last.
Freight costs from Hormuz and Red Sea routes are rising; EUR/USD near 1.12 is a forex sensitivity.
Non-agro margins fell in Q2 on conveyor-belt transport costs.

Management also called registration timing and regulatory outcomes "totally unpredictable."
key_quotes: We continue to maintain our FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10% to 15%.

So, it is very easy for us to pass on all the tariff increases to the customers.

FY27 planned capex of INR550–600 crore for product registrations, stated by management as aimed at increasing registrations.

Management did not split realisation from forex and offered to follow up offline.

Europe, the largest market, moderated after a strong FY26 as distributors restocked cautiously amid heat and drought in Central and Eastern Europe. Management called it temporary and weather-led and expects H2 recovery, with European profitability likely to improve.

Non-agro growth (+68% in Q2, +40% in H1) was mainly conveyor and rubber belts, driven by customers restocking after supply uncertainty and transport problems. Management did not say how long this lasts; Q2 non-agro margins fell on higher conveyor-belt transport costs.

Pricing: management said agrochemical prices are improving, though the pace is below expectations and prices remain well below pre-COVID levels. Management said tariffs do not affect agrochemicals and that increases can be passed on to customers. Freight costs are rising due to Hormuz and Red Sea routes, but management said this does not affect performance.

Management said volumes were improving in October in Europe and LATAM, and expects H1 weakness to normalise in H2. It gave no volume guidance. Management said China availability and prices for products remain good. Management said Q2 gross margins by region were Europe about 41%, NAFTA about 40%, LATAM about 14%, Rest of World about 31%, and group 35.9%.

rows.why: Management says agrochemical prices are improving, though slower than expected and still well below pre-COVID levels, and increases can be passed on to customers; price/forex/mix contributed 18.3% to Q2 revenue growth.

rows.why: NAFTA revenue grew about 30% YoY at about 40% gross margin and LATAM agrochemical revenue rose over 80% YoY, with management calling the NAFTA margin gains sustainable.

rows.why: Management expects the seasonally stronger H2 to recover after distributors restocked cautiously in Q2 amid heat and drought, with European profitability likely to improve, though the size has not been quantified.

538668|2026-03.headline: Meghna Infracon FY26 revenue rose 15.84% to INR46.2 crore, but PAT fell 4.28% as carry-over securities profits lapsed.

FY26 revenue from operations was INR46.2 crore versus INR39.88 crore, and Q4 revenue was INR18.48 crore, up 52.47% YoY. FY26 PAT was INR5.59 crore, down about 4.28% YoY, which management attributed to the absence of carry-over profits from the earlier securities business. Management guided to a sharp increase in GDV and profitability over the coming years, with current GDV pipeline stated above INR2,100 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Company aims to stay nearly debt-free; cash went into acquisitions of future projects that management expects to lift GDV and profit.

Andheri supply pressure from multiple launches.
Steel and cement price volatility on contracts that are mostly fixed price.
Rivaan completion target of December 2026 versus RERA deadline of March 2027.

538685|2026-06.headline: Shemaroo Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6% to about INR 132 crore, but EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR 2 crore from INR 56 crore.
538685|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was about INR 132 crore, down 6% YoY, with digital down about 17% to INR 56 crore and traditional up 5% to INR 76 crore. EBITDA loss narrowed sharply to about INR 2 crore versus INR 56 crore a year earlier, after about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend; excluding that, existing operations EBITDA was about INR 18 crore. Net loss reduced to about INR 8 crore. Management said this is the first quarter after the inventory charge-off exercise, now in a normal charge-off cycle, and guided to double-digit blended growth, EBITDA-positive for the year, and bottom-line positive next year.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of approx. INR 56 crore (call analyst cited 55.5 crore) in Q1 FY26
materially reduced YoY; no prior figure stated

segments.name: Digital media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 56 crore, down 17% YoY, as select B2B syndication deals were deferred on geopolitical uncertainty; consumer business grew on fresh content and ad monetisation. Management targets double-digit digital growth.

segments.name: Traditional media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 76 crore, up 5% YoY, helped by closure of B2B licensing deals that offset subdued ad environment. Management expects roughly flat traditional revenue for FY27, with near-term ad outlook subdued due to BARC ratings blackout.

segments.name: ShemarooMe (OTT, Gujarati)
segments.commentary: Acquired OHO Gujarati catalogue in April 2026 (over 22 Gujarati originals); released 10 new titles in the quarter. Company does not disclose subscriber, ARPU or revenue figures; management said it is about two years from OTT profitability.

segments.name: YouTube
segments.commentary: Approx. 9 billion views across channels in the quarter; Shemaroo Filmi Gaane passed 74.7 million subscribers and Shemaroo Entertainment 61.9 million. Management said views are seasonal but viewership share remains strong.

guidance_outlook: Blended revenue growth aim of healthy double digits over the next 2-3 years; digital targeted at double-digit growth, outpacing recent low-double-digit industry digital growth by a couple of percentage points.
Traditional media revenue expected flattish for FY27, not declining.
Aim for EBITDA-positive for full FY27 (conservative view); management expects bottom-line positive next year (FY28).
Debt reduction plan for FY27, but no quantified target given; quarterly fluctuations possible given geopolitical and BARC blackout impacts.

New-initiative spend to be cut by more than 50% in FY27 versus FY26; management said the company is on track.
capex_capacity: Content strategy shifted: new content creation scaled down in traditional, while new content acquisition is being scaled up in digital.
Traditional channel rationalisation possible; company now runs two FAST channels after earlier shrinking the number.
OTT (ShemarooMe) needs ongoing content and customer-acquisition spend (ATL, BTL and performance marketing); management said little upfront capex is needed.
Inventory of INR 348 crore at Q1 end; management said no remaining write-down risk and the company is now in a normal charge-off cycle.
demand_pricing: Digital decline attributed to deferred B2B syndication deals (geopolitical uncertainty) and lumpy B2B revenue; consumer digital grew on fresh content and better ad monetisation.
Traditional ad market subdued for a long period; BARC ratings blackout in recent month has hit traditional and syndication revenue.
Acquired content is priced competitively against other bidders, so new-content margins are lower than on legacy content already amortised or charged off.
YouTube Shorts monetisation has not moved meaningfully; company is focusing on connected-TV long-form content, and is only experimenting with micro-dramas.
FAST channel ecosystem globally has been shrinking for roughly 12-18 months; company is tracking it and scaling only if monetisation improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA excluding the new-initiative investment, and what revenue is needed for positive EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend, EBITDA would have been about INR 18 crore. Management said margin depends on both revenue growth and cost cuts, and on revenue mix, so it would not give a revenue threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Is the content library under-monetised, and what growth is expected over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no under-utilisation, citing 9 billion views in the quarter. Traditional monetisation is declining while digital is growing. The aim is healthy double-digit blended growth, outdoing digital industry growth by a couple of points.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and FY27 profitability and revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: A debt reduction plan exists for FY27 but no figure was given. EBITDA-positive for the year is the conservative aim, with bottom-line positive next year. Digital is seen at double-digit growth and traditional roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow digital faster, around 20%, given 9-10% CAGR over FY24-FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry underlying growth was low, and it would not burn cash to grow faster, since that would strain cash flow and the balance sheet. It cited its leadership in Gujarati entertainment.

qa_highlights.question: Which digital segments carry the highest margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin depends on content age, not platform. Legacy content can yield 80-90% margins, newly acquired content can be near zero or negative, and production work can earn 10-20%. YouTube is not inherently high-margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin, and is 20% EBITDA the aim on a reported basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was not satisfied with current margins and aspires to upwards of 20% EBITDA in 2-3 years. It declined to say whether this is on a reported basis net of all investments, and said the structural shift in the media industry is a factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and inventory at quarter end, and is further write-down likely?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was INR 311 crore and inventory INR 348 crore at quarter end. Management said the company is in a normal charge-off cycle with no further rationalisation planned.

qa_highlights.question: How long until ShemarooMe reaches break-even, and will it disclose subscriber or revenue data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is about two years from OTT break-even. It does not disclose DAU, MAU, subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue, and said it has no current plan to start.

risks_watch: Digital revenue fell 17% YoY on deferred B2B syndication deals; lumpy B2B timing could keep quarterly digital revenue volatile.
Traditional ad market remains weak and BARC ratings blackout is hurting traditional and syndication revenue.
Debt of INR 311 crore against an EBITDA-positive-for-year aim; quarterly debt movements may vary.
Limited disclosure: no OTT subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue data, and no quantified debt target; analysts asked for more granularity.
YouTube Shorts and micro-drama monetisation still unproven; a possible YouTube monetisation policy update was not confirmed.
538685|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the operating trajectory and cost discipline, but evasive on specifics: it declined to give debt targets, OTT data, profitability timing, or a revenue threshold for breakeven. It acknowledged margins are below its own aspiration.
key_quotes: Every quarter, I think we should be seeing an improvement on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
Are we satisfied with it? Definitely not.
I think if I see a 2 -3 year perspective, I think definitely upwards of 20% EBITDA is something that we should aim for.

rows.why: New-initiative spend was about INR 20 crore in Q1 and management says it is on track to cut it by more than 50% versus FY26, which is the main driver of the EBITDA turn.

538685|2026-09.headline: Shemaroo Q2 FY27 revenue fell 2% YoY to ~INR 141 crore, but EBITDA loss narrowed to ~INR 2 crore from INR 55 crore.
538685|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR 141 crore, down a marginal 2% YoY, while EBITDA loss narrowed sharply to about INR 2 crore from INR 55 crore a year earlier. Net loss reduced to about INR 8 crore from INR 45 crore, helped by completion of accelerated amortisation two quarters earlier and cost optimisation. Digital media grew 26% YoY to about INR 76 crore and was 54% of revenue, while traditional media fell 21% to about INR 66 crore, hit by the prolonged BARC rating blackout and deferred broadcaster content spends. Management reiterated that EBITDA break-even by year-end is an aspiration, not formal guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR -55 crore loss in Q2 FY26; management cites 96% improvement
vs ~INR -110 crore loss in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Digital media revenue (FY27 to date, as stated)
Traditional media revenue (FY27 to date, as stated)

segments.name: Digital media
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~INR 76 crore, up 26% YoY, driven by B2B licensing deals and YouTube ad revenue; about 54% of Q2 revenue and ~48% in H1. Management says licensing revenue is lumpy and should be judged over 12 months.

segments.name: Traditional media
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~INR 66 crore, down 21% YoY, due to BARC rating blackout reducing advertiser spend and broadcasters deferring content investments, which delayed TV licensing deals.

segments.name: Shemaroo Bhujrati (OTT)
segments.commentary: Released 9 new titles in the quarter across movies, web series and plays, including Lalo, Krishna Sada Sahayate, Zindagi Once More, Chaskaila S1, Shada Chani Bus, Stution and Ok Boss. Focus is on Gujarati and regional content.

segments.name: YouTube
segments.commentary: Flagship channel Shemaroo Filmi Gane passed 75 million subscribers; Shemaroo Entertainment channel crossed 62.3 million. Portfolio drew ~9.6 billion views in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management said it does not give formal guidance; the EBITDA break-even target by end of FY27 and cash-positive by FY28 are stated as aspirations.
Management expects EBITDA break-even at least by end of this year (FY27), moving further in FY28; the company says it remains very much working towards this.
Festive season is expected to support ad demand; management says demand is up YoY on both digital and traditional versus a weak festive season last year.
Net debt is directionally targeted to fall; management says net debt was held flat in Q2 and cash flow remains strong.
BARC rating blackout is a near-term challenge for traditional media revenues.
capex_capacity: Investment in new initiatives (television broadcasting and Shemaroo Bhujrati OTT) was ~INR 19.9 crore per an analyst question; management did not confirm the figure. Existing-operations EBITDA for H1 FY27 was stated as ~INR 35 crore before new-initiative spend.
Content spend is concentrated on digital, with rights bought as bundles for OTT, YouTube and licensing; TV channel budgets have been cut and programming rationalised.
Finance cost rose ~INR 0.45 crore on overall debt of ~INR 9 crore per management, due to temporary use of OD and CC limits to buy content. Company says it is not in debt.
demand_pricing: Traditional TV advertising is constrained because the absence of BARC ratings means advertisers cannot measure campaigns, so they price conservatively or shift spend to digital or print.
Festive-season demand is up YoY in both digital and traditional, versus a weaker festive season last year that was hit by GST cuts and logistics issues.
Licensing and syndication flow slowed in the geopolitical environment; digital revenue share dipped to about 40% in Q1 before rising to 54% in Q2, per management.
Management says YouTube continues to gain ad share versus other social platforms, citing Connected TV as a growth avenue.
Shemaroo is the worldwide digital and satellite distribution partner for the Telugu film Rambha Urvasi Menka.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth slowing in digital, given expectations of double-digit digital growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed geopolitical uncertainty hurting ad spend and slower licensing and syndication deal flow. Digital grew 3% in H1 but 26% in Q2 as delayed deals closed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company stick to its guidance of EBITDA-positive FY27 and cash-positive FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it gives no guidance and these are aspirations; it is still working towards EBITDA break-even at least by end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the BARC rating blackout affecting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: No measurement means advertisers hesitate and price conservatively or move spend to digital or print. Broadcasters have cut content budgets, and the company has tempered its own channel budgets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback timeline on content?
qa_highlights.answer: TV licensing is upfront and fixed-fee on about five-year rights, so payback is short. Digital licensing covers 1-3 year rights, and YouTube and OTT are monthly variable revenue share.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Temporary use of OD and CC limits to fund content purchases raised finance cost by ~INR 0.45 crore on ~INR 9 crore of debt (as stated by management).

risks_watch: Traditional media revenue keeps declining (-21% YoY in Q2) while the BARC blackout continues with no measurement timeline.
Digital licensing revenue is lumpy, so quarterly results are hard to read; the 12-month view will be key.
Whether EBITDA break-even by end-FY27 is achieved; it is an aspiration, not formal guidance.
Digital growth slowed to 3% for H1, and the festive-season recovery needs to hold.

538715|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, EBITDA up 45.6% to INR54.59 crores at a 20.6% margin, with the order book at a record INR174 crores.
538715|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, below management's earlier 20-25% target, because supplies on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR were deferred by buyers. Profitability improved sharply: EBITDA margin expanded 460 bps to 20.6%, PAT rose 67.2% to INR30.14 crores, and Q4 EBITDA margin crossed 21%. The company deployed about INR27 crores of capex in FY26 under a Board-approved INR100 crores programme spanning FY26-FY28, and entered aluminium windows and facade with INR56 crores of orders. Working capital rose as management paid suppliers early and stocked PVC resin and polymers ahead of West Asia-related price increases.

financial_highlights.change: Management says it will not reach 0.75
Record high; vs INR120-140 crores last year

segments.name: PVC/UPVC polymer products
segments.commentary: Management said about 84% of FY26 revenue (about INR220 crores) came from PVC and UPVC, of which about INR60 crores was UPVC windows and the rest PVC profiles. EBITDA margin in this segment was higher than modular; PBT margin was about 16.6%.

segments.name: Modular furniture (Dynasty)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR43 crores (about 16% of sales), with PBT margin around 9%, which management said was up about 80% YoY. Four new builder brands were added, including Godrej, M3M and Smart Homes, and exports to Europe are growing.

segments.name: Plastic profile core segment
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 13% and segment profitability rose 63%, per management. PVC profile capacity rose by 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT per annum, with utilisation around 66% in FY26.

segments.name: Aluminium windows and facade (Bangalore/Jaipur)
segments.commentary: New vertical under Mr. Varghese with INR56 crores of orders and revenue starting in Q4 FY26. Management guides INR40-50 crores of FY27 revenue; it targets EBITDA margins of about 20%.

segments.name: WPC doors and WPC wall/ceiling panels
segments.commentary: WPC door line (about INR10 crores capex) has finished trials and is due for commercial launch in Q2 FY27. Management expects about INR15 crores of FY27 revenue; WPC wall and ceiling profile lines are planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of about 30% revenue CAGR while sustaining EBITDA and PAT margins; management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is sustainable.
FY27 PVC profile extrusion volume growth of at least 20%; modular furniture growth of 20-25% expected.
FY27 new-capex revenue addition of INR55-60 crores, with aluminium facade INR40-50 crores and WPC doors about INR15 crores.
INR100 crores capex over FY26-FY28: about INR27 crores in FY26, INR35-40 crores in FY27 and INR20-30 crores in FY28.
Existing extrusion capacity can deliver more than INR450 crores of profile revenue at 85% utilisation; management did not give a year for reaching it.
Working capital expected to improve materially in FY27 as inventory is consumed and supplier payment cycles normalise.
capex_capacity: PVC profile extrusion capacity raised by 3,600 MT from 24,000 MT to 27,600 MT per annum in FY26; utilisation about 66%, with 80% cited as the practical benchmark.
WPC door line: machines commissioned and trials underway; commercial launch expected from Q2 FY27. WPC door capacity not yet finalised.
WPC wall and ceiling profile extrusion planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.
Aluminium windows and facade: Bangalore unit implemented; a new Jaipur factory site is under construction with capex planned in FY27. Custom fabrication, so no defined capacity.
Management expects ROE and ROCE of about 25-26% to be sustained on the new capex; it also said the new capex would earn similar returns across segments.
demand_pricing: Order book INR174 crores: UPVC windows and doors about INR84 crores, modular furniture about INR34 crores, aluminium windows and facade about INR56 crores; 100% expected to execute in 18-24 months.
Price hikes: three price revisions since the West Asia conflict began, up to 30 April. Management estimated 15-18% raw material cost inflation across its product lines.
Roughly 30% of revenue is fixed-price; B2B PVC profile distribution (over 60% of revenue) carries price revision clauses. Aluminium projects carry NALCO-linked base-price pass-through clauses.
Management said PVC resin fell from about INR115 in March to INR80-85 now; prices can move both ways.
Mobilisation advances of 10-20% of project value; net advances exceed INR7 crores versus about INR5 crores last year.
Management says WPC doors have no direct competition in India today; aluminium facade faces large international system brands and local fabricators.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the shortfall versus the 20-25% growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buyers deferred supply on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and one or two in Delhi NCR. Order book was healthy and the shortfall was described as timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is a 20%+ EBITDA margin sustainable amid raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing product mix, upgraded offerings for upper-middle and high-end customers, and pre-buying of raw materials in February-March. It expects price revisions to offset the 15-18% input cost rise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did payables fall to almost zero and inventory and receivables rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it paid suppliers in full in the last two months of FY26 to secure supply during the Middle East disruption and bought PVC resin and polymers heavily in March. Receivables rose only in line with revenue, and it expects the cycle to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 volume growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to at least 20% volume growth in PVC profile extrusion, with new verticals adding on top. Price growth was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crores capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly internal accruals (about INR50 crores of operating cash generation in FY26), with some borrowing. Debt-to-equity is currently 0.56 and is not expected to reach 0.75.

risks_watch: Revenue timing risk: deferred project deliveries by buyers caused the FY26 shortfall against the 20-25% target.
Raw material and aluminium price volatility tied to crude oil and LME aluminium; the aluminium contracts carry base-price clauses, but UPVC and modular contracts are largely fixed-price.
Working capital: inventory build, receivables growth and near-zero payables; management guided to normalisation in FY27.
Execution of the new WPC door launch in Q2 FY27 and the aluminium facade ramp-up, including the Jaipur factory build.

538836|2026-09.headline: Monte Carlo Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.51% to Rs 262 crore, but PAT fell to Rs 1.17 crore as raw-material costs rose; H1 posted a Rs 22.25 crore loss.

Management attributed the weakness to higher material cost, lower other income, higher employee cost and early discounting to clear old inventory, and said the timing of festive demand and retailer returns distorts the half-year. Guidance was held at low double-digit revenue growth, 40-45 new EBOs and about 20% home textile growth, with EBITDA margin now guided at plus or minus 100 bps of last year.

538920|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 57.2% YoY to INR165.3 crore with EBITDA margin of 18.5%; capacity now 11,000 MT after brownfield expansion.
538920|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR165.3 crore, up 57.2% YoY and 9.8% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR30.6 crore (18.5% margin) and PAT of INR21 crore (12.7% margin). Installed capacity rose from 6,500 MT to 11,000 MT through an internally funded brownfield expansion, now fully operational from Q1 FY27. Management guided to about 95% utilisation (10,200–10,400 MT) in FY27 and a 5,500 MT freeze-dried coffee (FDC) plant by Q2 FY28, with a larger capex and debt plan outlined.

segments.commentary: 5,500 MT plant with capex of about INR550 crore, of which about INR150 crore is spent; commercial operations expected from July 2027 after a three-month trial, with about 70% utilisation and about 9 months of output in FY28. FY28 margin expected to improve further (about 20–21% with 8–9 months of FDC output); FY29 margin 22–24%.
FY27 operating cash flow expected positive overall, with Q1 seasonally negative and Q3–Q4 positive.

FY27 debt expected to rise by about INR30–40 crore over FY26 at about 8.3–8.4%. Peak debt for the FDC project of about INR400 crore (INR300 crore ECB at about 5–6% including hedging, plus INR100 crore working capital at about 8.3–8.4%).

Global instant coffee production (including freeze-dried) is about 1,000,000 MT, growing about 30,000 MT per year, per management.
Management said it has no plans to enter retail; focus is on e-commerce and local presence.
EBITDA per kg for Q4 was similar to Q3; Q4 volume was 1,924 MT versus 1,802 MT in Q3 (one answer cited 1,824 MT for Q4 before correcting to 1,924 MT).

qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR550 crore, about INR150 crore spent; remaining about INR400 crore over roughly the next year. Commissioning by March 2027, commercial operations from July 2027 (not a six-month delay, per management).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue potential and the chicory contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 revenue ballpark is INR850-900 crore on 10,500 MT. Chicory revenue is INR40-45 crore a year, and EBITDA from chicory in Q1 was about INR2.1 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt and capex plans for FDC?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt capped at INR450 crore; phase 2 to be funded from FY28 incremental cash flow; no equity dilution planned at present.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital days high at 120-130 and when does cash flow improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth inventory is the main reason; CFO said FY27 operating cash flow will be positive, with working capital days around 125 and the FY27 cash-generation capacity estimated at about INR79 crore if growth inventory was not needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any hedging or inventory loss risk given production above sales in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said beans are bought back-to-back, with 40-45 days of stock held; surplus Q1 production is expected to be picked up by customers in Q2.

risks_watch: FDC ramp-up: 5,500 MT line depends on June 2027 trials, with production from Q2 FY28 and FY28 volume of about 2,400 MT at 60-65% utilisation over 8-9 months; LOIs cover 70-80% of capacity but are subject to quality and price.

Pricing and inventory: prices are reset quarterly on cost-plus; Q1 production of 2,402 MT exceeded sales of 1,856 MT, so Q2 offtake of surplus stock and the back-to-back bean hedge (40-45 days stock) need to hold.
Margin trajectory: management guided a 0.5-1% EBITDA margin uplift from Q1 levels and a 23-24% consolidated margin in the business plan; bulk mix and FDC mix could dilute EBITDA per kg.

Working capital and cash: 120-130 day cycle, FY27 operating cash flow guided positive, peak debt capped at INR450 crore; Phase 2 FDC funding relies on FY28 incremental cash flow with no equity dilution currently planned.

Chicory and EBITDA per kg reconciliation: management's Q1 EBITDA per kg of INR157 differs from the INR172 analyst calculation on the INR32 crore EBITDA base; disclosure of volume and per-kg figures in press releases was requested by an analyst.

Ours is a cost-plus margin. So, obviously, we have fixed profits on a per-kg basis.

538920|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 64.4% YoY to INR222.97 crore and EBITDA rose 88.8% to INR42.16 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18.9%.
538920|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR222.97 crore in Q2 FY27, up 64.4% YoY and 38.5% QoQ, with growth attributed mainly to volume rather than realisation. EBITDA of INR42.16 crore (18.9% margin, up 244 bps YoY) and PAT of INR28.06 crore (12.6% margin) both grew strongly. H1 FY27 revenue was INR383.97 crore (+61.9%), with operating cash flow of INR51.16 crore. Management reiterated the 5,500 MT freeze-dried coffee (FDC) project, now expected to start trial production in August 2027 and commercial production from September 2027, and discussed a possible small equity raise that is still subject to alternative funding.

financial_highlights.change: +52.3% YoY vs INR32.07 crore (ETR 9.3% in H1 FY26)

segments.commentary: Installed capacity is 11,000 MT per annum after 4,500 MT was commissioned at end-March 2026; utilisation is about 95%. Product mix is about 55% agglomerated and 45% spray-dried, and management plans to shift further toward agglomerated.

segments.name: Chicory
segments.commentary: Capacity is fully utilised. Volume rose about 5% because of a crop shortage, and sales prices rose about 4-5%.

segments.commentary: Exports are about 85% of revenue and domestic about 15% in Q2 FY27.

capex_capacity: Installed capacity is 11,000 MT of spray-dried and agglomerated coffee. Total capacity rises to 16,500 MT when the 5,500 MT FDC Phase 1 comes on stream, and to 22,000 MT after Phase 2 (FY30).
FDC Phase 1 total capex is about INR550 crore, of which about INR220 crore is spent. About INR150 crore is planned for the rest of FY27 and the balance in H1 FY28.
Phase 2 (5,500 MT brownfield FDC) capex is about INR350 crore. The final decision and order are expected in Q1 FY28, with commercial operations from April 2029 and full capacity in FY30.
A separate agglomeration line and packing line (funded partly by promoter warrants, with a 25% contribution expected in 10-15 days) will add capacity within the 11,000 MT spray and agglo envelope.
Land of 22 acres was acquired at TGIIC Food Processing Park, Telangana, to cover the entire FDC facility.
Letters of intent covering 100% of Phase 1 capacity have been received from customers.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth was mainly volume-driven, not realisation-driven. Management described Q2 realisation as marginally higher than Q1 and expects Q3 to be stable with a slight improvement from pack mix.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 to be higher-sales quarters as they are the peak season for soluble coffee.
Volume growth of about 40% against value growth of about 60-65% was attributed to a higher coffee mix; the chicory share is included in volume.
Bean sourcing is 65-70% from India and 30-35% from Uganda and Indonesia. Management expects bean prices to stay flat to slightly lower.
Four to five new customers were added for spray and agglomerated coffee in H1 FY27.
Roasted and ground coffee: initial export orders for a couple of containers have been shipped; management expects a sizeable order if the first orders execute.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 growth came from volume versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the growth came from volume, not higher realisation per kg.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11,000 MT plant at 95% utilisation, and how much FDC capex is done?
qa_highlights.answer: Spray and agglo utilisation is about 95%; FDC capex incurred is INR220 crore of INR550 crore, with the rest in the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there an equity dilution if expansion was to be funded by debt and internal accruals?
qa_highlights.answer: European FCY loans are sanctioned, but a negative pledge clause makes Indian bank borrowing difficult, so a small dilution is being considered and alternative funding is being explored. The board has approved a fundraise of about INR325 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the B2C strategy change the B2B focus?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C via e-platforms continues for now; large-scale B2C is planned from FY30 after the second FDC line, with domestic and international options.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a delay in the FDC project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the start moved from June-July 2027 to August-September 2027 because of ESG formalities linked to the European bank loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin uplift from FDC and the second phase?
qa_highlights.answer: FDC adds 2-3% to margins once Phase 1 runs, and Phase 2 adds 1-1.5%, giving 3-4% in total at 22,000 MT utilisation.

risks_watch: Funding: the equity dilution (board-approved, about INR325 crore) is not final and depends on alternative debt; the negative pledge clause limits Indian bank loans.
Execution: the FDC Phase 1 start moved by one to two months to August-September 2027; the Phase 2 decision is due Q1 FY28.
Logistics and geopolitics: export-heavy (85%) sales depend on international shipping, and rising ocean freight raised selling expenses. Other expenses rose from INR7 crore to INR14 crore QoQ.
Key-person and disclosure issues: the transcript lists the FDC completion and capex figures inconsistently (INR500 crore vs INR550 crore), and the FY28 volume and margin figures need confirmation.
Utilisation: spray and agglo is at about 95% against the 11,000 MT cap, so further growth depends on the new agglo line and capacity additions.
Comparability: H1 FY26 figures are not restated for the amalgamation of subsidiaries, which took effect from 1 October 2025.

538962|2026-03.headline: Minda Corp Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 1,704 crore (+29% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 203 crore at 11.9% margin and PAT of INR 124 crore.
538962|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly and full-year revenue, EBITDA and PAT for Minda Corporation, with Q4 revenue up 29% YoY and FY26 revenue up 22.3% to INR 6,185 crore. Full-year PAT rose 40.3% to INR 358 crore, helped by higher associate income from Flash Electronics and lower interest costs. Management highlighted new JVs (Turntide, Toyodenso), the planned consolidation of Minda VAST from FY27, and a FY27 capex plan of INR 400-450 crore. Commodity inflation (copper, zinc, aluminium up 30-40% through the year) is largely passed through to customers, though management flagged some EBITDA-margin drag from the lag.

qa_highlights.answer: Commodities are largely pass-through, so profit should be protected, though EBITDA margin will see some impact. 538962|2026-09.headline: Minda Corp Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 2,189 crore, up 43% YoY, with PAT of INR 143 crore up 69%.

segments.commentary: Europe and North America about 6% of revenue, South Asia about 5%, India about 89%.

Management reiterated FY27 laminate revenue growth of 10-12% and total revenue growth target of 18%, but gave no visibility on freight or raw material normalisation.

539046|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 13.5% to INR896 crore and PAT grew 164% to INR40.69 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 6.84% on the Middle East cost shock.

Management said new contracts since April 2026 pass through the full incremental cost, and that H1 FY27 margins should recover meaningfully.
