rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Second colour coating line (+1,50,000 MT, colour capacity 86,000 to 2,36,000 MT, INR65 crore, Mas Rollpro order placed) is in advanced erection and commissioning with completion targeted July 2026; the 7 MW solar plant (INR30 crore) is also targeted July 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Alu-zinc line (capacity 1,32,000 to 1,80,000 MT, +36%) is at 60-65% utilisation and guided to 80-85% within FY27; management guides INR300-500 crore incremental FY27 revenue over FY26, and the INR350-400 crore order book is mostly export.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Cold rolling complex (3,60,000 MT, second alu-zinc plant, 2,36,000 MT pre-painted) is planned for FY28 with no date or financing yet; management aims for 1x-1.5x debt-equity and targets ROCE above 20%, though it is undated and unmodelled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides 10-12% sustainable EBITDA margin and INR300-500 crore incremental revenue, but ramp-ups have not yet proved out and the Middle East cost shock is ongoing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 6.84%, freight rose about 100% QoQ and LPG about 200%, and the alu-zinc and colour line ramps could slip past July 2026, delaying the INR300-500 crore uplift.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Alu-zinc coated product is ramping (60-65% utilisation, 80-85% targeted in FY27) and the colour coating line adds 1,50,000 MT of pre-painted capacity from July 2026, with new alu-zinc export markets (South/Central America, Caribbean) targeted at a slight premium.

rows.label: Alu-zinc premium of INR3,000-5,000/ton with full cost pass-through on new contra
rows.why: Alu-zinc premium over galvanized is about INR3,000-5,000 per ton and all contracts since April 2026 pass through the full incremental cost, though management declined to quantify EBITDA-per-ton upside.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA down to 1.01x and D/E at 1.13x
rows.why: Net debt to EBITDA fell from 1.93x to 1.01x and D/E from 1.81x to 1.13x in FY26, while interest coverage rose to 2.85x from 1.63x, leaving room for the INR65 crore and INR30 crore projects with no fund raise planned now.

rows.label: INR350-400 crore order book, mostly export
rows.why: Order book of INR350-400 crore is mostly from export customers, and export tonnage rose 110% to 66,172 MT in FY26, supporting near-term volume.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY26 record, forward capacity and the INR300-500 crore FY27 uplift, but cautious on Q4 margins and Q1 FY27 costs; analysts pressed on ROCE, IRR, funding of cold rolling, alu-zinc pricing power and FY27 revenue totals, which management declined to quantify.

539046|2026-06.headline: Manaksia Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 86% QoQ to INR29.08 crore (11.06% margin), with record EBITDA/ton of INR10,400 on Alu-Zinc ramp-up.
539046|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR263 crore, up 15% QoQ and about 3.6% YoY, with realisation up nearly 12% QoQ to INR88,597/ton on mix and new-order pricing. PAT rose 163% QoQ to INR14.10 crore (5.36% margin). Management said all new Q1 orders are priced to cover current raw material and freight costs plus a margin buffer. Volumes were slightly down YoY (about 27,900 t vs about 29,000 t), which management attributed to Alu-Zinc ramp-up teething issues rather than demand. The second colour coating line and 7 MW solar plant are targeted for Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR79,180/ton in Q4 FY26, nearly +12%

segments.name: Pre-Painted Steel
segments.commentary: Production 20,510 t at 95.4% utilisation on the existing line; 74% of Q1 sales volume. Pre-painted exports grew 25% YoY.

segments.name: Alu-Zinc
segments.commentary: Production 27,941 t, up 8% QoQ, on the new line running at 62% utilisation; 26% of Q1 sales. Galvanised steel sales were nil in Q1 as the shift to Alu-Zinc was completed in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 65% of total volume, 18,221 t. Export revenue grew 20% YoY. Four new markets added in Q1: Latvia, Brazil, Jamaica and Somalia.

guidance_outlook: Second colour coating line (Pre-painted capacity 86,000 to 236,000 tpa, +174%) and 7 MW captive solar plant (offsets 50-55% of Kutch grid power) both targeted for Q2 FY27.
Alu-Zinc Phase 1 utilisation expected to reach 75-80% in about 3 more months; second colour coating line expected 50-60% utilisation in H2 FY27.
FY27 tonnage of about 150,000 t and revenue of INR1,300-1,350 crore assumed on new capacity at 50-60% utilisation.
FY28 tonnage of 180,000-200,000 t and revenue of INR1,700-1,750 crore targeted; a separate analyst question quoted 1.80-2.10 lakh t and INR1,700-1,800 crore.
Management guided to EBITDA margin of about 1-2% further growth on top of 11%, but said it is too early to say whether that is reached in FY27. Management does not expect a dip in EBITDA in Q2.
Phase 2 (cold rolling backward integration plus second Alu-Zinc line) estimated at INR350 crore; peak Alu-Zinc revenue after Phase 2 INR2,500-2,700 crore on about 3 lakh t.
capex_capacity: Capex already concluded of about INR140 crore (Alu-Zinc technology upgrade, second colour coating line, solar plant), mostly in CWIP and to be capitalised within Q2 FY27; only INR15-20 crore of debt remains to be deployed.
Current debt about INR115 crore, including term debt for these projects; peak debt estimated at INR125-130 crore given ongoing repayments.

Phase 2 capex INR350 crore, funded by internal accruals, debt and equity; additional debt estimated at about INR100 crore, not yet frozen. Management expects debt-equity not to exceed 1.25x (currently just above 1x).
Phase 2 cold rolling unit is in FY28 and is expected to cut working capital cycle from about 75 days to single-digit days by reducing SKU inventory.
Salesforce CRM implementation underway. Planned GSPC natural gas pipeline agreement in Gujarat to diversify away from LPG.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR450 crore (plus or minus INR20-25 crore), execution time 4.5-5 months; management guided a continuous 3-5 month book, around INR350-450 crore for the rest of FY27.
Order flow is largely repetitive quarterly orders from long-term export and domestic OEM customers, backed by annual offtake MoUs; Deepesh's note said about 80% of the order book is export.
Pricing is reset every quarter with export customers, passing through raw material, freight and energy changes. Management said most raw material is booked against orders in hand.
Q1 volume shortfall attributed to Alu-Zinc ramp-up pace, not demand. Pre-painted line ran at 95.4% utilisation.
Incremental EBITDA from galvanised to Alu-Zinc estimated at INR1,000-3,000/ton, from both lower cost and a price premium.
LPG/propane prices spiked from about INR60/kg to INR200/kg during the Iran war and Hormuz disruption, and have eased to about INR80/kg, roughly 25% above pre-war levels.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the record EBITDA/ton and how much can it rise after solar and CCL2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Alu-Zinc ramp-up, export tonnage and higher realisation drove INR10,400/ton. Further margin upside is possible if the capacity additions and solar plant execute well.

qa_highlights.question: How is the capex funded and how much is spent?
qa_highlights.answer: Total planned Phase 2 capex is INR350 crore, funded by a mix of internal accruals, debt and equity. Around INR140 crore is concluded, largely in CWIP; additional debt about INR100 crore is an estimate, and leverage is capped at 1.25x debt-equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume fall YoY from about 29,000 t to about 27,900 t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed 100% of the shortfall to Alu-Zinc ramp-up pace (teething issues for 3-4 months), not demand. It expects utilisation to reach 75-80% in about 3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and how will it change?
qa_highlights.answer: The cycle is about 75 days after creditors. The cold rolling unit (Phase 2, FY28) is expected to halve inventory and compress the cycle to single-digit days.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 revenue and tonnage targets?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27: about 150,000 t and INR1,300-1,350 crore on new capacity at 50-60% utilisation in H2. FY28: 180,000-200,000 t and INR1,700-1,750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply risk from the LPG/Hormuz disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Buffer stock kept the plant running nonstop. Supply was diversified to private as well as PSU suppliers at extra cost, and LPG prices have eased to about INR80/kg from INR200/kg peak.

risks_watch: Alu-Zinc Phase 1 ramp-up is still at 62% utilisation; delays would hold back volumes and the INR1,300-1,350 crore FY27 revenue plan.
Heavy working capital and receivables/inventory build-up, with cash flow directed to capex and working capital during scale-up.
Fuel (LPG/propane) price and supply volatility; the GSPC natural gas pipeline agreement is still being signed.
Commissioning of the second colour coating line and solar plant in Q2 FY27; ramp-up timing for CCL2 (50-60% in H2).
Phase 2 funding not frozen (INR350 crore, additional debt about INR100 crore); execution and leverage risk.
Management's guidance on FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12% was not firmly confirmed; it said it is hard to be precise.
539046|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, pricing discipline and capacity ramp-up, but cautious on specifics: management declined to give precise FY27 margin or Phase 2 timing and said several figures are estimates. Some Q&A answers were unclear, including the order-intake and EBITDA-peak questions.
key_quotes: This quarter, the plant ran without any disruption.
all the new orders in Q1 were priced to fully cover the current cost environment with the margin buffer on top.
And this is 100% attributable to the pace of ramp-up of the Alu-Zinc line.
So demand or ability to sell is not a concern for us at all.

rows.label: New product launch

539056|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR178 crores and EBITDA 24% to INR90 crores (50.7% margin), with footfalls up 22%.
539056|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR178 crores, with footfalls up 22% to over 11.5 lakh visitors and parks revenue up 22% to INR161 crores. EBITDA rose 24% to INR90 crores and PAT rose 30% to INR58 crores. Management attributed the soft spots to an extended heat wave that kept Khopoli park non-operational for about two weeks and a shift in some CBSE school holiday calendars, and said it deliberately priced softer to build footfall. Management also announced the acquisition of a 50.002% stake in Mehsana Next Parks (Shanku's Water Park) for INR50 crores and the entry into indoor entertainment via a Hello Park franchise.

segments.name: Mumbai-Pune catchment (4 parks)
segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY on footfalls +19%; largest contributor and most affected by heat wave and Khopoli closure.

segments.name: Rest of Maharashtra (Shirdi, Saiteerth)
segments.commentary: Revenue +33% YoY on footfalls +14%; ARPU +17% on better product mix and higher guest spend.

segments.name: Gujarat (Surat, Mehsana)
segments.commentary: Footfalls +32% but revenue only +15%; ARPU lower YoY on visitor mix change and promotional pricing at Surat.

segments.name: Central India (Indore)
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing catchment: footfalls +48%, revenue +44% YoY.

segments.name: Hospitality (Novotel Imagicaa, 287 keys, Khopoli)
segments.commentary: Revenue largely stable despite occupancy at 62%; ARR INR9,657.

guidance_outlook: Target of 12 parks by 2030, adding roughly one park a year; 12 count includes smaller outdoor parks but excludes Hello Park indoor centres.
Hello Park: plan to add 2-3 indoor centres a year; first centre in Hyderabad (Lake Shore Y Junction Mall) later this year; second at Phoenix Mall, Surat.
Pricing: management said headroom exists to lift ticket prices; a price action plan is expected from Q3-Q4 FY27.
Mehsana Next Parks becomes a subsidiary now; consolidation reflected from Q2 FY27 onward. Management fee of 6-10% of revenue expected.
Debt/EBITDA: average 2.5-3.0x, peak up to 3.0-3.5x for limited periods.
Dave & Buster's integration into the listed company: not expected in the next three to four months; no firm timeline.
capex_capacity: New park cost guided at INR200-450 crores depending on location and size; B-tier city park about INR150 crores on 20-25 acres; A-category metro park about INR450 crores with about 25 rides.
Maintenance capex expensed in P&L at about 6-8% of revenue; new attractions capex budgeted at about 5% of top line.
Hello Park capex INR8-12 crores per centre (about 10,000 sq ft in malls); EBITDA margin 24-25% after mall rentals; payback 3-4 years; royalty 5% of revenue.
Ferris wheel of about 45 m costs INR20-25 crores landed in India.
Sabarmati Riverfront (Ahmedabad) project expected to be partly operational in the coming year if all goes well.
Funding: mix of internal accruals and moderate debt; banking limits approved by a couple of leading banks.
demand_pricing: Heat wave led to around two weeks of non-operation at Khopoli; some CBSE schools shifted holiday patterns; hotel bookings tapered during heat wave.
Management consciously ran softer ticket pricing this quarter to drive footfall and non-ticket spend; no price hikes taken yet during integration.
Surat ARPU fell as management tested price elasticity; revenue still above FY25 levels per management.
Ticketing and F&B/retail revenue reported combined by catchment; management agreed to split them in future press notes.
Spiritual parks: management in talks with state governments to replicate the Shirdi model; one or two locations expected in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is like-for-like growth weak given Q1 FY25 revenue of about INR184 crores vs INR177 crores now, and is ARPU flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the heat wave, Khopoli closure and school calendar shifts; it chose softer pricing to push footfall and expects headroom to correct pricing over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Hello Park economics: margins after rent, royalty and year-one footfall/ARPU?
qa_highlights.answer: Ticket price target INR800-900; ticketing about 65-70% of revenue; EBITDA margin 24-25% after mall rent; royalty 5% of revenue; capex about INR10 crores per 10,000 sq ft centre; payback 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters convert warrants priced at INR73.5?
qa_highlights.answer: Jai Malpani said the promoter group is positive and the conversion will happen before the due date.

qa_highlights.question: Funding for large capex and debt levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of internal accruals and moderate debt; average debt/EBITDA 2.5-3x, up to 3-3.5x for a limited period.

qa_highlights.question: Dave & Buster's integration timing?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm timeline; the model is still being stabilised; not expected in the next three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gujarat ARPU drop sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat price sensitivity; a deliberate price test; adjoining hotel and mall not yet operational; expected to recover over time.

risks_watch: Weather and seasonality: Q1 is the strongest quarter and Q2-Q3 are weak; the heat wave and monsoon drove the Q1 shortfall.
Pricing: ARPU has been flat for some time and the Gujarat ARPU fell sharply; the price-hike plan is due from Q3-Q4 FY27.
Gujarat concentration (Surat, Mehsana, Ahmedabad) as flagged by analysts.
Debt and capex funding for INR200-450 crore parks; the 2.5-3x debt/EBITDA guideline.
Promoter warrant conversion at INR73.5, timing still to be seen.
Hello Park execution: first centre in Hyderabad later this year; royalty of 5% and mall-dependent economics.
Disclosure: management moved to half-yearly calls; ticketing vs F&B split to be disclosed from next results.

539083|2026-03.headline: Inox Wind Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue flat YoY at INR1,306 crore; FY27 guidance of ~75% revenue growth and 20%+ EBITDA margin.
539083|2026-03.overview: Inox Wind reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR1,306 crore (flat YoY), EBITDA of INR333 crore, PBT of INR216 crore, PAT of INR106 crore and cash profit of INR268 crore, with FY26 revenue of about INR4,500 crore against an earlier INR5,000 crore target. Management attributed the shortfall to geopolitical disruption: delayed imported ECS components, shipping and commodity cost pressures, and a PSU contract with payment delays. The company is pivoting from turnkey EPC to equipment supply, with equipment supply now about 50% of the order book and a target of 75% to 80%. Inox Green (O&M) reported Q4 total income of INR120 crore (up 40% YoY) and EBITDA of INR57 crore, and it is guided to above INR600 crore EBITDA in FY27 after consolidating two pending acquisitions and a demerger.

financial_highlights.value: INR4,600 crore against INR5,000 crore guideline
financial_highlights.change: INR400 crore shortfall expected to be recovered in Q1-Q2 FY27
about INR40 crore from acquisition-linked debt, about INR10 crore value-added services, about INR10 crore treasury

segments.name: Inox Wind (WTG/EPC)
segments.commentary: Consolidated Q4 revenue INR1,306 crore flat YoY with EBITDA INR333 crore; order book 3.1 GW, with about 600 MW added in FY26, and visibility of more than 24 months. Only about 500 MW of the order book is from group company Inox Clean.

segments.name: Inox Green (O&M / evacuation)
segments.commentary: Portfolio 13+ GWp (about 10.5 GW wind, rest solar) with 96.5% average machine availability; Q4 EBITDA INR57 crore on about INR120 crore total income. Management says O&M margins are about 50%, and FY27 EBITDA is guided at above INR600 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% over FY26 (approx. INR7,500 crore on a INR4,500 crore base), with EBITDA margin of about 20% (stated as '20% to 20%').

Inox Green FY27 EBITDA guidance of upwards of INR600 crore, with management saying consolidation of two acquisitions (about 6.5 GW of wind O&M assets) will lift FY27 consol EBITDA and PAT multifold over FY26.
Group Inox Clean targets about 14 GW capacity by FY29, adding about 3 GW+ annually, of which 20-30% is expected to be wind, to drive recurring orders for Inox Wind.
New 4.4 MW turbine on track for approvals and commercial launch within calendar 2026, expected to aid penetration and margins.
Most EPC projects expected to be completed by H1 FY27, except one leading job, after which projects await statutory compliances for commissioning.
capex_capacity: Inox Green's two acquisitions cover about 6.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets; entity one order expected within a couple of weeks, entity two expected within 60-90 days.

Evacuation infrastructure demerger from Inox Green into Inox Renewable Solutions approved by NCLT Ahmedabad; about INR1,000 crore gross block and INR50-55 crore annual depreciation removed. Completion expected in 1-2 months.
Cranes moving in-house (half in-house, a couple more due this year); power transformer manufacturing started last year and ramping up.
Management plans to expand into power electronics (transformers, inverters, power electronics, ECS) with details to follow in coming months.
Group Inox Clean has about 2 GW installed, 6 GW solar module and 3 GW cell capacity; targets 10 GW each of IPP, cell and module over about 15 months.
demand_pricing: Order book 3.1 GW, diversified; recent wins include Aditya Birla, Gentari/Amplus, Jakson Green, First Energy and Leap Green. Multiple customer negotiations near closure.
Order mix is about 50:50 turnkey to equipment supply, targeted to move to 75% equipment supply (management also cited 75-80%).

Management says margins are guided at about 20% or higher on equipment supply; equipment supply is on LC terms, passing steel price changes through, reducing exposure to land/ROW cost and payment delays.
Revenue mix: about 10% O&M and 90% Inox Wind currently; O&M expected to rise to about 18-20% of consolidated revenue.
Management said it does not have FY27 order inflow targets and is 'sold out' for about 2.5 years on its stated ambitions.

qa_highlights.question: How will the two Inox Green acquisitions contribute to EBITDA and when will they be consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both acquisitions carry roughly 50% EBITDA margins, as they are former OEMs with substations and evacuation systems. Entity one's order is expected within a couple of weeks; entity two is 60-90 days away, and all revenues from 1 April 2026 are to be reflected in consolidated results.

qa_highlights.question: What was the FY26 working capital position against the INR5,000 crore guideline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it achieved INR4,600 crore against the INR5,000 crore guideline, with the INR400 crore balance expected in Q1-Q2 FY27 after supply-chain issues from delayed imported ECS components.

qa_highlights.question: What was actual MW execution in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give megawatt execution, saying the company guides on revenue only, and reiterated this stated policy.

qa_highlights.question: Will equipment supply shift raise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins stay at about 20% or higher, with equipment supply carrying less risk and more upfront cash; O&M at about 50% margin would add a higher-margin bias.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of INR61 crore at Inox Green: how much is recurring and how much is treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions (debt-linked, net of deferred tax, roughly INR25-26 crore at PAT level), INR10 crore is value-added services and INR10 crore is treasury income.

539118|2026-03.headline: VRL Logistics Q4 FY26 total income rose 6% YoY to INR859 crore, with tonnage back to 3% YoY growth and EBITDA margin at 21.4%.
539118|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR859 crore, up about 6% YoY and 3% QoQ, helped by better realisation, new clients and return of previously lost accounts. Realisation per ton was about INR8,147, up roughly 3% YoY, and daily tonnage crossed 11,500 tons. EBITDA margin was about 21.4%, down about 190 bps YoY from an exceptional Q4 FY25 (23%+) but up about 48 bps QoQ. FY26 total income was about INR3,245 crore, profit INR237 crore (up about 29%), and EBITDA margin 20.8%. Management guided to FY27 tonnage growth of 6-7% and kept an EBITDA margin of around 20%+ despite fuel cost pressure, which it plans to pass on via selective rate hikes and fuel surcharges.

segments.commentary: New customers contributed about 17% of quantity, lost customers reduced volume by about 14%, and existing customers grew about 1%.

539118|2026-06.headline: VRL Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs 81 crore (9% margin) on freight realisation up 9% to Rs 8,546/tonne and volumes up 9%.

539118|2026-09.headline: VRL Logistics Q2 FY27 total income rose about 20% YoY to INR967 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 23.3%, with management guiding 21-22% sustainable.

EBITDA rose 43% to INR226 crore with margin up 367 bps to 23.3%, and PAT nearly doubled to INR103 crore (10.7% margin). Net debt fell to INR337 crore from INR440 crore at March 2026, and a INR280 crore buyback at INR320 per share closed for tenders on 2 November 2026 with settlement due 9 November. Management flagged fuel cost volatility as the main risk and said freight rates would be cut in step with any fuel price reduction of about 5% or more.

539141|2026-06.headline: UFO Moviez Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹1,118 mn (vs ₹1,090 mn YoY) and advertisement revenue grew 33% YoY, helped by Dhurandhar spillover.
539141|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose about 3% YoY to ₹1,118 mn, while EBITDA was flat at ₹189 mn versus ₹193 mn a year earlier and PAT fell to ₹56 mn from ₹65 mn. Management credited a 33% YoY jump in advertisement revenue to the spillover from "Dhurandhar" and to annual advertisers onboarded around it. Product sales declined YoY, driven by roughly ₹7 crore lower international sales because Dubai imports were delayed by the regional war; management says these orders remain in hand. Releases fell to 399 titles in the quarter from 456 in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Advertisement revenue grew 33% YoY, with spillover from Dhurandhar and new annual advertisers. Advertising footprint is 3,891 screens (2,565 multiplex, 1,326 single).

segments.name: Product sales
segments.commentary: Declined YoY mainly due to international product sales falling about ₹7 crore on Dubai import delays. Indian product sales rose marginally. International sales were over 80% of product sales until last year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects delayed international product orders to be executed in Q2 FY27, or at the latest Q3 FY27.
Q2 FY27 started with releases 'Alpha', 'Dhamaal 4' and 'Jana Nayagan'; upcoming slate includes 'Batwara 1947', 'Toxic', 'Haiwan' and 'Awarapan 2'.
Management sees a consistent content pipeline with no significant gaps this year and expects advertising growth confidence over coming quarters, without quantifying it.
Historically 30-40% of advertising revenue comes from annual advertisers; the mix may evolve with the content pipeline.
capex_capacity: Advertising footprint at 3,891 screens (2,565 multiplex, 1,326 single). No capex or screen addition plans were discussed.
Off-screen (lobby) digital advertising is an unexplored opportunity; it would require a new arrangement with theatres and separate infrastructure investment, with no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Releases in Q1 FY27 were 399 (including versions/languages) vs 456 in Q1 FY26 and 459 in Q4 FY26.

Quarter drivers: Dhurandhar: The Revenge (carried over from Q4), Malayalam 'Drishyam 3', Marathi 'Raja Shivaji', and June titles 'Welcome to the Jungle', 'Main Vaapas Aaunga' and 'Cocktail 2'. Southern regional cinema stayed subdued.
Management says tactical advertising spikes last 1-4 weeks around major releases; Dhurandhar was described as an outlier with no precedent for that level of tactical spend.
Management did not quantify the share of the 33% advertising growth attributable to Dhurandhar.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 33% advertising growth came from Dhurandhar, and will growth normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a part of the growth is attributable to Dhurandhar spillover, plus new annual advertisers. It declined to give a percentage split.

qa_highlights.question: Trade receivables: how have they moved since March 31 and what was cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: India net debtors fell to ₹89.4 crore from ₹93.5 crore; consolidated net debtors fell to ₹148.1 crore from ₹152.4 crore. Management said receivables are within historical ageing and anything over one year is fully provided.

qa_highlights.question: Is the drop in product sales a concern or seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the YoY decline is mainly lower international product sales (about ₹7 crore) due to Dubai import delays from the regional war. Orders are in hand and expected in Q2 or by Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split between tactical and annual advertising?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically 30-40% of advertising revenue comes from annual advertisers and the balance from tactical spend. Management said the mix may change with the content pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Could digital ad boards in theatre lobbies be added?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said off-screen lobby advertising is a separate opportunity that is not yet pursued. It would need a new arrangement with theatres and infrastructure investment; the focus remains on on-screen inventory.

risks_watch: Advertising growth is concentrated in a few blockbuster titles; management could not quantify the Dhurandhar contribution, so normalisation risk is open.
Release count fell to 399 from 456 YoY; a thinner slate could weigh on tactical advertising.
International product sales depend on Dubai import logistics affected by the regional war; the pending orders must be executed by Q3 FY27.
PAT fell 14% YoY despite higher revenue; cost and margin drivers were not explained in the call.
Receivables are still ₹148.1 crore consolidated; watch whether DSO normalises as management expects.

Management was candid that international product sales fell on war-related import delays, and it framed the shortfall as deferred rather than lost.
key_quotes: The comforting factor is that these sales have not been lost. The orders continue to remain in hand and are only awaiting execution.
Overall, Q1 FY27 reflected encouraging theatrical trends for the industry, despite southern regional cinema remaining subdued.

539141|2026-09.headline: UFO Moviez Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹1,299 million (+17% YoY) but EBITDA was flat at ₹213 million and PAT fell to ₹64 million.
539141|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17% YoY to ₹1,299 million in Q2 FY27, driven by higher product-sale revenue from equipment sales, while EBITDA was broadly flat YoY at ₹213 million (vs ₹218 million) and net profit fell to ₹64 million from ₹75 million. H1 FY27 revenue rose 10% to ₹2,417 million, but H1 EBITDA (₹402 million) and PAT (₹121 million) were both lower YoY. Management attributed the margin squeeze mainly to a ~₹1 crore rise in variable incentive accrual and a 66% jump in equipment cost of goods sold, and guided to stronger Q3 and Q4 on a film slate of sequels and tentpole releases. Analyst questions focused on cost structure, operating leverage, promoter holding and dividend/buyback capacity.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue share costs rose only 2% YoY; management says services ad margin is above 55%. Ad revenue growth was not quantified for the quarter.

segments.name: VPF and Digital Cinema Network (CDC)
segments.commentary: VPF revenue share costs rose 16% YoY, in line with VPF revenue; management cites a 60-65% margin for VPF plus CDC services.

segments.name: Sale of equipment/products
segments.commentary: Product revenue rose 66% YoY to ₹422 million with a net margin up 68%; management puts historical product gross margin at 18-24% over about 20 quarters.

guidance_outlook: No revenue number committed for Q3 or Q4 FY27; management said advertisers are buying across film bunches and that the next two quarters should be better than the trailing quarters.
Management said no cost surprises are expected in Q3 and Q4, with costs budgeted and the incentive accrual already rationalised.
Board discussions on a capital distribution policy (dividend or buyback) are underway; management expects clarity by Q3 or Q4 FY27, not a payout for the current year.

Management said operating leverage should kick in at current ad and service revenue levels; illustrative ₹6 crore of extra ad revenue at ~70% PBT margin would lift PBT by ~₹4.2 crore (45-50%) from the reported ₹9.6 crore PBT.
capex_capacity: Advertising footprint at 3,946 screens: 2,606 multiplex and 1,340 single screens.
Releases in Q2 FY27: 386 movies including versions/languages, vs 462 in Q2 FY26 and 399 in Q1 FY27.
Capex, capacity utilisation and commissioning timelines were not discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Q2 film performance was mixed: Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Hanuman Ansh (sleeper hit), Awarapan 2 and Mirzapur: The Movie did well; Alpha, Batwara 1947, Toxic, Haiwaan underperformed.
Q3 FY27 started with Drishyam 3, Jailer 2, Udta Teer and Prahaar; upcoming slate includes Ramayana Part 1, King, Avengers: Doomsday, Eetha, Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Godzilla.
Advertisers are willing to commit to bunches of films rather than film-by-film, per management.
Management said Q3 and Q4 FY26 benefited from Dhurandhar, so the comparison base is tougher.

qa_highlights.question: How much accumulated losses remain, and can the company pay a dividend or buyback given its cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ~₹119 crore accumulated losses are tax losses held as a deferred tax asset. Companies Act losses were removed through a NCLT-approved share capital reduction about two years ago, so dividends and buybacks are permitted. A capital distribution policy is being discussed at board level, with an update expected in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter holding has been falling; will promoters raise their stake?
qa_highlights.answer: The fall is due to Apollo International being reclassified as non-promoter after depromoterisation in Q4 FY26, not promoter selling. Founder group (Valuable Technologies, Sanjay Gaikwad, Hete) stake is intact. Any increase is the promoters' decision; no indication has been given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct costs rise sharply and why did profit growth lag revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating direct costs rose 28% YoY, mostly from COGS on equipment sales (+66%), which was matched by product revenue (+66% to ₹422 million). EBITDA fell 2% YoY because the variable incentive accrual rose about ₹1 crore and fixed salary and SG&A increased. Excluding the incentive, EBITDA would be up about 2%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company quantify the operating leverage threshold, and are there further cost cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave an illustration: ₹6 crore of additional ad revenue at a 70% PBT margin would add about ₹4.2 crore to the reported ₹9.6 crore PBT. It said major manpower and SG&A cuts were made about 2.5 years ago and that further cost-cutting is not the focus.

qa_highlights.question: Can management give a Q3 advertising revenue range, and are there cost surprises ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Siddharth Bhardwaj declined to give a revenue number, citing no past practice, but said Q3 and H2 should beat expectations on the film slate. Asked for above ₹400 million per quarter, he did not confirm it. Ashish Malushte said there would be no cost surprises and costs are budgeted.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression: EBITDA margin fell as revenue grew 17% while EBITDA grew only about 2%; watch whether the product-sales mix keeps diluting margins.
Content dependence: several highly anticipated Q2 titles (Toxic, Batwara 1947, Haiwaan) underperformed, and management acknowledged audience selectivity.
Q3 and Q4 depend on the release slate (Ramayana Part 1, King, Avengers: Doomsday) and on advertisers committing to film bunches; no revenue guidance was given.
Dividend or buyback policy: timing is set for Q3 or Q4 FY27, and the board has not decided.
Management's statement that Q2 revenue was ₹1,118 million compared with Q1 FY27 conflicts with the ₹1,299 million Q2 figure, so the QoQ comparison needs verification against the filing.
539141|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the demand outlook and cost discipline, but evasive on specific Q3 and Q4 revenue numbers. Management was defensive when pressed on the margin decline and attributed it to incentive accrual and product-mix effects.
key_quotes: So the current reported 9.6 crores PBT would have gone up by 4.2 crores, so almost 45-50% increase in my PBT.
So we would refrain from committing a revenue number because we have never done this in the past.
And that is the accumulated losses that actually stands in my balance sheet in the form of a deferred tax asset.
There are not going to be any surprises when you see the revenues going up.

539150|2026-03.headline: PNC Infratech FY26 standalone revenue fell to INR 4,633 crore; management guides ~30% growth to INR 6,000 crore in FY27 with ~12% EBITDA margin.
539150|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR 1,458 crore with 12.02% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 100 crore, while FY26 standalone revenue of INR 4,633 crore was below earlier expectations due to delayed appointed dates on four projects worth over INR 4,400 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 6,000 crore (~30% growth), FY28 about 25% higher, and EBITDA near 12% in FY27, citing bitumen and crude-driven cost pressure partly offset by new escalation mechanisms. The company has an unexecuted order book above INR 22,000 crore, and it is diversifying into solar, BESS, coal mining and water. Net surplus on a standalone basis was INR 327 crore, while consolidated net debt to equity was 0.76 times.

segments.name: Highways (HAM/EPC/BOT)
segments.commentary: Four delayed projects (three NHAI, one MPRDC) worth over INR 4,400 crore drove lower FY26 turnover; 14 HAM projects with aggregate bid cost above INR 17,200 crore, 5 at PCOD/COD and 6 under construction.

segments.name: Water (Jal Jeevan Mission, irrigation)
segments.commentary: About INR 300 crore received in FY26 from state payments; FY27 revenue target INR 750 crore. Andhra irrigation: INR 380 crore work done to 31 March, ~INR 700 crore remaining, FY27 target ~INR 200 crore.

segments.name: Coal mining (MDO/item-rate EPC)
segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,956 crore over five years; FY26 turnover ~INR 68 crore; FY27 target ~INR 400 crore and FY28 ~INR 600 crore. Capex of ~INR 350 crore, of which ~INR 250 crore spent in FY26.

segments.name: Solar and BESS
segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,000 crore in development; physical execution to start Q3 FY27 after PPA with NHPC. Revenue target INR 600 crore in FY27 and INR 1,400 crore in FY28; equity requirement ~INR 400 crore, ~INR 120 crore in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue guided at ~30% growth to ~INR 6,000 crore; FY28 ~25% growth to ~INR 7,500 crore.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at ~12%; FY28 margin to be shared later, expected ~12% if commodity prices normalise.
FY27 new order inflow target ~INR 15,000 crore (INR 3,957 crore highways secured so far, plus ~INR 2,000 crore solar); 60-70% targeted from highways.
FY27 capex target INR 150 crore; interest cost expected to fall INR 3-4 crore from current quarter.
Equity infusion for HAM projects: INR 542 crore remaining over two years, ~INR 350 crore in FY27; internal accruals expected to cover it.
Revenue targets: Varanasi-Kolkata packages INR 1,600-1,800 crore; Jalna-Nanded and Pune Ring Road INR 1,500-1,600 crore; Haryana Orbital Rail balance ~INR 360 crore to FY27/FY28.
capex_capacity: Coal mining capex ~INR 350 crore, ~INR 250 crore spent in FY26; FY27 company capex target INR 150 crore.
Solar: land identified, connectivity in-principle approval received, final approval expected in 1.5-2 months; physical execution from Q3 FY27 after PPA with NHPC.
HAM equity: INR 1,623 crore total requirement (excluding two new HAMs awaiting LOA); INR 1,081 crore infused to March 2026.
Western Bhopal HAM: appointed date expected by end-September 2026 after alignment change; ~INR 100 crore FY27 revenue assumed.
Two new NHAI HAM projects in UP (bid cost INR 3,483 crore combined): appointed date expected in Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded 3,124 km in FY26, over 30% below the 4,500 km target; management expects awarding to improve but timing uncertain.
EPC competition described as cutthroat; management sees less competition in larger HAM and BOT-Toll projects, citing reduced bidder numbers on two recent HAM wins of about INR 1,700 crore each.
Company submitted 15 EPC bids and one HAM bid worth ~INR 14,000 crore; price bids expected to open before end-May and in June.

MoRTH cost escalation mechanism from 1 April 2026 for EPC/HAM/PBMC projects with monthly price adjustment (earlier three months); management expects revised authority cost or extended compensation for new tenders.
Back-to-back pass-through: SPV inflation indices (WPI/CPI) and bitumen price compensation flow to EPC contractor per management.
Vertis Infrastructure Trust: entire payment for the 12-asset divestment received, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY27 and FY28 revenue and margins be viewed given the FY26 shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided ~30% growth to ~INR 6,000 crore in FY27 and ~25% in FY28 (~INR 7,500 crore), with ~12% EBITDA in FY27; some margin pressure expected in Q1-Q2 from bitumen and crude costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the INR 6,000 crore guidance between approved and pending projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance excludes new orders; based on awarded projects with appointed dates, except Western Bhopal (~INR 100 crore assumed) and only 30% of the INR 2,000 crore solar order (INR 600 crore) is included.

qa_highlights.question: Will diversification into new segments hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no cross-subsidy effect is expected; earlier target was 13-13.5% EBITDA, now guided ~12% across the mix, with water and irrigation earlier delivering similar margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on the Varanasi-Kolkata packages and Haryana Orbital Rail?
qa_highlights.answer: Varanasi-Kolkata: INR 336 crore revenue in FY26, INR 1,600-1,800 crore targeted in FY27, no obstructions. Haryana Orbital Rail: over INR 400 crore done (53%), balance ~INR 360 crore to be executed in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost outlook and what drove the Q4 jump to INR 30 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 rise was from working capital utilisation and term loan interest on machine financing; management expects a reduction of INR 3-4 crore from the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company bid for BOT-Toll projects and how will asset monetisation proceed?
qa_highlights.answer: No BOT-Toll bid submitted yet; evaluating NHAI BOT-Toll opportunities and direct bidding is planned. Monetisation of the five PCOD assets is under evaluation; no framework announced.

risks_watch: Bitumen and fuel cost volatility from West Asia tensions; margin pressure expected in near term before escalation benefits fully flow.

Solar revenue (INR 600 crore FY27) depends on 30% land possession, PPA with NHPC and final approvals.

Consolidated net debt to equity of 0.76x and rising working-capital-linked interest cost.

rows.why: Guidance is ~30% revenue growth to INR 6,000 crore in FY27 and ~25% to INR 7,500 crore in FY28, backed by an unexecuted order book above INR 22,000 crore, Varanasi-Kolkata targeted at INR 1,600-1,800 crore and Haryana Orbital Rail balance of about INR 360 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, and FY27 company capex is held at INR 150 crore, but HAM equity needs about INR 350 crore in FY27 and the INR 1,623 crore total requirement plus solar equity of about INR 400 crore point to further equity-linked commitments.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 6,000 crore (~30% growth) and ~12% EBITDA, and the guidance excludes new orders, but NHAI awarded 3,124 km in FY26, over 30% below the 4,500 km target, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 standalone revenue of INR 4,633 crore fell short after four projects worth over INR 4,400 crore saw delayed appointed dates, and Western Bhopal, the two UP HAMs and MPRDC are still exposed to timing slippage, while bitumen and crude costs pressure margins in Q1-Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Solar and BESS platform with a ~INR 2,000 crore order in development moves to physical execution from Q3 FY27 after the NHPC PPA, with only INR 600 crore (30% of the order) included in FY27 guidance.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow target of ~INR 15,000 crore
rows.why: Only INR 3,957 crore of highways secured so far plus ~INR 2,000 crore solar, with 15 EPC and one HAM bid worth ~INR 14,000 crore pending price-bid opening in May-June, and NHAI awarded 3,124 km in FY26 versus a 4,500 km target.

rows.label: MoRTH escalation mechanism from 1 April 2026
rows.why: Monthly price adjustment (earlier three months) applies to EPC/HAM/PBMC projects, and management expects revised authority cost or extended compensation for new tenders, partly offsetting bitumen and crude costs.

rows.label: Interest cost falls INR 3-4 crore from current quarter
rows.why: Q4 FY26 interest rose to about INR 30 crore on working-capital use and machine term loans, and consolidated net debt to equity is 0.76x with consolidated debt of INR 5,151 crore against cash of INR 2,856 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR 22,000 crore order book and the ~30% FY27 revenue and ~12% EBITDA guidance, but cautious on margins from bitumen and crude costs and on appointed-date timing; analysts pressed on the FY26 revenue shortfall, the FY27 order target, and the rise in interest cost.

539150|2026-06.headline: PNC Infratech Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs 1,518 crore and PAT to Rs 271 crore, while management kept FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 6,000 crore.

Net worth Rs 7,147 crore; total debt Rs 5,448 crore (D/E 0.76x); cash and bank Rs 2,870 crore
About Rs 20 crore in Q1, guided run-rate about Rs 20 crore/quarter
financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 30 crore in Q4

segments.name: Water (Jal Jeevan Mission and irrigation)

JJM revenue targeted at Rs 700-800 crore in FY27 and about Rs 1,000 crore in FY28; project to complete by December 2028.
Andhra Pradesh irrigation: Rs 150 crore targeted in FY27, balance about Rs 600 crore in FY28, subject to timely payment.
Effective tax rate guided at 25-27% for FY27. Capex guided at about Rs 150 crore for standalone FY27 and FY28 (Q1 spend about Rs 70 crore), plus about Rs 350 crore on the mining project.

Pantnagar airport expected before end-September 2026; Bhopal bypass AD pushed to Q3 CY26 due to scope change.
capex_capacity: Standalone capex guided at about Rs 150 crore for FY27 and about Rs 150 crore for FY28; Rs 70 crore spent on machinery in Q1.

Rs 1,187 crore of HAM equity infused to June 2026 out of Rs 1,623 crore requirement (excluding the two new HAMs).

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for Kanpur-Lucknow issue (non-performer or bidding ban), possible duration, UP-level bidding impact, repair cost and standalone vs subsidiary impact?

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 and FY28 guidance changing, given about Rs 5,900 crore of new business secured versus Rs 12,000-15,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: No change. FY27 revenue Rs 6,000 crore, FY28 Rs 7,500 crore, about 12% margin and FY27 new business target Rs 12,000-15,000 crore all maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Barabanki-Mustafabad appointed date and equity quantum for the two new HAMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Concession agreements signed 16 July 2026 with 150 days for financial closure. Appointed date follows NHAI handing over 90% of land. Equity expected around Rs 400 crore, not Rs 490 crore as the analyst suggested.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital details: inventory, debtors, payables, mobilisation advance, retention, unbilled and HAM/water debtors?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory Rs 847 crore, debtors Rs 1,900 crore, trade payables Rs 680 crore, mobilisation advance Rs 178 crore, retention Rs 295 crore, unbilled Rs 462 crore, HAM debtors Rs 479 crore, water debtors Rs 925 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise in Q1 and what is the ICD and interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose due to a term loan for machinery financing, repayable over 4-5 years. ICD is Rs 485 crore. Quarterly interest run-rate about Rs 20 crore, and debt is expected to decline.

qa_highlights.question: Water (JJM and AP irrigation) revenue targets and receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: JJM revenue Rs 700-800 crore in FY27 and about Rs 1,000 crore in FY28, project completion by December 2028. Rs 741 crore excluding GST is due from government. AP irrigation Rs 150 crore in FY27 and about Rs 600 crore in FY28, with Rs 153 crore receivable and Rs 94 crore release expected within 7-10 days.

qa_highlights.question: Coal mining and solar revenue and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal mining revenue about Rs 500 crore each in FY27 and FY28; total mining capex about Rs 350 crore, front-loaded. Solar EPC about Rs 2,000 crore with equity about Rs 400 crore; solar revenue minimal in FY27, more than Rs 1,000 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Order book reconciliation versus last quarter's Rs 22,000 crore figure?
qa_highlights.answer: The earlier Rs 22,000 crore included the two new HAMs; the current unexecuted order book is about Rs 19,100 crore, including the two HAMs, Pantnagar airport, Ganga bridge and LDA flyover.

rows.label: Receivables collection from government (JJM and AP irrigation)

539150|2026-09.headline: PNC Infratech Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 17% to ₹1,146 crore; FY27 guidance of ₹6,000 crore revenue and 12% margin reiterated.
539150|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹1,146 crore (up 17% YoY) with EBITDA of ₹138 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT of ₹73 crore. H1 FY27 standalone revenue was ₹2,664 crore (up 26%), including a ₹217 crore arbitration award booked on realisation. Management kept FY27 revenue (₹6,000 crore), 12% EBITDA margin and ₹12,000–15,000 crore order inflow guidance unchanged, while the NHPC BESS project was exited after the LOA lapsed. The High Court stay on NHAI debarment (granted October 12, 2026) allows bidding to resume, with the next hearing on November 26, 2026.

financial_highlights.value: 0.21x (0.10x net of cash and current investments of ₹1,252 crore)
Over ₹18,000 crore (incl. two new NHAI HAM projects)

segments.name: Highways (core)
segments.commentary: Highways are 63% of the ₹18,000 crore unexecuted order book; 14 HAM projects with aggregate bid cost above ₹17,200 crore, of which 6 are at PCOD/COD and 5 under construction.

segments.name: Water, canal, railway and airport
segments.commentary: These contracts are about 21% of the order book. Water receivables fell after ₹267 crore was released in the quarter; the Pantnagar airport EPC (₹302 crore, 24 months) was awarded in July 2026.

segments.name: Coal mining
segments.commentary: Coal mining is 16% of the order book. FY27 coal revenue guidance was cut to ₹350–400 crore from ₹500 crore, with about ₹160 crore executed through September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹6,000 crore unchanged, including the ₹217 crore arbitration award; H2 implied revenue of about ₹3,336 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 12% maintained on ₹5,800 crore excluding the arbitration award; management said bitumen cost pressure is already factored in.
FY27 order inflow guidance of ₹12,000–15,000 crore maintained; ₹4,260 crore secured so far, with ₹8,000–11,000 crore targeted before March 31, 2027.
FY28 revenue guidance of ₹7,500 crore (about 25% growth) and 12% margin retained; management cites ₹15,000 crore opening FY28 order book.
Water revenue FY27 revised to about ₹650 crore (from ₹750 crore); FY28 water about ₹1,000 crore. Coal FY28 about ₹500 crore.
Capex guidance: about ₹200 crore for FY27 (₹155 crore spent in H1) and about ₹150 crore for FY28. Equity for HAM projects: ₹913 crore outstanding, ₹460 crore targeted in FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex of ₹155 crore spent in H1 FY27; about ₹200 crore expected for FY27, implying roughly ₹50 crore in H2.
Equity infused in HAM projects: ₹1,212 crore to date against ₹2,125 crore requirement; ₹913 crore balance over two to three years, funded by internal accruals.

NHAI HAM projects (two, concession signed July 16, 2026): financial closure within 150 days; appointed date expected in Q4 FY27; 730-day build period with 35–40% progress in FY28 and about 60% in FY29.
MPRDC Bhopal bypass HAM: appointed date expected before December 31, 2026, with some progress in FY27.

Canal project paused until mid-November due to water release; about ₹60–70 crore work in FY27 and about ₹400 crore in FY28; ₹495 crore executed to date, about ₹790 crore left; extension to December 31, 2028.
NHPC BESS project exited: PPA/PSA not signed in time, LOA cancelled, bid security refunded; excluded from order book.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded about 230 route km in Q2 FY27 vs 107 km in Q1; 19 of 54 identified projects approved and 17 appraised for the remainder of FY27.
17 bids submitted worth ₹16,600 crore (13 EPC, 3 HAM, 1 TBCB); price bids not yet opened. Pipeline of about 80 projects worth ₹180,000 crore to be bid through January 2027.
Management says competition is intense in small EPC jobs but less so in large, fund-based HAM and TBCB projects.
Input costs rose from West Asia conflict (diesel, bitumen); MoRTH/NHAI/AAI extended monthly price-adjustment escalation through December 31, 2026, with limited mitigation.
Management reports ₹267 crore water receipts and ₹183 crore Andhra Pradesh irrigation receipts in the quarter; irrigation revenue of about ₹500 crore booked.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹244 crore arbitration award included in Q2 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It is recognised only on realisation; ₹217 crore of the arbitration was recognised in H1 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will the arbitration award be included in the ₹6,000 crore guidance and the 12% margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the ₹6,000 crore includes it. The 12% margin applies to the ₹5,800 crore remaining revenue excluding the award.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone debt has doubled while cash is high; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is equipment finance (about ₹400 crore+, five-year terms) and short-term working capital; ₹494 crore is inter-corporate deposits from operational SPVs. Management denied the position is arbitrage-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company buy back shares at current prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is thinking along those lines (buyback), without giving details.

qa_highlights.question: Are the NHAI HAM appointed dates on track?
qa_highlights.answer: MPRDC appointed date expected before December 31; NHAI HAM projects expected in Q4 FY27, with 90% ROW achieved on the NHAI projects and financial closure within 150 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹8,000–11,000 crore H2 order inflow come if the NHAI ban persists after November?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes the relief continues and expects over 50–60% of new orders from NHAI, MoRTH and NHIDCL, with 30–40% from non-NHAI.

risks_watch: Stay on NHAI debarment order: next hearing November 26, 2026; bidding eligibility depends on outcome.
Standalone debt rising while cash is held; management attributes this to working capital and equipment finance, with inter-corporate deposits from SPVs.
Input cost inflation (bitumen, diesel, batteries, logistics) with only partial escalation coverage through December 31, 2026.
Order inflow of ₹8,000–11,000 crore needed in H2 to meet the ₹12,000–15,000 crore guidance, with no visibility beyond the 17 bids pending price opening.
Overseas expansion (Kazakhstan subsidiary, Georgia bid) and the lack of a clear growth driver after BESS exit; management flagged aggressive bidding in roads.
Coal mining execution affected by local resistance on land vacation, though October execution improved; water receivables pending.

We are giving the guidance of 12% EBITDA on the INR5,800 crores, excluding the arbitration claim.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two NHAI HAM projects (concession signed July 16, 2026) expected to reach appointed date in Q4 FY27 and MPRDC Bhopal HAM before Dec 31, 2026, but capacity is not quantified and HAM projects add equity rather than plant capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY28 revenue guided at Rs 7,500 cr (about 25% over FY27) backed by a Rs 15,000 cr opening order book and NHAI awards of about 230 route km in Q2 FY27 versus 107 km in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is guided modestly at about Rs 200 cr for FY27 (Rs 155 cr spent in H1) and Rs 150 cr for FY28, with HAM equity of Rs 460 cr targeted in FY28; management is also thinking about a buyback, but no utilisation figure is disclosed to justify a new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 revenue at Rs 6,000 cr (H1 Rs 2,664 cr), and the Rs 217 cr arbitration award is already included, leaving little room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coal FY27 revenue was already cut to Rs 350-400 cr from Rs 500 cr and water to about Rs 650 cr from Rs 750 cr, and H2 needs about Rs 3,336 cr revenue plus Rs 8,000-11,000 cr order inflow amid NHAI debarment risk with a hearing on Nov 26, 2026.

rows.label: H2 order inflow of Rs 8,000-11,000 cr
rows.why: Rs 4,260 cr secured so far against a Rs 12,000-15,000 cr FY27 target, with 17 bids worth Rs 16,600 cr pending price opening and dependence on NHAI debarment being lifted after the Nov 26, 2026 hearing.

rows.label: Share buyback under consideration
rows.why: Management said it is thinking along buyback lines without details, while standalone net cash is Rs 1,252 cr against standalone debt that has doubled.

rows.label: Standalone debt rising despite cash
rows.why: Standalone net debt/equity is 0.21x gross and 0.10x net of Rs 1,252 cr cash, but debt has doubled on equipment finance and Rs 494 cr inter-corporate deposits, so a reduction is not guided.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY27/FY28 revenue guidance, order pipeline and 12% margin but defensive on the BESS exit, the rising standalone debt and dependence on NHAI order inflow; analysts pushed on feasibility of the Rs 8,000-11,000 cr H2 inflow and the arbitration-driven margin.

539199|2026-03.headline: SG Finserve FY26 PAT rose 58% to INR 128 crore on a INR 3,936 crore loan book (up 75%), with management guiding AUM growth of 25-30% medium term and 35-40% for FY27.
539199|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 operating income of INR 334 crore (up 96% YoY), closing loan book of INR 3,936 crore (up 75%, stated as an all-time high) and PAT of INR 128 crore (up 58%). Q4 PAT was INR 42 crore, up 30% QoQ, and Q4 fee income was about INR 6.2 crore against about INR 1.5-1.9 crore in earlier periods. Management reiterated nil NPA as its guidance and said it is comfortable with leverage of about 1.9x, aiming for 3x over two to three years without fresh equity. Q&A covered NPA philosophy, TReDS entry, related-party exposure and the sharp rise in fee income, and several answers were framed as conservative guidance.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / anchor financing)
segments.commentary: More than three-fourths of the business per management. Construction is the largest sector at about 35% of AUM, followed by automotive; average ticket about INR 5 crore per borrower.

segments.name: Factoring
segments.commentary: Bilateral factoring commercialised in March 2026 with INR 175 crore outstanding at 31 March. TReDS participation expected to go live in Q1 FY27 through RXIL and M1xchange.

segments.name: Cross-sell (LAP, working capital, business loans)
segments.commentary: Opportunistic cross-sell within the anchor/dealer ecosystem at near-zero acquisition cost; management said it is not a core focus. Mobile is about 2% of AUM.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 25-30% CAGR medium to long term; FY27 aspiration of 35-40% AUM growth.
Profit guidance of 30-35% CAGR, measured on full-year PAT of the previous financial year, not Q4 exit run rate.
Profitability range: ROA 4.5-5%, ROE 14-16%, cost to income 13-17%.
Leverage to rise from about 2x to 3x over two to three years, in phases; comfortable range 2x-3x.
Internal AUM target of INR 10,000 crore in three to four years without fresh equity, with bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore.
NPA guidance remains nil; management said the aim is no losses, while acknowledging that lending involves losses.
capex_capacity: Operates from 30 hub locations pan-India, each covering about a 100 km radius; business is 100% domestic with no import-export financing.
Bank lines of more than INR 3,000 crore, with INR 3,000-3,500 crore estimated, not fully utilised.
Gross disbursements for FY26 crossed INR 25,000 crore; Q4 disbursements about INR 7,700 crore against a book of about INR 3,900 crore (average churn about 45 days).
New businesses (unspecified) are under groundwork, subject to regulatory approvals; timing of FY27 or FY28 uncertain.
demand_pricing: Management said fewer than 100 of the top 500 corporates are active in supply chain finance, and only 25-30% of anchors' sales are covered by organised programmes, so headroom is large.

Management estimated the wider supply chain market, including PSU banks, at upward of INR 1 lakh crore; five to six private banks and a few NBFCs each run AUM of INR 10,000-15,000 crore in dealer finance.
Fee income is being pursued as a strategy; fees on disbursements range from 10 paise to 50 paise, with some cases at 1%.
Management said no stress is visible in top sectors but is monitoring geopolitical and fuel/gas supply risks; steel import effects are yet to be assessed.

qa_highlights.question: How does the business model support nil NPAs, and is there a buffer in NPA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exposure is short-term (about 45-day churn), invoice-backed and end-use monitored, with anchors paid directly and early-warning tracking of dealer cycles. It said Ind AS ECL and RBI rules limit conservative provisioning, with about INR 18 crore provision already held; the guidance is nil NPA by design.

qa_highlights.question: What is the leverage target and how will growth be funded?

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income jump in Q4?

539199|2026-09.headline: SG Finserve posted an all-time high quarterly PAT of INR59 crore in Q2 FY27, with loan book at ~INR5,700 crore and H1 PBT of INR150 crore.
539199|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR59 crore and a loan book of about INR5,700 crore, up roughly 25% QoQ on period-end basis (average AUM up 17% QoQ). Asset-to-equity rose from 2.8x to 3.7x over the last year, and quarterly ROE reached about 15%. Management revised its mid-term debt-to-equity ceiling from 3x to 4x, which it said would take AUM to about INR11,000 crore, and it expects no equity raise this year. New initiatives during the quarter included factoring/TReDS, digital lending, loan against property (LAP), and a stake in an AI/digital subsidiary, plus a GIFT City subsidiary and an AIF pending SEBI approval.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / deep-tier)
segments.commentary: Supply chain is ~70% of AUM. Group ecosystem share of book has fallen to 25%; the company powers ~60 brands. Steel and building products ~35% of AUM and auto ~20%.

segments.name: Factoring / TReDS
segments.commentary: Factoring licence received in March 2026; now ~15% of book after starting in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Digital lending (BharatPe merchant LSP model)
segments.commentary: ~10,000 loans disbursed; book only INR121 crore at 30 Sep 2026. Management expects ~10% of AUM in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP) / business loans
segments.commentary: Just started in Delhi NCR with four disbursals and INR17 crore outstanding; tickets above INR25 lakh.

segments.name: Project finance
segments.commentary: 12 accounts disbursed recently, none commercially operational; management expects starts in 6-9 months.

guidance_outlook: Debt-to-equity mid-term ceiling revised from 3x to 4x; board approved incremental borrowing in the call's board meeting.
AUM growth guidance of 30-35% CAGR on a one-year-forward basis; profitability CAGR guidance of 35-40%.
Management targets INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM in 2-3 years, implying ~100% growth from current book; equity dilution or higher leverage mandate expected only after that.
Full-year PAT guidance of INR225 crore reiterated; management said it may do slightly better.
Expects around 7,000 crore AUM by year end on current run rate (per management comment); Q2/Q4 seasonality of 2-3% on the higher side.
Target of adding 2 anchor corporates per month for the next 12-18 months.
GIFT City finance subsidiary (~INR48 crore investment approved) expected operational in about a year, subject to RBI and IFSCA approvals.
Planning to keep ROA above 4.5% and cost-to-income below 15%; yield maintained at ~13% on AUM.
capex_capacity: Headcount ~100 (roughly doubled in one year); per-employee annualised PAT above INR2 crore; presence in 34 locations.
Digital lending built on LSP framework; in-house AI/digital stack being built via a 15% stake in a subsidiary rather than external SaaS.
New subsidiaries: AIF (Cat III equity AIF, SEBI approval awaited), AMC subsidiary, GIFT City finance company (~INR48 crore), shared services company (cost amount undecided), AI/technology subsidiary.
Project finance: 12 accounts, none yet operational.
LAP: specialist team hired; scaling to be gradual, starting in Delhi NCR.
demand_pricing: Wallet share across the ~60 anchor brands is under 5%; management targets doubling to 10%, plus 20-25 new brands in the next year.
~800 active customers, average ticket ~INR7 crore; per-borrower appetite limited.

Lending rates are benchmarked to the SGFL benchmark rate; management said any repo-linked cost increase would be passed on, though benchmark not yet raised.
Management positions the company as filling the INR10-20 'untied' portion of borrowers' funding need after banks/NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity this financial year, given borrowings near 3x net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Debt-to-equity mandate raised to 4x, with incremental borrowing approved by the board; equity dilution or higher leverage considered 2-3 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue grow ~18% QoQ while AUM grew 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Income accrues on daily outstanding; average AUM grew 17% QoQ, so period-end growth overstates income growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost as a percentage of income rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher leverage (asset-to-equity 2.8x to 3.7x); management said this lifts ROE.

qa_highlights.question: What is the collection efficiency and DPD profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly collection efficiency 99.5%; 60+ DPD is zero overall and 30+ DPD is zero in non-supply-chain book; 0.5% slips to 1+ DPD and is mostly collected within 30 DPD.

qa_highlights.question: How does the RBI draft on revolving credit affect the model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the product is term-based with no rollover or extension, so it is aligned; only documentation and reporting systems need tweaks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds and funding mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Single source is banks and NBFCs (19 lenders), plus opportunistic commercial paper; cost of borrowing about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 credit cost increase a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisioning is an ECL/IRAC regulatory requirement, not cash credit cost; ~INR25 crore accumulated on ~INR5,700 crore book, and nil NPA is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Why would borrowers choose SG over banks?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowers often get INR80-90 of a INR100 requirement from banks; SG funds the remaining untied portion, under a coexistence model across PSU banks, private banks, large NBFCs and mid-layer NBFCs.

risks_watch: Leverage rising toward the 4x D/E ceiling; equity dilution likely around INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM given the ~3x price-to-book; watch the CCD/OCD option.

Draft RBI norms on revolving credit could require documentation and system changes for supply-chain products (about two-thirds of AUM).
BharatPe digital-lending book: management acknowledged gross NPAs are possible, relying on FLDG and LSP cushions.
New businesses (AIF, GIFT City, LAP, project finance) carry execution and gestation risk; project finance accounts not yet operational.
Management said the Q2 front-loading of growth may normalise; the 30-35% growth guide must be tested in H2.
Opex discipline as headcount and locations expand; the cost-to-income target is below 15%.

539221|2026-03.headline: Sportking expects top line up 7-10% and margins to expand 15-20% QoQ over next three quarters on higher yarn prices and a long sales book.

Demand was attributed to China's resurgence as a cotton yarn importer, Bangladesh recovery, and a stronger rupee-driven competitiveness shift for Indian spinning. Management said spreads are at roughly three-year highs and expects margins to expand over the next two to three quarters, with the 150,000-spindle greenfield project slated for commercial operations in Q3 FY27. Acquisitions of a majority stake in Marvel Dyers and Processors and the Sobhagia Sales manufacturing facilities were approved, with closure targeted within the calendar year.

segments.commentary: Accounted for 22% of Q1 revenue. Zoetis offtake was absent this quarter; Mangalore small-molecule utilisation expected to ramp this year, and Bayview biologics facility targeted to be operational later this year with revenue from FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided to a single-digit decline in rupee terms; analyst question cited a low-single-digit decline and a mid-single-digit decline was also referenced in the Q&A.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided in the mid-20s, relying on a stronger H2 with H1 the weakest period; Q4 is seasonally the strongest quarter.
Management expects a return to profitable and sustainable growth from FY28, with double-digit growth targeted from next fiscal.
Zoetis is not expected to fall to zero in FY28; it has inventory for a couple of years and delivery obligations in H2 FY27. Zoetis FY28 forecast expected by year-end.
Bayview will not be capitalised in FY27; minimal Bayview expenses expected in the P&L this year.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex about INR 70 crore, mainly Bayview facility plus automation and AI platforms; further investment planned through the year to operationalise Bayview.

Bayview (US biologics) to be operationalised later this year; customers will be locked in only after operationalisation. One or two expressions of interest converted into project-based CMO requirements in the US, with revenue from next year.
Mangalore site was under-utilised; lock-ins for commercial and clinical molecules secured and significant utilisation ramp-up expected this fiscal and further in FY28.

Stelis facility: customers signed and batches taken; ramp-up during this year and into next year. Molecules mostly clinical or development stage, with no large-volume commercial molecule from Unit 3 yet.
demand_pricing: Management said the company drifted into commoditised research services with pricing pressure; it is deliberately not competing on low-cost offerings, leading to client attrition.
Biologics dependence on one large customer (Zoetis) cost about $50 million of revenue impact; spare capacity created and being filled with new customers.

Pipeline for large-molecule CDMO is described as robust; US-based capacity seen as benefiting from tariffs and Make in US demand, and Biosecure Act seen as helping shift molecules from China to India.
New commercial organisation led by Abhijit Zutshi (ex-CCO, Biocon Generics) is building segmentation and business development; management expects RFP-to-revenue gestation.
Management said green shoots are visible and will give more clarity from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance cut from roughly flat to a decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the loss of Zoetis contribution this quarter; gap expected to be filled by other customers only by fiscal year-end, so guidance is a slight decline.

qa_highlights.question: Will the revenue gap be filled by clinical or commercial molecules?
qa_highlights.answer: A combination; Mangalore has commercial and clinical lock-ins with significant utilisation ramp this year and into FY28, while Bayview revenue depends on discussions to be converted by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did discovery clients attrite, and what is the value-added vs commoditised split?
qa_highlights.answer: Attrition was driven by cost-based competition in commoditised services that management chose not to match; the split was deferred to an offline discussion.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue decline is due to Zoetis, and is Zoetis now at zero?
qa_highlights.answer: Zoetis impact was about $50 million; not zero, as Zoetis holds inventory for a couple of years with H2 FY27 delivery obligations and is not expected to be zero in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What gives visibility to a strong H2 margin pick-up to hit mid-20s EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain cited H2 revenue uptick, savings from FY26 cost actions and continued cost initiatives, seasonally strong Q4, and steady-state margins historically above mid-20s.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost measures and the margin outlook for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost optimisation covers people and operating expenses, with technology as a lever; Bayview not capitalised this year. Management said it is too early to comment on FY28 margins but does not expect flat margins.

risks_watch: H1 FY27 revenue and margin weakness; guidance depends on H2 ramp across Mangalore, Stelis and Bayview.
Zoetis run-off: delivery obligations in H2 FY27 and FY28 forecast due by year-end.
Client attrition in research services and pricing pressure in commoditised discovery work.
Bayview operationalisation timing and conversion of expressions of interest into contracts.
Forex hedge losses (INR 50 crore in Q1) and their effect on reported margins; cash decline from INR 1,800 crore last year to INR 1,541 crore.
539268|2026-06.management_tone: Candid and cautious: management openly acknowledged a transition year, loss of a major customer and over-reliance on commoditised work, while staying confident on CDMO and AI-led discovery recovery from FY28. Specifics on pipeline, long-term growth and discovery segment splits were deferred to next quarter or offline.
key_quotes: FY27 is a year of transition for Syngene. It is a year of course correction, strategic renewal, and disciplined execution under a new leadership team.
The loss of that business has had a significant impact on our near-term financial performance and has reinforced the importance of building a more diversified and resilient commercial portfolio.
Otherwise, it becomes a race to the bottom because it becomes commoditized and then you're just basically providing very low-margin services, which is what has happened to us.

rows.why: Mid-20s EBITDA margin guided for FY27 versus 12% in Q1 (including INR 50 crore forex hedge loss), relying on H2 revenue uptick, FY26 cost-action savings and seasonally strong Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bayview US biologics facility to be operationalised later this year (INR 70 crore Q1 capex, not capitalised in FY27), and Mangalore and Stelis ramp-ups are under way with lock-ins secured; revenue from FY28.

rows.label: Return to double-digit growth from FY28

rows.why: One or two expressions of interest converted into project-based US CMO requirements with revenue from next year; the pipeline is described as robust, but conversion to contracts is still pending.
