539289|2026-03.headline: Aurum PropTech Q4 FY26 continuing-operations revenue rose 10.2% QoQ to INR 123.85 crores, with second straight profitable quarter and FY26 revenue up 50.8% to INR 381.09 crores.
539289|2026-03.overview: Management framed Q4 FY26 as an inflection point: second consecutive PAT-positive quarter, operating leverage starting to show, and debt retirement planned by June 30, 2026 via sale of buildings. Continuing-operations PBT was INR 1.85 crores in Q4 versus INR 2.93 crores in Q3, so profitability is still thin on a pre-tax basis. Distribution was the main growth engine, with PropTiger reporting its highest-ever quarterly gross commission of INR 42.8 crores. Management reiterated AI-first positioning (business value optimization and a longer-term "Unified Brain") but gave few quantified AI outcomes; the first measurable target is revenue per team member.

financial_highlights.change: +10.2% QoQ vs INR 112.36 crores in Q3

financial_highlights.metric: Total income from continuing operations (Q4 FY26)
Profit before tax from continuing operations (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR 2.93 crores in Q3 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Total income incl. discontinued operations (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: +8.1% QoQ vs INR 124.55 crores; excludes INR 17.72 crores other income from partial building sale

financial_highlights.metric: Loss before tax from continuing operations (FY26)
financial_highlights.change: improved by INR 28.44 crores vs loss of INR 43.40 crores in FY25

segments.name: Rental (continuing)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 52.70 crores vs INR 52.09 crores in Q3; segment loss INR 3.61 crores in Q4. FY26 revenue INR 200.71 crores, +27.4% YoY, with segment loss INR 18.54 crores. Including discontinued building operations, Q4 rental revenue was INR 55.20 crores and combined loss INR 2.74 crores.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 66.87 crores vs INR 59.60 crores in Q3 (+12.2%); segment profit INR 13.63 crores in Q4. FY26 revenue INR 172.55 crores, +117.7% YoY, with segment profit INR 32.30 crores. Management cites 22-25% segment margins.

segments.name: Capital
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 4.28 crores vs INR 0.67 crores in Q3; segment loss INR 0.53 crores in Q4. FY26 revenue INR 7.84 crores vs INR 15.94 crores in FY25 (down), segment loss INR 5.27 crores.

segments.name: PropTiger (within distribution)
segments.commentary: Highest-ever quarterly gross commission of INR 42.8 crores in Q4 FY26; 175 active developer clients and 11 active mandates; developer relationships cited at 180+.

segments.name: Aurum Analytica (within distribution)
segments.commentary: Sold over 1,48,000 leads in Q4 FY26 (+93% YoY) to 145 active clients across 275 signed projects; active accounts +23% and projects +20% YoY. Later answer cited 1,20,000 leads, an inconsistent figure.

segments.name: Sell.do (within distribution)
segments.commentary: 916 active accounts (+38% YoY) and 10,378 active licenses (+32% YoY) at Q4 end; 40+ new developers and 600+ new licenses added in the quarter.

segments.name: HelloWorld (rental)
segments.commentary: 259 active co-living properties (+13% YoY) and 19,286 beds under management (+9% YoY). Management says HelloWorld reached adjusted EBITDA break-even in the current month.

segments.name: NestAway (rental)
segments.commentary: About 9,600 rentable units across 5,214 houses at Q4 end; house count declined YoY after portfolio rationalisation. NestAway Select premium cluster model launched in Q4. Management targets rental profitability in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management said it could not give forward-looking statements but expects growth of about 40% YoY to continue over the next three years, citing a 40% revenue CAGR since inception.
Sale of buildings expected to retire all lease rental discounting debt in full by June 30, 2026; surplus cash to fund AI initiatives over the next couple of years.
Company expects to cross INR 1,000 crores annualised revenue in coming quarters (current run-rate cited at around INR 500 crores).
Rental profitability trends expected to emerge in FY27; HelloWorld already at adjusted EBITDA break-even.
Management expects higher adjusted EBITDA and PBT margins in coming quarters from AI-driven automation; revenue per team member to be tracked as the key AI metric.
SM REIT (commercial, pre-leased Grade A assets) targeted for launch within FY27 across Mumbai, Pune, Delhi NCR, Bangalore and Ahmedabad.
capex_capacity: Sale of buildings: partial sale recognised INR 17.72 crores other income; Q5 and Q6 buildings sale is expected to clear lease rental discounting debt by June 30, 2026.
Rental portfolio: about 30,000 beds under management across HelloWorld and NestAway combined; growth planned via beds and higher-value rental revenue streams.
NestAway Select (premium cluster-based rental) launched in Q4 FY26 in high-demand micro-markets.
SM REIT pipeline being built; pre-leased commercial assets under evaluation, with detailed due diligence pending.
Win a Pin Code strategy: supply concentrated in pin codes with robust momentum for student living, co-living and family rentals.
demand_pricing: PropTiger shifting from transaction model to mandate (exclusive) model; management says mandates carry higher gross commission and margins than standard brokerage.
Distribution segment (PropTiger, Analytica, Sell.do) contributes around 60% of total income, per management.
Cross-sell: about 22% of the distribution network uses multiple products; management says ecosystem cross-sell revenue is still in single digits as a share of revenue and is now being tracked.
Management cited a addressable industry spend of INR 38,000 crores by developers in top eight cities on lead generation, aggregators and transaction management.
Rental demand headwinds in IT cities: Pune weaker (BPO-dependent), Bangalore relatively resilient; management says quality pin code selection offsets this.

qa_highlights.question: How will AI be implemented, and what are the capital allocation priorities after the building sale?
qa_highlights.answer: AI split into business value optimisation (mapping rental, distribution and capital processes, with revenue per team member as the guiding metric) and a longer-term Unified Brain agentic layer on top of existing LLMs. Surplus proceeds after debt retirement will fund AI over the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions planned, given PE/VC-backed peers may be divesting?
qa_highlights.answer: No active acquisition pipeline; management will only pursue deals that sit between two existing operating businesses. PropTiger was the example. Focus is organic growth plus SM REIT.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY26 growth organic, and how will rental and distribution grow given IT hiring slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution growth was partly inorganic via PropTiger (transaction concluded in Q2 FY26). Management sees rental growth from HelloWorld and NestAway via Win a Pin Code, and says distribution gains from developer lead-gen spend during slow sales cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NestAway house count decline YoY while the model is asset-light?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the decline to deliberate rationalisation and consolidation of houses; revenue rose due to value-added services at pin-code level. Rental profitability targeted for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SM REIT timeline and focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on commercial pre-leased Grade A assets given SEBI rules; pipeline being built with channel partners; launch targeted within FY27 subject to due diligence.

qa_highlights.question: How are AI benefits measured versus operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Performance metrics (conversion, connection rates, time to go live) to be tracked over a few quarters, with revenue per employee as the net metric. Employee count excludes outsourced staff and interns.

qa_highlights.question: What are PAT margin prospects by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution consistently profitable with 22-25% margins; rental still takes time due to NestAway platform, tech and go-to-market spend. HelloWorld near adjusted EBITDA break-even.

risks_watch: Continuing-operations PBT was only INR 1.85 crores in Q4 and the rental segment is loss-making (Q4 loss INR 3.61 crores); profitability depends on rental turning positive in FY27.
NestAway house count fell YoY; management's rationalisation claim needs confirmation in next quarter's unit numbers.
Rental demand exposure to IT and BPO hiring slowdown, especially in Pune; management concedes a dip in demand.
AI benefits unquantified: revenue per team member is the only stated net metric and will be tracked from the next quarters.
Capital segment revenue fell sharply in FY26 (INR 7.84 crores vs INR 15.94 crores).
Distribution revenue depends on developer sales cycles and the PropTiger mandate pipeline; cross-sell still single digit as a share of revenue.
Verify the building sale and June 30, 2026 debt retirement, and the SM REIT launch timing.
key_quotes: First, we are now a profitable company. And we believe this is not cyclical; we are structurally profitable.
The sale of buildings Q5 and Q6 will ensure that we retire all lease rental discounting debt in full by June 30, 2026.

Nishita, we are not allowed to give forward -looking statements, but if you look at the last 4 years right from inception of Aurum PropTech and our PropTech business model, we've consistently delivered a growth of 40% year-on-year from a revenue standpoint.
Those numbers are still in single digit, and that is one focus that we have this year, to start evaluating internally that how much of the revenue is coming as a cross-sell revenue.
539289|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, debt retirement and AI, with management repeatedly calling Q4 an inflection point. Cautious and evasive on forward numbers: it declined to give forward-looking statements, gave no quantified AI outcomes, and conceded rental demand weakness in Pune and single-digit cross-sell revenue.

rows.why: Management expects higher adjusted EBITDA and PBT margins from AI automation, distribution runs at 22-25% segment margins, and HelloWorld reached adjusted EBITDA break-even, though Q4 PBT was only INR 1.85 crores on INR 123.85 crores revenue.

539289|2026-06.headline: Aurum PropTech Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 70.9% YoY to INR 111.84 crore and PBT turned positive at INR 2.31 crore, with Housing.com acquisition announced.
539289|2026-06.overview: Aurum PropTech reported its third consecutive profitable quarter, with revenue from operations of INR 111.84 crore (up 70.9% YoY but down from INR 123.85 crore QoQ) and PBT of INR 2.31 crore (2.1% margin). Management said PBT margins expanded 1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margins 1,320 bps YoY. The quarter also featured the announced acquisition of Housing.com, which management says is loss-making and targeted to reach profitability in four to six quarters; the company guided to a burn of about INR 200 crore annualised at Housing. Management also said the INR 112 crore sale of a building closed during the quarter, contributing INR 52.38 crore of other income from discontinued operations.

segments.name: Distribution (developer and distribution)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 55.94 crore, down from INR 66.87 crore QoQ; segment profit INR 7.97 crore. Platform serves over 1,200 developers across 1,50,000 projects in 40+ cities.

segments.name: Capital
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1.55 crore, down from INR 4.28 crore QoQ; segment loss of INR 0.05 crore.

segments.name: Discontinued operations (building sale)
segments.commentary: Building sold for INR 112 crore; other income from discontinued operations INR 52.38 crore in the quarter (INR 17.78 crore in previous quarter). Discontinued-operations PBT INR 52.40 crore.

Management expects Housing.com burn of about INR 200 crore annualised as-is; cost streamlining targeted post-closing.

demand_pricing: Housing.com holds about 24% of India's online portal market; online portals capture about INR 1,200 crore of an estimated INR 38,000 crore annual property marketing and mortgage spend (less than 5% penetration).
Housing.com has 58 million average monthly visits and 12 million monthly active users on the app.

PropTiger brokerage is slab-based on annual gross transaction targets with developers; Q1 seasonally lower as slabs unlock in second half of the year.
Management cited marketplaces valued at 4.5x revenue in India and 10x in another marketplace; says Aurum acquired Housing at about 1.5x revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is there cannibalisation risk between Housing.com organic listings and Aurum Analytica paid lead generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no cannibalisation and views Housing as adding an end-to-end vertical from listings to advertising, lead generation and transactions.

qa_highlights.question: Where will Housing.com market share go over the next two to three years and what tax rate should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to upsell more SKUs within the Housing cohort and extend into transactions; tax structure evaluation is ongoing, with positions to be given in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics and loss at Housing.com and what are the priority fixes?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: monetise intent via transactions, increase utilisation of under-used Housing SKUs, ancillary cross-selling, cut top-heavy corporate costs, streamline sales team and marketing spend (Meta, Google). Target four to six quarters to break-even.

qa_highlights.question: What is Housing.com's FY26 loss and burn, and how does it compare with 99acres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Housing's current burn is about INR 200 crore annualised; FY26 numbers still under audit and to be shared later. It argued listing-only models carry losses and the transaction layer is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: How will dilution and ecosystem cross-selling be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Deora said the REA stake (24.9% post-deal) brings strategic value; Housing adds the top of the funnel for cross-selling to PropTiger, KuberX and Analytica. No numerical cross-sell metric was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be profitable at company level within two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees potential for company-level profitability as existing businesses are profitable, but will guide after the Housing deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Shrikant Jagtap said a PropTiger revenue category crystallised on target-slab achievement in Q4 FY26; slabs unlock mainly in the second half, so the drop is seasonal rather than one-time.

539289|2026-09.headline: Aurum PropTech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 64% YoY to INR 130.2 crores, with EBITDA margin at 29.8% and a return to profit from continuing operations.

539300|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 92.32% YoY to INR197.59 crore and PAT rose 87.89% to INR12.10 crore; management targets INR1,000 crore revenue by FY28.

For FY26, revenue rose 237.34% to INR607.75 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 9.66% from 14.24% and PAT margin to 5.76% from 6.11%, which management attributed to product mix. Management reiterated an INR1,000 crore revenue aspiration by FY28 and an internal 7% PAT margin target.

539300|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 8.18% on raw-material and crude-linked cost pressure.
539300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR276.33 crores, up 120.64% YoY and 39.85% QoQ, with PAT of INR15.04 crores (up 130.67% YoY). EBITDA rose 94.41% YoY to INR22.59 crores, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 9.28% a year earlier and 10.19% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the margin squeeze to dyes, chemicals, boiler fuel, LABSA and PP packaging costs linked to geopolitical crude volatility, which hit the textile business hardest. Installed FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity rose to 20,840 tons per month after a 1,700 MT soap line was commissioned at Roorkee. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR900-1,000 crores and a ~6% profitability level, with a further 0.75-1% improvement in FY28.

539301|2026-03.headline: FY26 bookings hit record INR1,550 crore (+22% YoY) while FY26 revenue fell to INR564 crore from INR713 crore on revenue-recognition timing.

Full-year revenue declined to INR564 crore from INR713 crore, which management attributed to timing of revenue recognition and occupation certificates slipping into FY27, while adjusted EBITDA fell to INR156 crore and PAT to INR103 crore. Q4 PAT rose 103% YoY to INR44 crore on revenue of INR155 crore. Business development added projects worth INR3,140 crore in FY26, and a further INR2,400 crore Mumbai high-rise was signed after year-end.

qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that about 3 years is a fair assumption for launched inventory, while overall portfolio monetisation is 4-5 years.

539301|2026-06.headline: Arvind SmartSpaces Q1 FY27 presales rose 147% YoY to INR432 crores; PAT jumped to INR97 crores on Orchards Phase 1 BU receipt.
539301|2026-06.overview: Presales of INR432 crores grew 147% YoY, with management attributing it to both Aqua City demand and broader core-market strength. Revenue rose to INR318 crores from INR102 crores and adjusted EBITDA to INR150 crores from INR25 crores, mainly from Orchards Phase 1 in Bengaluru receiving BU. Collections grew 76% to INR336 crores and net operating cash flow was INR81 crores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 35-40% bookings growth, INR4,000-5,000 crores BD and 22-25% EBITDA margin on new sales, and India Ratings upgraded the company to AA- (stable).

segments.name: Ahmedabad (Aqua City, horizontal)
segments.commentary: Aqua City named as standout booking performer in Q1; new Vastrapur project planned for launch this year. Management cites leadership in horizontal development in Ahmedabad.

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Orchards Phase 1 BU received, driving the quarter's revenue and profit step-up; Bengaluru stock close to INR3,000 crores. Three launches planned this year, including Sarjapur, which has approvals.

segments.name: Mumbai / MMR
segments.commentary: Mumbai stock of INR4,000 crores-plus GDV; two Goregaon redevelopment-related and BD additions. Goregaon saleable carpet area about 6.7 lakh sq ft, 35-floor-plus, about 4 years to complete; 2 Mumbai launches planned this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bookings growth of 35-40% over FY26, implying about INR2,100-2,200 crores (per Q&A).
FY27 business development of INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV; INR2,600 crores already added in Q1; management leaning to upper band.
EBITDA margin on new sales of 22-25%; management says portfolio average about 25%, JD projects at lower end and outright at higher end.
FY27 operating cash flow target of INR400-500 crores (FY26 about INR400 crores).
Launch pipeline of about INR3,000-3,500 crores booking value across 6 projects (Ahmedabad 1, Bengaluru 3, Mumbai 2) this year.
Land outflow for FY27 of about INR600-900 crores (Q&A), with 4-5 year realisation of INR5,100 crores operating cash flow from existing portfolio.
Management did not give revenue guidance; expects strong YoY growth in FY27 revenue but timing depends on OC receipts, some lined up in Q4.
Medium-term 25-30% CAGR target over 4-5 years; comfort debt-to-equity at 1:1.
capex_capacity: Unrecognised revenue of INR3,825 crores to be recognised over about 4 years: plotted projects 2-3 years, high-rise OC in about 4 years.
Existing portfolio operating cash flow of over INR5,100 crores expected over next 4-5 years.
Construction spend ramped up in Q1; management says larger incremental outflow is construction cost.
Goregaon redevelopment: 200-plus units to be handed to existing members; area for members not yet disclosed.
Pen Khopoli project in Mumbai awaiting approvals; company hopes to launch at least 2 of 3 Mumbai projects this year.
demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand is strong; Aqua City plus broader core-market strength drove bookings.
Sustenance sales improved through sales team build-out across 3 cities, channel partner and marketing reach; sustenance may exceed plan.
Price increases expected to moderate after 3-4 years of strong appreciation; company does not underwrite large price hikes.
Bengaluru price uplift giving better margins on some older projects.
Management sees Mumbai, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad each delivering 22-25% EBITDA; no Tier 2 plans for now.
Management sees annual residential absorption of INR3-4 lakh crores across the three focus markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is Aqua City-driven booking strength project-specific or indicative of underlying demand in Gujarat and Bengaluru?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination of both; the market is strong and stable and responding well to most projects, and underlying demand remains quite strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unrecognised revenue conversion and normalised margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 margin was boosted by Orchards BU; the 25% portfolio average is the base case. Revenue recognition is OC-linked and lumpy, so no annual revenue guidance is given.

qa_highlights.question: How is OCF flattening and what is FY27 OCF guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 OCF was about INR400 crores; FY27 target INR400-500 crores. Q1 OCF of INR81 crores reflects higher construction outflow, which management views as positive catch-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and leverage comfort level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to equity at 0.29x; management comfortable up to 1:1 and expects gradual debt increase, funded by OCF and debt lines.

qa_highlights.question: How will BD of INR600-1,000 crores be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores from operating cash flow plus debt headroom; BD cash deployment guided at INR600-1,000 crores in the year (land outflow INR600-900 crores per earlier answer).

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for an annuity or commercial portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Not today; management is considering it after a few years, starting with for-sale assets to test development before holding assets.

risks_watch: Revenue and margin are lumpy and dependent on OC timing, with some OCs lined up in Q4; the Q1 margin of about 48-49% is well above the 25% portfolio average.
Net debt to equity rising from prior level to 0.29x as BD accelerates; management's comfort threshold is 1:1.
Launch execution: 6 launches worth INR3,000-3,500 crores this year depend on approvals, including Pen Khopoli.
Labour and construction cost inflation is gradual per management but may pressure margins.
Guidance inconsistency: BD cash deployment quoted as INR600-900 crores in one answer and INR600-1,000 crores in another.

539301|2026-09.headline: Arvind SmartSpaces raised FY27 bookings guidance to INR2,600-2,700 crore (70-75% YoY) after Q2 bookings of INR906 crore, more than double YoY.
539301|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 presales hit a record INR906 crore (vs INR432 crore in Q2 FY26), and H1 bookings reached INR1,338 crore, up 120% YoY. Revenue was INR475 crore for H1 (up 96%) and INR157 crore in Q2; H1 PAT was INR120 crore (about 4x) and Q2 PAT INR23 crore (up 25%). Management raised FY27 bookings guidance from INR2,100-2,200 crore to INR2,600-2,700 crore, kept the 22-25% EBITDA margin guidance, and signalled a strong likelihood of the upper end of the INR4,000-5,000 crore GDV addition guidance. Net debt fell to INR200 crore from INR215 crore in the quarter.

segments.commentary: Launched one project in Q2; contributed about 70% of sales last year. Existing Gujarat projects contribute through sustenance sales.

segments.name: Mumbai (MMR)

539302|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR 2,121 crore, while FY26 order inflow of ~INR 7,210 crore missed the INR 10,000 crore target by about 28%.
539302|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 2,121 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 237 crore (+2% YoY, margin 11.17%) and PAT of INR 153 crore (+18%). FY26 revenue was INR 6,107 crore (+16%), EBITDA INR 750 crore (12.3% margin) and PAT INR 412 crore (+18%). Order inflow missed guidance after cancellation of a INR 1,563 crore BESS order by the West Bengal electricity department, and the water division faced certification delays. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, order inflow of about INR 12,000 crore and EBITDA margin of about 12.5%.

segments.name: Power vs non-power mix
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 57% power and 43% non-power; FY26 was 64% power and 36% non-power. Backlog is about 70% power and 30% non-power.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 94% domestic and 6% international; FY26 was 95% domestic and 5% international. International work is mainly O&M and manpower supply (Middle East, Nigeria), with international revenue of INR 327 crore in FY26 versus INR 292 crore in FY25.

segments.name: MDO (mining, KBP and SAIL/Tasra)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 MDO revenue was INR 226 crore, including INR 117 crore in March. Management targets INR 500 crore in FY27 and INR 1,250 crore in FY28, with EBITDA margin of about 15% now rising toward 20% at peak rated capacity (FY29-30).

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M is the highest-margin business at about 15-16% EBITDA. Management cites O&M order growth of about 8% and about 4,100 MW of O&M orders in FY26, including a INR 279 crore Mumbai Monorail/metro O&M contract.

segments.name: EPC / civil
segments.commentary: Construction margins are below 8-10%. The BOP EPC order for the 800 MW Singareni project from BHEL is about INR 2,550 crore. Electrical transmission work has ended and was moved into civil.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, which management says it is confident of achieving.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR 12,000 crore, mainly BOP EPC and O&M; FY28 target INR 12,000-15,000 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% including other income, up 0.25-0.3 percentage points.
MDO revenue targets: about INR 500 crore in FY27 (KBP INR 350 crore, Tasra/SAIL INR 150 crore), INR 1,250 crore in FY28, and about INR 2,100-2,200 crore at full capacity in FY29-30.
Blended EBITDA is guided to rise about 0.5% a year to 14% by FY30 and about 14.25% in FY31.
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore at Power Mech level (washery) and about INR 400 crore at the Tasra SPV, without debt.
capex_capacity: KBP mine (Kurmitar area) began production in November 2025; the client is lifting above contract capacity, and FY26 offtake was about 1.6 million tonnes.
Tasra washery construction should finish by December 2026, with washed coal from Q4 FY27 and Tasra production from mid Q4 FY27. Management says the Tasra ramp-up reaches peak rated capacity in FY29.
Target full capacity: KBP about 5 million tonnes by FY30; SAIL/Tasra about 4 million tonnes by FY29.
Current metro O&M covers about 1,095 operational km in India, expected to reach 2,000 km; Mumbai light rail O&M covers 15 stations.
Annual power commissioning is expected to reach about 8,000 MW a year, which management sees as driving installation, civil and O&M demand.
demand_pricing: Management identified about INR 70,000 crore of opportunities for FY27 across power, non-power, metro O&M and EPC. Its past bidding is about INR 40,000-50,000 crore at a hit ratio of about 15%.
BOP opportunities worth about INR 15,000 crore are being bid for 2-3 projects, with a target of one more BOP win in FY27.
Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages; management says BHEL is changing its packaging approach.
Named opportunities: BALCO O&M about INR 1,500 crore, Butibori O&M about INR 700 crore, and NMDC EPC tenders worth about INR 8,000-10,000 crore with Thyssenkrupp as partner.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value remains, with about INR 128 crore of work awaiting certification and INR 90 crore receivable. Management has stopped new water bids.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 10,000 crore order target missed, and is FY27 better?
qa_highlights.answer: The miss was mainly the INR 1,563 crore West Bengal BESS cancellation. Management expects West Bengal to re-tender, and says Bangalore Metro and Monorail (L1 in April) support about INR 10,000 crore; FY27 target is INR 12,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook given water division delays and labour code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 EBITDA of about 12.5%, up 0.25-0.3 points, helped by more O&M and EPC mix. The Labour Code gratuity provision in Q4 was about INR 4.5 crore for the full-year impact.

qa_highlights.question: Do escalation clauses protect margins against commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic contracts carry PVC/escalation clauses that are billed to clients. International business is mainly O&M manpower, so impact is limited; the 1.2-1.5% of international order book is largely O&M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDO FY28 cut from INR 1,800-1,900 crore to INR 1,250 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The KBP washery is not ready on the CCL side, so offtake is conservatively put at INR 350 crore in FY27. The SAIL/Tasra ramp from zero to 4 million tonnes in one year is treated as a challenge, so FY28 is INR 750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDO margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin is about 15% at present, and management expects about 1 percentage point a year, reaching 20%-21% at peak rated capacity around FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Are there labour shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is above 40,000, with 70-75% in labour roles and about 18,000 in O&M. Management says construction and installation labour is the constraint, but schedules have been met so far.

risks_watch: Order inflow execution: FY26 missed by about 28%, and the FY27 target of INR 12,000 crore depends on BOP wins against BHEL's changed packaging approach and pricing.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value is stalled pending central and state fund release, and certification delays weigh on margins.
MDO ramp-up: KBP and Tasra volumes depend on client offtake, the CCL washery, and the rainy season. The FY27 MDO target (INR 500 crore) is well above the Q4 monthly run-rate once March is excluded.
Commodity and labour inflation: steel, cement and diesel prices have risen. Recovery relies on PVC clauses, and labour availability is a constraint.
Management's 1-point-a-year margin expansion in MDO and blended EBITDA targets rest on O&M and EPC mix shifts.
539302|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and bullish on long-term power and O&M demand, but cautious on near-term order inflow and the water division. Management was explicit about the BESS cancellation and the MDO timing shortfall, and gave specific numbers on most questions. Some answers on segment figures and MDO revenue were revised during the call, which weakens the precision of the guidance.
key_quotes: Otherwise, our numbers would have been much better in order backlog.
Of course, on the BOP side, we are going to bid for two- three projects, that's worth INR 15000 crores.
We are confident of achieving that, and even the MDO business ramp -up of production is happening, and we are more focused on the high -margin O&M business.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% incl. other income, up 0.25-0.3 pts from 12.3% in FY26, helped by O&M and EPC mix, with MDO margin (about 15%) expected to rise about 1 pt a year toward 20-21% at peak capacity.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Tasra washery done Dec 2026; washed coal from Q4 FY27; Tasra
rows.why: KBP mine already producing since Nov 2025 (FY26 offtake ~1.6 Mt vs target ~5 Mt by FY30) and Tasra washery (INR 400 cr capex) is under construction, with ~4 Mt targeted by FY29; ramp is conditional on client offtake and CCL washery readiness.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 21% on FY26 revenue of INR 6,107 cr, with MDO revenue targeted at INR 500 cr in FY27 vs INR 226 cr in Q4 FY26 alone (of which INR 117 cr in March), though the FY27 MDO target looks stretched.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Only committed capex is INR 400 cr at Power Mech (washery) plus INR 400 cr at Tasra SPV, both debt-free; no utilisation figure is given, and no new plant or line has been announced, so a fresh capex round is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 order inflow missed the INR 10,000 cr target by about 28% (INR 7,210 cr), and FY27 order target of INR 12,000 cr depends on one more BOP win and re-tender of the cancelled INR 1,563 cr West Bengal BESS order.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: MDO FY28 target was already cut from INR 1,800-1,900 cr to INR 1,250 cr, FY27 MDO target of INR 500 cr is well above the Q4 run-rate ex-March, water division has ~INR 900 cr stalled with INR 128 cr awaiting certification, and FY26 orders missed by ~28%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed; the only new business lines are MDO ramp-ups already in motion.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow target INR 12,000 cr
rows.why: FY26 inflow was ~INR 7,210 cr (72% of target); FY27 needs BOP wins (~INR 15,000 cr BOP opportunities in 2-3 bids, target one more win), plus Bangalore Metro/Monorail (~INR 10,000 cr, L1 in April) and possible West Bengal re-tender.

rows.label: Water division stall
rows.why: About INR 900 cr contract value stalled pending central/state fund release, INR 128 cr awaiting certification and INR 90 cr receivable; management has stopped new water bids, so this drag persists.

rows.label: BHEL package pricing
rows.why: Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages and BHEL is changing its packaging approach; the 800 MW Singareni BOP (~INR 2,550 cr) and NMDC EPC (INR 8,000-10,000 cr with Thyssenkrupp) hinge on this.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 21% revenue growth, 12.5% margin and long-term power/O&M demand, but cautious on order inflow, water division and MDO timing; analysts pressed on the order miss, MDO FY28 cut and margin path, and some segment figures were revised during the call.

539332|2026-09.headline: JSW Infrastructure Q2 FY27 consolidated operating revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore, but PAT fell to INR328 crore on forex loss and Fujairah shutdown.
539332|2026-09.overview: Consolidated operating revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR1,481 crore (up 17% YoY) and operating EBITDA was INR674 crore (up 11%), while PAT declined to INR328 crore from INR369 crore. Port volumes grew only 2% YoY to 29.4 million tonnes, with the India business up 8% and Fujairah contributing nothing. Logistics EBITDA rose to INR81 crore from INR25 crore as the rake fleet grew from 42 to 78, and management cut the FY27 logistics margin guidance to 28% from 24% while keeping the INR400 crore EBITDA target. Management reiterated the consolidated FY27 EBITDA range of INR2,950-3,000 crore, though the port component was trimmed.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR463 crore a year ago

segments.name: Ports
segments.commentary: Q2 volumes 29.4 Mt (+2% YoY); India ops +8%, third-party volumes 45% of total. Fujairah contributed nil volume and an EBITDA loss of about INR16 crore in H1; port EBITDA margin fell to 49.4% from 53.1%.

segments.name: Logistics
segments.commentary: Domestic cargo 459,000 MT (+16% YoY); EXIM 88,000 TEUs (+12%). EBITDA INR81 crore (3.3x YoY). H1 logistics EBITDA was about INR153 crore; FY27 logistics margin guidance raised to 28% from 24% after accounting change netting haulage.

segments.name: Fujairah (international)
segments.commentary: Zero volume contribution in Q2. Eight tanks under commissioning with final FOIS permission expected around 29 October, with operations targeted for early November, but storage demand has fallen sharply.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBITDA target of about INR2,950-3,000 crore: port EBITDA now expected at INR2,550-2,560 crore against earlier INR2,600 crore; logistics EBITDA slightly above INR400 crore.
FY27 logistics EBITDA margin guidance revised to 28% from 24%; FY28 logistics margin guidance unchanged for now, with a revision to be considered in Q3 or Q4.

Rake fleet to rise from 78 to 110 by March 2027 (6 more to be operational in Nov-Dec; 32 more to be delivered in H2). Longer-term rake plan of around 267-270 (157 container, 110 LSFTO) is fluid and may rise.
FY27 capex expected at INR5,000-6,000 crore; overall FY27-28 capex guidance of INR16,500 crore retained. Cumulative capex about INR8,250 crore plus INR6,000 crore committed.
Port capacity target of 300 Mtpa by FY28 and 400 Mtpa by FY30 unchanged. Oman, Murbe work expected to start Q4 FY27; Keni awaits environment clearance (3-4 months more).
Q3 volume: H2 domestic cargo growth expected at 8-10% YoY; Jaigarh plus Dharamtar expected to handle about 46 Mt in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What was rail rake revenue in Q2 and H1, and what is the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the overall logistics EBITDA margin is around 28% and the rake business margin around 90%, since only premium and rebate are booked as revenue with haulage netted off. Vishesh Pachnanda pointed to a logistics revenue of about INR279 crore, of which Navkar revenue was INR223 crore, with the balance being rail freight.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income rise sharply QoQ, and how is H1 capex tracking versus FY27 plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income rose due to interest on QIP proceeds. H1 FY27 capex was about INR2,100 crore against expected FY27 spend of INR5,000-6,000 crore; committed capex including INR6,000 crore of orders takes the total to about INR14,250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Ports EBITDA margins suppressed beyond Fujairah?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said terminal volumes carry 30-35% margins, and a dip at Jaigarh lowered the overall margin; a Jaigarh pickup is expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fujairah status and when can volumes resume?
qa_highlights.answer: Eight tanks are in commissioning, with FOIS final permission expected around 29 October and operations targeted for the first week of November. Management flagged that storage demand in the area has fallen substantially because ships are not calling.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on Oman, Murbe and Keni, and are there delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Oman tenders were floated with bids expected mid-November and work to start in Q4 FY27; Murbe land acquisition is underway with work also expected Q4 FY27. Keni has been delayed on environment clearance: KCZMA recommended the proposal to MoEFCC, with 3-4 months more expected for EC.

qa_highlights.question: Can Jatadhar expand beyond 30 Mt and what is the cargo start timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Jatadhar has about 3.5 km of waterfront permission with 690 m in current development for 30 Mt; EC covers 52 Mt, and management sees potential to 100-120 Mt with more machinery. Cargo handling is expected to start around end-March 2027 or April 2027, with Cape-size facilities in Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was logistics revenue guidance cut and can FY27 logistics targets be met?
qa_highlights.answer: The revenue cut reflects netting off haulage, while the EBITDA target of INR400 crore is kept; the rakes added by Q2 end give full H2 availability, which management said gives confidence. FY28 logistics margin guidance is unchanged for now, with a review in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA bridge and how are Jaigarh LPG delays explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Port EBITDA is now expected at INR2,550-2,560 crore against INR2,600 crore earlier, with logistics slightly above INR400 crore, for a total of INR2,950-3,000 crore. Jaigarh LPG marine works start by March 2027, while tankage was delayed by a change in planning authority and is now approved, with tanks around Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What were Fujairah EBITDA contributions and what is the insurance claim status?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY26 Fujairah EBITDA was about INR134 crore and full-year FY26 about INR250 crore; H1 FY27 showed a loss of about INR16 crore. Insurance claims are still under assessment, pending a state declaration on whether the event is a war.

capex_capacity: Cumulative capex about INR8,250 crore up to September 2026, including INR1,500 crore spent in Q2; H1 FY27 capex about INR2,100 crore.
FY27 capex expected at INR5,000-6,000 crore; FY27-28 capex guidance of INR16,500 crore retained, with about INR6,000 crore committed via orders and about INR950 crore outstanding capex creditors.

Port capacity target of 186 Mtpa currently, 300 Mtpa by FY28 and 400 Mtpa by FY30. Oman tender bids due mid-November, work expected to start Q4 FY27; Murbe land acquisition and tenders done, work expected Q4 FY27; Keni awaits EC, 3-4 months more.

Slurry pipeline about 88% complete (257 km lowered, 10 km HDD in progress), commissioning on schedule by March 2027. Jatadhar berths ready for cargo by March 2027 (Panamax), Cape-size facilities Q3 FY28; Jatadhar EC covers 52 Mt, 690 m waterfront supports 30 Mt in phase 1.

Rake fleet 78 now, 72 operational since October, 6 more in Nov-Dec, 32 more in H2 to reach 110 by March 2027. Long-term rake plan of around 267-270 (157 container, 110 LSFTO) described as fluid and likely to rise.

Jaigarh LPG: marine operations by March 2027; tankage delayed by change in planning authority, now approved, with 2 large tanks expected by around Q3 FY28. Dharamtar mechanisation to complete Q4 FY27; Jaigarh mechanisation Q1 FY28. Kolkata OCT (13 Mtpa) concession signed; Kolkata interim operations at 6.3 Mtpa terminal began in Q2.
demand_pricing: Q2 port volumes 29.4 Mt (+2% YoY); India operations +8% in Q2 and +10% in H1; third-party volumes 45% of total in Q2 and third-party in India +13% YoY in Q2.
Q2 domestic logistics cargo 459,000 MT (+16% YoY); EXIM 88,000 TEUs (+12% YoY); H1 domestic cargo +26% YoY and EXIM +7% YoY.
Port revenue INR1,202 crore (+9% YoY), port EBITDA margin 49.4% vs 53.1%, attributed to Fujairah absence and lower-margin coal terminal volumes (Paradip Coal, Ennore Bulk, Mangalore, Tuticorin).
Paradip iron ore volumes fell after a 22 August vessel sinking off Paradip led to moisture-limit restrictions; about 8 lakh tonnes stock built up by end-September before shipments resumed.
H2 domestic cargo growth guided at 8-10% YoY; Jaigarh plus Dharamtar expected at about 46 Mt in FY27; Fujairah storage demand has fallen sharply as ships are not calling.

Logistics margin: rake business margin about 90% on premium and rebate only, with haulage netted off; FY27 logistics EBITDA margin guidance revised to 28% from 24%, EBITDA target INR400 crore retained.
risks_watch: Fujairah: 8 tanks targeted to start in early November, but storage demand has fallen sharply and operations may stay constrained; insurance claim pending.
FY27 EBITDA target of INR2,950-3,000 crore requires a steep H2 ramp in logistics with 32 rakes still to be delivered in H2 and 6 more in Nov-Dec.
Keni environment clearance expected in 3-4 months; Oman and Murbe work start in Q4 FY27 depends on bids and land acquisition; port capacity 300 Mtpa by FY28 at risk.
Jatadhar Cape-size facilities not until Q3 FY28; Jaigarh LPG tankage delayed; Jaigarh volumes soft in Q2.
Forex losses on rupee depreciation and higher finance cost and depreciation; finance cost in H2 may rise from ROU lease expense on rakes.
Q3 FY27 results: watch the FY28 logistics margin revision, the rake fleet progress against 110, and Paradip iron ore and Kolkata terminal volumes.
key_quotes: Despite these uncertainties, India's economic fundamentals remain strong, supported by robust domestic demand, continued investments in infrastructure, manufacturing-led growth and favorable policy initiatives.

In the short-term, in the immediate-term, the strategy is to get the 8 terminals, as I told you, which are currently under testing to get them official commissioning done and start operations by November 1st week.
Long-term prospects, extremely bullish, but immediate prospects, we have to wait and watch.
So from a logistics perspective, we are confident that we should be in a position to achieve slightly above INR400 crores in terms of EBITDA.
539332|2026-09.management_tone: Management was confident on the India port and logistics ramp-up and on the FY27 EBITDA range, but cautious on Fujairah, describing the situation as fluid and the immediate demand outlook as wait-and-watch. Answers on Keni timing and Jaigarh tankage were direct about delays.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: H1 FY27 capex was about INR2,100 crore against FY27 guidance of INR5,000-6,000 crore, and the INR16,500 crore FY27-28 plan was held, so further capex and project awards are expected, with Oman and Murbe work starting Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Consolidated FY27 EBITDA was held at INR2,950-3,000 crore with port trimmed, and Fujairah is still at zero volume, so no raise is signalled.

rows.why: Eight tanks are in commissioning with FOIS permission expected around 29 October and operations targeted for early November, but H1 FY27 EBITDA was a loss of about INR16 crore versus about INR134 crore in H1 FY26 because ships are not calling.

rows.why: Capacity goes from 186 Mtpa to 300 Mtpa, with about INR6,000 crore committed via orders, but Keni still awaits environment clearance (3-4 months more) and Oman and Murbe work starts only in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Logistics margin reset to 28%
rows.why: The FY27 logistics EBITDA margin guidance was raised to 28% from 24% after netting haulage, with Q2 logistics EBITDA up to INR81 crore from INR25 crore and a margin of 29%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the India port and rake ramp-up and on the INR2,950-3,000 crore FY27 EBITDA range, but cautious on Fujairah with storage demand down sharply; analysts pushed on rake revenue and margin, capex pacing, Fujairah status and Keni and Jaigarh delays.

539334|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 21.1% to Rs 976.6 crore, but Unit 5/6 commissioning is stalled by raw-material price spikes, with FY27 revenue guided to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore.
539334|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 976.6 crore (+21.1%), EBITDA Rs 99.5 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT Rs 70.1 crore (7.1% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 218 crore with EBITDA Rs 22.1 crore and PAT Rs 12.9 crore, held back by raw-material availability. Management said it deliberately stopped dispatches in the second week of March 2026 as ammonia and sulphur prices roughly tripled, and new Unit 5 and Unit 6 capacity has not been commissioned. Management lowered its FY27 revenue visibility to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 72,423 MT (+27.9%) for Rs 531.8 crore, with segment revenue up 25.2%. Q4 FY26 sales 13,725 MT (+36% YoY) for Rs 126.4 crore. Management cited H Acid at about Rs 750/kg (from Rs 525-530/kg) and Vinyl Sulphone at about Rs 350/kg (from Rs 240/kg).

segments.name: Fertilisers
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 252,777 MT for Rs 444.8 crore, with segment revenue up 16.5%. Q4 FY26 sales 50,500 MT for Rs 91.8 crore. Management said NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but is still not sufficient for current raw-material costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue visibility lowered to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore, assuming about Rs 1,000 crore from existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore from Rabi season; no benefit from higher current prices assumed.
Kharif FY27 season expected to contribute no revenue from Unit 5 or Unit 6; start of trial production under evaluation, with management saying it could start within about one month.
Q1 FY27 expected to benefit from liquidating inventory held back in Q4; management said PAT should be about 8-8.5% of revenue and Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore, without firm numbers.
Normal tax rate guided at 22-25% for FY27, with deferred tax expected to rise significantly as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar capitalise.
Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable, while noting that sulphur may settle at about Rs 70-75/kg rather than the earlier Rs 30-35/kg.
capex_capacity: Total planned capex Rs 512 crore; Rs 189 crore incurred as of 31 March 2026, funded by internal accruals and preferential allotment.

Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 are mechanically ready; Unit 6 about 90-95% complete. Commissioning delayed by electricity issues (resolved in March 2026) and raw-material price spikes; no capitalisation yet.
Solar: 1.1 MW DC commissioned at Hisar, Haryana, taking installed capacity to 10.6 MW DC; 10 MW Nanded plant on track, which would take total to 20.6 MW DC.

Planned Rs 350 crore additional facility at Madhya Bharat Phosphates, Meghnagar (Unit 3). About Rs 140 crore sits in AAA-rated bonds, plus Rs 30 crore preferential allotment to promoter; remaining about Rs 180 crore to come from accruals, with possibly 25-30% term loan.
Plant utilisation currently 65-70% per CFO; Unit 1 sulphuric plant was shut for maintenance in Q4.
demand_pricing: Ammonia rose from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg and sulphur from Rs 30/kg to about Rs 100/kg, according to management.
Sulphur rose a further 20% in May 2026 up to 19 May, per management.
Management said demand is weakening as prices rise and that the market is accepting the higher prices for chemicals, though fertiliser acceptability at current prices is uncertain.

Company stopped SSP dispatches in the second week of March 2026 deliberately to avoid selling at the old cost base; management said FY26 revenue would have crossed Rs 1,000 crore if sales had continued for 15 more days.
Management said the company has not factored in the higher current selling prices in its FY27 outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 320-odd crore capex be funded, and what is the maths?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 174 crore and Rs 155 crore phases were funded internally except a Rs 25 crore HDFC solar term loan, and the new Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat project will use about Rs 170 crore of existing bonds and preferential allotment, with the balance from accruals or a possible 25-30% term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-28 outlook for Unit 5 and 6 after the delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the electricity issue was resolved in March 2026 but raw-material price spikes delayed start-up; FY27 revenue is now visualised at Rs 1,250-1,300 crore, with no Kharif contribution from Units 5 and 6.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory benefit flow into Q1 FY27, and can it be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 should be better than recent quarters as held-back Q4 inventory is liquidated, but declined to quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue flat YoY in Q4 despite chemical volumes up over 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not answer on the call and said the company would respond through its IR advisor.

qa_highlights.question: What tax rate should be assumed for FY27?

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.

EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.

Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.

Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.

K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.

Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

539334|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 58.2% YoY to INR403.5 crore and EBITDA 87.7% to INR49.2 crore, helped by China-driven dye intermediate demand.
539334|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR403.5 crore in Q2 FY27, up 58.2% YoY and 44% QoQ, with H1 at INR683.6 crore (+34.1%). EBITDA rose to INR49.2 crore at a 12.2% margin and PAT to INR35.7 crore at an 8.9% margin. Management attributed the gain to China-driven shortages of dye intermediates, Kharif-season volumes and better realisations, and commissioned Unit 5 (about 6,000 TPA dye capacity) and a 10 MW DC solar plant. The board also approved a INR70 crore new chemical plant at Unit 5 (3,000 TPA, commissioning by March 2028) funded partly by a promoter warrant issue.

qa_highlights.answer: Balance warrant money expected before March 2027, against a June 2027 deadline, to fund Madhya Bharat expansion.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY28 revenue should be near INR2,000 crore, with about 10% variation, while FY27 is at least INR1,250 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: NCLT delays made the merger overtaken by events, so management withdrew the application as a conscious decision.

539336|2026-03.headline: Gujarat Energy FY26 EBITDA rose to INR3,772 crore (from INR3,241 crore) while PAT was flat at INR2,299 crore; the merger became effective 1 May 2026.
539336|2026-03.overview: The GSPC/GSPL merger into Gujarat Gas became effective 1 May 2026, with the company renamed Gujarat Energy from 14 May 2026. Q4 FY26 EBITDA was INR943 crore (vs INR790 crore a year earlier), and CNG volume hit a record 3.6 mmscmd. Morbi ceramic demand ramped sharply to about 8 mmscmd after the Middle East conflict constrained propane and LPG supply. Management said FY26 financials are not like-for-like with FY25 because of the demerger and merger accounting, and gave segment EBITDA for the first time on a call. The board recommended a dividend of INR8.90 per share (about INR835 crore outgo).

The company is reviewing options for the 700 MW combined-cycle plant, whose PPA runs to 2036.

qa_highlights.question: Is Morbi volume at a peak, and what is the pricing?

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in gas trading and the segment profit baseline?

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the power business and its outlook?

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage LNG price risk as Morbi volumes grow?

qa_highlights.question: What is the deployment plan for surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has appointed McKinsey to develop a growth and deployment strategy. It expects to share the way forward in the next quarter or a subsequent one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company transfer trading profits to CGD on a cost basis?

539336|2026-06.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
539336|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR9,670 crores (up 63% YoY), EBITDA INR1,482 crores (up 65%) and PAT INR998 crores (up 78%), with total sales volume of 15.66 mmscmd. Gas trading EBT rose 206% to INR726 crores, helped by Brent-linked long-term contracts and a Morbi industrial volume surge during the Middle East-driven propane shortage. Management kept FY27 gas trading profit guidance at about INR1,100 crores (reiterated as INR1,100-1,200 crores in one answer) and CGD EBITDA guidance at INR5.5-6.5/scm, while saying Morbi volumes will likely settle near 3 mmscmd as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources.

segments.name: CGD - CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.76 mmscmd, up 13% from 3.33 mmscmd (Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%). Network at 844 stations after adding 6 and upgrading 9 in the quarter; plans for more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades in FY27.

segments.name: CGD - PNG domestic
segments.commentary: Added about 59,000 domestic PNG customers in the quarter, taking the base above 2.477 million households. Commercial PNG volume was 0.17 mmscmd with more than 16,600 commercial customers.

segments.name: PNG industrial
segments.commentary: Volume 7.17 mmscmd vs 4.71 mmscmd, up 64%. Morbi averaged 5.67 mmscmd and non-Morbi 2.04 mmscmd; non-Morbi realisation about INR70/scm and Morbi about INR78/scm, against propane at about INR65/scm.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Gas-based plants run at very low utilisation: about 6% PLF at the 51 MW GSEG plant and about 1% at Pipavav in Q1, with peak summer demand the only driver.

segments.name: E&P and renewables
segments.commentary: Q1 FY26 EBITDA was INR7 crores (E&P) and INR14 crores (renewables); Q4 FY26 was INR14 crores and INR5 crores. No Q1 FY27 figures were given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current Morbi run-rate and how does pricing compare with propane?

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG growth outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects CNG growth of about 12-13% to be sustained for the next couple of years, supported by more than 75 new stations planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will third-party gas trading volumes recover, and what is the long-term range?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd to about 3.3 mmscmd due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and weak power volumes. Management expects long-term third-party volume of 4.5-5 mmscmd, mainly in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CGD EBITDA position against guidance, and why is it below range?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD EBITDA was about INR5.18/scm, below the INR5.5-6.5/scm guidance, which management attributed to a larger volume base. Management kept the guidance and said it looks at portfolio margins rather than segment-level Morbi margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Morbi industrial volume plans and constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Morbi volume is about 2-2.2 mmscmd; management targets at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise. It cited infrastructure build-out, with about 86 new industries added in April-June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Morbi volume floor and how is the propane terminal funded?

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Q2 CNG volumes 3.67 MMSCMD (+11% YoY); H1 at 3.72 MMSCMD. Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%. 18 stations added in H1, taking the total to 857; target 75+ additions in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

539359|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 36.2% YoY to INR138.46 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.02% on raw material and gas cost spikes.
539359|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue for FY26 reached INR482.95 crore, up 35.32% YoY, with EBITDA of INR71.03 crore (14.71% margin) and PAT of INR23.20 crore. Q4 EBITDA margin dropped to 12.02% from the 16-17% range management cited earlier, which management attributed to raw material, gas, freight and outsourced labour cost increases in March 2026. Management expects margins to recover toward 15-16% if the war-related cost disruption does not worsen, and guided Q1 FY27 revenue at a similar run rate to Q4. Capacity is about 72,000 MTPA with FY26 output of 52,620 MT, and the company plans about 7,800 MT of foundry addition in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Large castings (gearboxes, transmission cases, differential carriers)
segments.commentary: Management calls large castings the main driver of product mix improvement, citing fewer competitors (about 8-10 in India for tractor large castings) and higher value addition.

segments.name: LFC (lost foam casting) via Meeta Casting
segments.commentary: Contributes about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book; management targets 30% in three years. Margin is about 1-2% higher than conventional castings.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Not yet material; product development and qualification ongoing with three to four products developed. Initial contributions expected in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue target of INR600 crore; management says 15% growth for the next two years gets there. Also cited 15% growth for the company against 6-8% expected from customers in FY27.
Margins expected to recover toward 15-16% (EBITDA) if no further war-related disruption; Q1 FY27 revenue expected similar to Q4 FY26.

FY27 capex of about INR25-30 crore, of which about INR35 crore is for the 7,800 MT foundry addition (the figures on the 7,800 MT project were given inconsistently in the call). FY28 LFC project of 2,400 MT, with about INR60-70 crore capex.
Long-term target of crossing 1 lakh MT capacity by FY28.
Target minimum EBITDA of 18-20% for planned US finishing operations, versus 14-15% in India.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 72,000 MTPA across Dera Bassi, Hoshiarpur, Mohali and Tahliwal. Utilisation about 73-74% (around 52,000 MT); management says 80-85% is achievable in FY27 if market holds.
FY27: about 7,800 MT green sand foundry addition, to be commissioned in H1 FY27, plus matching machining capacity. Capacity to reach about 80,000 MT.
FY28: about 2,400 MT of LFC capacity; capacity to cross 1 lakh MT. Management said LFC capacity mix would be about 70/30 to 65/35 (conventional/LFC) after this addition.
Greenfield LFC economics: 3,000 MT capacity at about INR75 crore versus INR120-150 crore for conventional, roughly 50% lower capex.
Hoshiarpur land acquired via ARC auction was withdrawn after litigation; refund received. Company is looking for fresh land in about two to three months for capacity beyond 1-2 years.
demand_pricing: Customers expect 6-8% growth in FY27 with H2 facing a high base; company expects about 15% from new products and projects.
Company says it gained share with almost all customers: market grew 16-17% while the company grew 34%.
Top three customers (M&M, Swaraj, TAFE, Escorts named) contribute about 50-55% of revenue.
Order book described as overbooked; Vishal's estimate of INR500-600 crore was affirmed as easily achievable, but no official figure was stated.

Raw material cost up about 4-6% in March; management says raw material is passed through with about a one-quarter lag, while freight pass-through is being negotiated (monthly for some customers, quarterly for others).

Exports started to South Korea (one lot shipped, another going); Europe being explored. US subsidiary (Omnia Engineering Inc., Delaware) acquired for $50,000 with up to $100,000 planned; not yet operational.

qa_highlights.question: What is installed capacity and maximum utilisation, and why have EBITDA margins fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is 72,000 MT; utilisation about 73-74%, with 80-85% achievable this year. Margin fell to 12% because raw material prices rose sharply in March, aggravated by gas issues; recovery expected from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall in Q4, and will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material rose about 4-6%, and gas, outsourced labour, manpower and freight costs also rose in March. Management expects a reversion to 15-16% margins if war-related disruption does not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan and funding for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR25-30 crore, with about INR35 crore for the 7,800 MT project per management. FY28 LFC project of 2,400 MT needs about INR60-70 crore, funded by debt and equity; FY27 funded by debt only.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels and leverage comfort?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose to about INR180 crore this year, with interest cost about INR22 crore. Management said net debt-to-equity will stay below 1 at all times; comfortable at about 0.65.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US entity's margin profile and plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The US entity is aimed at direct US customers; initial work would be manufacturing in India, with later possible acquisition or a US plant. Finishing-only US operations are expected to give 18-20% EBITDA margins versus 14-15% in India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LFC share of revenue and order book, and what is the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: LFC is about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book. Margin is 1-2% higher than conventional castings. Customers added include KION India (domestic) and one in South Korea.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin recovery depends on stabilisation of gas, crude-linked chemicals and diesel/freight costs; freight pass-through is still under negotiation.
Debt rose to about INR180 crore in FY26, with interest about INR22 crore; FY28 capex funding mix depends on equity raise plans that were not specified.
The 7,800 MT addition's capex figure was stated inconsistently (INR35 crore vs an earlier INR60-70 crore for the project); clarity needed.
Customer concentration: top three customers are about 50-55% of revenue.
Legacy components (about 60% of mix per management) carry lower margins; the new-component mix shift will determine margin trajectory.
US entity and export ramp-up are early-stage, with no revenue or timeline disclosed.

539359|2026-09.headline: Pritika Auto Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31.55% YoY to INR153.19 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 13.85% from 15.99%.
539359|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 grew 31.55% YoY to INR153.19 crore, supported by higher production volumes (15,665 MT, up about 22%) and OEM programme execution. EBITDA rose 13.97% to INR21.21 crore, but margin compressed about 214 bps YoY to 13.85%, which management attributed to raw material (scrap and pig iron) price spikes not yet passed through. Margin improved sequentially from 13.45% in Q1 FY27. PAT rose 12.41% to INR7.43 crore. Management flagged an export order via subsidiary Pritika Engineering Components and a target of 1 lakh MT installed capacity by end-2028.

segments.commentary: About 7% of business. Already supplying Ashok Leyland, with plans to expand product portfolio and volumes there.

segments.commentary: Developing 2-3 components; RDSO route to start by Jan-Feb 2027, with supplies targeted from Sep-Oct 2027 (H2 FY28).

qa_highlights.question: How does management see export growth over the next 2-3 years and what share of revenue is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports have potential in Europe and the USA; the Italian order of INR12 crore per annum could reach INR40-50 crore in 3 years, and exports should contribute a minimum 10-15% of sales in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA grow only about 14% when revenue grew about 31% in Q2, and what is the pass-through period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a sharp rise in raw material prices (scrap and pig iron) in Q2, which is passed on with a one-quarter lag, so Q3 margins should improve.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation and return profile of the capacity investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Green sand capacity is running at about 90% and LFC at about 50%; 7,800 MT is being added by end of the month, and the balance-sheet plan is a combination of debt (major part) and equity.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the increase in other expenses (INR28 crore to about INR34 crore) and interest expense (INR5.60 crore to INR6.33 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses rose in line with sales, and interest rose in line with growth; as a percentage it had reduced from 25% (answer brief, no breakdown given).

qa_highlights.question: What is the expansion roadmap to 1 lakh MT capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity moves to 80,000 MT with 7,800 MT by end of November; another 24,000 MT is planned by 2028 after land acquisition, with 2027 as the construction year and 1 lakh MT by end-2028.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and margin guidance over the next couple of years?

539400|2026-03.headline: Mallcom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR147 crore, but EBITDA margin fell 185 bps to 9.34% on raw material costs.
539400|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR147 crore (+7% YoY), with EBITDA down 11% YoY to INR14 crore and margin at 9.34%, and PAT of INR6 crore (4.29% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR540 crore (+11%), EBITDA INR61 crore (11.21% margin, down 130 bps), and PAT INR30 crore; FY25 PAT included a one-time INR25 crore land-sale gain, so the years are not directly comparable. Export OEM realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and tariff-driven concessions, while the domestic business grew about 20%. Both new units (Sanand, Gujarat and Chandipur, West Bengal) are now commissioned and ramping up.

segments.name: Domestic (branded)
segments.commentary: Management says the domestic business grew about 20% YoY in FY26 and is the growth engine; branded business has better pricing power. Last month of Q4 was softer on cautious sentiment and gas shortages for some industries.

segments.name: Exports (OEM / white label)
segments.commentary: Realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and concessions to hold share. South America, Australia, Russia and Africa were described as doing well; Europe and US weak; Middle East okay. LatAm sales are white label.

segments.name: New products (PU coated gloves, PVC gumboots, nitrile)
segments.commentary: In-house manufacturing started as import substitutes; management says pricing is competitive with imports and margins are similar to company level. India PU glove imports estimated at INR80-90 crore.

segments.name: Sanand, Gujarat (workwear/Protec unit)
segments.commentary: Commercial production started; running at about 50% utilisation, with INR40 crore minimum annual revenue targeted from existing capacity.

guidance_outlook: Management says 10-12% revenue growth is the bare minimum for FY27 and it is confident of achieving it, with upside if conditions improve.
Management wants to return to pre-investment EBITDA margins over time, but said there are many ifs and buts at this stage; an analyst's 14-15% normalised margin framing was not explicitly confirmed.
Expects FY27 revenue growth to come more from domestic than exports.
Capex: INR34 crore spent in FY26; budget INR10-15 crore for FY27 and similar annual levels thereafter, covering maintenance plus added machinery at Sanand and Chandipur.
Expects to apply for a capital subsidy for Sanand, estimated at about INR10 crore under the state policy.
Expects debt, mainly working capital, to decline further and most debt to be repaid over about 4 years; finance cost could approach near zero in 3 years (analyst framing, CFO said 'possible').
capex_capacity: Sanand, Gujarat (Protec unit) has commenced commercial production; utilisation about 50%, with INR40 crore minimum annual revenue targeted.
Chandipur, West Bengal industrial safety shoe unit is fully operational; capitalised in FY26 with INR7 crore of subsidy received against INR14 crore machinery cost.
In-house manufacturing of PU coated gloves and PVC gumboots started.
FY26 capex about INR34 crore; FY27 budget INR10-15 crore, with ongoing annual spend in a similar range.
demand_pricing: Export OEM realisations fell in FY26 due to near-full-year prohibitive US tariffs, weak EU demand and concessions to retain share; price pass-through lags, especially in long-lead OEM business.
Input costs rose across textiles, leather, PU/PC/NBR polymers, driven by petro-linked prices, FX depreciation, freight and energy costs.
Domestic: price list revised twice in the last quarter; competitors also raised prices, and some stopped taking orders or cancelled open orders.

US: volumes fell, but management says this reflects tariff conditions, not product, quality or price. India is outside the US TAA list, so an FTA is seen as key to regaining share; order cycles run 3 months to 2-2.5 years.
Competition: China seen as better placed on raw material sourcing and currency; unorganised players expected to be hurt by the cost environment, which management sees as favouring organised players.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall, and which export product prices decreased?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower realisations were mainly in export OEM markets, due to weak demand and concessions to keep customers. Domestic price increases lag input cost rises.

qa_highlights.question: How much could 10-12% growth and a 14-15% normalised margin be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-12% growth is the bare minimum and it is confident of it. It wants to return to pre-investment EBITDA margins, which it describes as the profile it would like to maintain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and finance cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: no term loan; working capital debt is about flat YoY at INR110-115 crore. Expects further reduction and most debt repaid over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key domestic demand drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code formalisation, BIS standards tightening, rising worker awareness, wider distribution, more marketing and fleet, and import substitution. Management says domestic growth is sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and subsidy?

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable market for PU gloves and PVC gumboots?
qa_highlights.answer: India imports an estimated INR80-90 crore of PU gloves; PVC gumboot market size was not quantified. Export revenue is also targeted for both products.

Sanand utilisation (about 50%) and ramp-up of new products against the INR40 crore revenue target.

Q4 PAT margin of 4.29% and EBITDA margin of 9.34% as the base for FY27 margin recovery.
