539400|2026-06.headline: Mallcom Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 25% QoQ to Rs 110 crore, while EBITDA margin rose 317 bps to 12.51% on pricing and raw material relief.
539400|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was Rs 110 crore, down 25% QoQ, driven by weaker international sales and West Asia disruption. EBITDA held flat QoQ at Rs 14 crore, with margin up to 12.51%, and PAT rose 5% QoQ to Rs 7 crore (6.03% margin). Domestic revenue of Rs 64 crore grew 10% QoQ and was the highest-ever Q1 domestic number; international revenue was Rs 46 crore. Management said port congestion and weak Western demand cost the company a targeted double-digit export growth.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 64 crore, up 10% QoQ and the highest Q1 domestic revenue to date; brand recall and the SMILE reseller programme (over 1,000 resellers) cited as drivers.

segments.name: International / Export
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 46 crore, down sharply QoQ on weak Western demand and port congestion; management says exports are about 55% of the mix. Europe is down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1 against about Rs 170 crore for last year.

segments.name: Sanand plant
segments.commentary: Three lines now operating (helmets, foam caps, nasal caps); FY26 revenue about Rs 5 crore (Q4 only); FY27 minimum target Rs 40 crore, described as on track.

guidance_outlook: Management will not revise the Rs 1,000 crore revenue ambition for FY28, calling it a stretch but still a goal.
Top-line guidance of about 10-12% growth maintained; management hopes to reach the Rs 600 crore level for the year.
Export and domestic mix expected to approach 50:50 by year end, which management called realistic.
Aim to return to the regular margin profile, helped by price pass-through and Sanand efficiency.
Europe expected to grow YoY this year, with a target to recover the lost sales over the next three quarters; the India-EU FTA effect is seen mainly from next year.
Working capital borrowings expected flat through the year; term loans taken for Sanand capex and incentives.
capex_capacity: Sanand plant: three lines operating; helmet, foam cap and nasal cap production underway; management looking to add further capacity.
New EN812 certified bump cap mould launched and manufacturing started at Sanand.
Ongoing machinery capex to add capacity (no new building or land spend), per CFO.
Newer Gujarat investments aimed mainly at domestic and branded markets, with some export; large export contracts not expected quickly.
demand_pricing: Export demand weak in the West; management attributes part of the export shortfall to port congestion and containers stuck at sea.
Roughly 60-70% of export sales are planned and 30% spot/L1-priced (about 30% of export is commoditised).
Raw material prices remain elevated vs pre-West Asia levels for crude-linked products; some easing seen versus March-April.
Price pass-through: own-brand pricing adjusted from the start of the crisis; white-label contracts lag and will be recovered over the rest of the year.
No FX gain in the quarter; the company says costs are largely hedged.
New FR workwear (EN/US certified) launched for own brand and white label; value-added products cited at about 60-70% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Are raw material prices trending and how should margins move?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude-linked products remain at escalated levels versus pre-war; overall RM costs are higher than at start of calendar year, with some easing. Pass-through is gradual because of long-term fixed-price contracts.

qa_highlights.question: How much export growth was lost and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both weak Western demand and port congestion. The company had targeted at least double-digit export growth, which it missed this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a margin base now and what about under-recovery and FX?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a base and the aim is to grow from here. CFO said there is no under-recovery after the price increases taken at the start of the quarter, and no FX gain as costs are hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its Rs 1,000 crore target for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not revise the target now, calling it a stretch, and levers include capacity, distribution, new geographies, FTAs and larger contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Sanand revenue target and new lines?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: minimum FY27 target of Rs 40 crore, on track after Q1. FY26 was about Rs 5 crore. Three lines are operating; more capacity is being considered.

qa_highlights.question: Have any large LATAM or US export contracts been won?
qa_highlights.answer: Some long-term contracts exist for workwear and footwear. Large new contracts are not expected quickly; US demand is uncertain due to tariffs.

risks_watch: Export demand in Europe and LATAM remains weak; Europe was down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1.
White-label price pass-through lags, so margin recovery depends on contract renewals within the year.
US tariff uncertainty and importer hesitation; no large US contract yet.
Port congestion and container availability disrupting shipments and Middle East supply.
Revenue must rise to earn back the fixed-cost absorption lost in Q1 (lower turnover).
539400|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and domestic execution, but cautious and somewhat defensive on exports, US and the Rs 1,000 crore target. Management stressed that volatility and logistics, not strategy, drove the export shortfall.
key_quotes: Despite the challenging and volatile market environment during the quarter, we delivered a meaningful improvement in profitability supported by lower raw material cost, improved operational efficiency at our Sanand plant, and our continued ability to pass on cost increases to our customers.
So, there is no FOREX gain because in our case, mostly we are hedged.
So, whatever cost increase was there, we have been able to pass on this to the customer, and we took this exercise at the beginning of the quarter itself.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 317 bps QoQ to 12.51% on price increases and raw material relief, and management aims to return to its regular margin profile via price pass-through on white-label contracts that lag and will be recovered over the rest of the year, plus Sanand efficiency.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (already live); further lines under consideration

rows.why: Top-line growth guidance of about 10-12% is maintained with a Rs 600 crore FY27 aspiration, supported by domestic revenue up 10% QoQ to Rs 64 crore, but Q1 revenue fell 25% QoQ to Rs 110 crore and export missed its double-digit growth target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is looking to add further capacity and ongoing machinery capex continues with no new building or land spend, but no amount or board-approved plan was quantified and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management maintained rather than raised top-line guidance, and Q1 revenue fell 25% QoQ to Rs 110 crore with exports down sharply on weak Western demand and port congestion.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Export growth target was missed, Europe was down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1 against about Rs 170 crore last year, and the Rs 1,000 crore FY28 target is described as a stretch, though management has said it will not revise it now.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New EN812 certified bump cap mould launched and manufacturing started at Sanand, and new FR workwear (EN/US certified) launched for own brand and white label.

rows.label: White-label price pass-through catch-up
rows.why: Own-brand pricing was adjusted from the start of the crisis, while white-label contracts lag and will be recovered over the rest of the year, with crude-linked raw materials still above pre-West Asia levels.

rows.label: Europe recovery and India-EU FTA
rows.when: Europe YoY growth this year; FTA effect mainly from next yea
rows.why: Europe was down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1 against about Rs 170 crore last year, with management targeting recovery of lost sales over the next three quarters and FTA benefit seen mainly from next year.

rows.label: Large US or LATAM export contracts
rows.why: No large US contract has been won yet, US demand is uncertain due to tariffs, and management does not expect large export contracts quickly.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, domestic execution and the Sanand ramp, but cautious and somewhat defensive on exports, US demand and the Rs 1,000 crore FY28 target; analysts probed the export shortfall, raw material trajectory and whether the target would be revised.

539404|2026-03.headline: Satin Creditcare FY26 consolidated PAT rose 79% to INR330 crores; Q4 PAT up 125% QoQ, with FY27 standalone AUM growth guided at 15-20%.
539404|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated AUM of INR15,174 crores (up 19% YoY), revenue of INR3,161 crores (up 23%) and PPOP of INR928 crores (up 23%). Consolidated PAT was INR330 crores for FY26, and Q4 PAT rose 640% YoY and 125% QoQ, which management attributed to lower credit costs and growth, not one-offs. Standalone GNPA was 3.1% at March 2026 and credit cost fell to 3.8% for FY26 from 4.6% in FY25, with Q4 at 2.5% standalone and 2.2% consolidated. Management guided FY27 standalone AUM growth of 15-20% and credit cost of 3-3.5%, and raised its 2030 consolidated AUM target to INR32,000 crores from INR25,000 crores.

financial_highlights.change: NIM 13.23% in FY26 vs 12.42% in FY25

financial_highlights.value: FY26 3.8% standalone; 3.55% consolidated; Q4 2.5% standalone, 2.2% consolidated (INR79 crores)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 standalone -77 bps vs 4.6% in FY25

segments.name: Standalone microfinance (JLG)
segments.commentary: Standalone AUM INR12,853 crores (+14% YoY) with disbursements of INR11,202 crores; UP is 23% of portfolio with PAR 90 of 3%, Assam PAR 90 0.7%, Punjab 1.5%. Stage 3 coverage 73% (from 67% in Dec 2025); on-book provisions INR273 crores (2.9%) vs RBI requirement INR172 crores.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,267 crores, 3-year CAGR 36%; GNPA about 3%, CRAR 53.8%; ICRA A- stable. Average yield about 15.5-16%.

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL, MSME subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,054 crores, up 92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%; 121 branches in 14 states; disbursed INR255 crores across 34 green loans. Lending is secured by receivables, equipment and property, per management.

segments.name: Satin Technologies (STL)
segments.commentary: Enterprise tech (HRMS, LMS, core banking, cybersecurity, agentic AI); first two clients within two months of incorporation; strategic stake in QTrino (post-quantum cryptography) acquired January 2026.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives (SGAL)
segments.commentary: SEBI licence received for INR200 crore Category II AIF, a gender-lens impact fund for rural MSMEs; MOU with SBI for co-investment; progressing toward first close with soft commitments.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone AUM growth 15-20% YoY, implying about INR14,800-15,100 crores.
FY27 standalone credit cost target 3-3.5% vs 3.8% in FY26.
Consolidated AUM growth management estimate about 25-30% (average), so consolidated AUM roughly doubles toward the 2030 target.
2030 consolidated AUM target raised to INR32,000 crores from INR25,000 crores; non-MFI share target 30% (17% today).

NIM expected stable at about 12-13% consolidated (management also cited 13.5-14% over a longer period); no explicit ROA guidance, but management said ROA should improve on FY26's 2.6%, and that a >3% ROA is 'positive' rather than guided.
Cost of funds expected stable to lower; management says it could fall further as repo rates decline.
risks_watch: Q4 overall collection efficiency of just over 97% versus 99.9% X-bucket; monitor whether April holds and whether geopolitics or inflation (fuel prices) affects collections and demand.
Consolidated PAT is sensitive to forex and treasury gains: INR144 crores consolidated derecognition gain, of which INR92 crores is FX-related; management says this reverses over time.
Q4 PAT surge partly reflects lower credit cost; sustainability depends on the 3-3.5% FY27 credit cost target being met.
Yield regulation: incremental MFI yield about 25% and RBI commentary on interest rates; management says the pricing is justified but did not comment on future caps.
Subsidiary ramp-up (SGAL first close, STL client wins) is still early; the consolidated 25-30% growth and 30% non-MFI mix by 2030 depend on it.
Standalone net worth (INR3,129 crores) exceeds consolidated (INR2,868 crores) due to an old revaluation gain, which has limited analytical value.
539404|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on asset quality, profitability and diversification, with strong claims on Q4 performance. Management was evasive on specifics: declined to give ROA guidance, the April collection-efficiency number and the Q4 absolute consolidated PAT, and gave a vague answer on the RBI yield question.
key_quotes: Consolidated PAT grew 640% year -on-year and 125% quarter -on-quarter.
There's no one-off.
We are not growing blindly. We are growing into our infrastructure with the discipline that has defined Satin.
So there is no question where I think it could be singled out as in terms of tax and it's an interest rate play which is going to be there.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about Satin Finserv's customer profile, collateral and underwriting approach.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SFL serves graduated MFI customers and green-finance/micro-enterprise borrowers, underwrites on cash flows and internal scores with data analytics, and lends on secured terms (receivables, equipment, property). It did not give a percentage of the book secured by property; LTV is about 40-45%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for April X-bucket collection efficiency and whether geopolitical issues are causing stress.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April is holding at a similar level to Q4 (99.9%) but did not give a figure, and said there is no stress from the geopolitical situation in any state. Q4 overall collection efficiency was a little over 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether there was any one-off in Q4 PAT, including forex.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-off; Aditi Singh attributed the Q4 PAT rise to reduced credit cost and the growth strategy. Management did not separately quantify the Q4 absolute consolidated PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for FY27 ROA guidance and whether ROA above 3% is achievable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give explicit ROA guidance, saying it is a function of AUM growth and credit cost; it said it expects ROA to be better than FY26's 2.6% and that the direction is positive.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the consolidated AUM path to the 2030 target and the growth pace.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 15-20% guidance applies to standalone MFI only; consolidated growth is expected to average about 25-30%, which supports the revised INR32,000 crore 2030 AUM target (from INR25,000 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the INR144 crore net gain on derecognition of financial instruments and whether treasury income is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidated INR144 crore line includes a INR92 crore FX effect offset by a corresponding finance-cost item, while derecognition gains are DA income and fair-value gains are treasury income on mutual funds and forex contracts. Management said treasury income is incidental to liquidity, and that NIM is broadly stable at 13.5-14% over a longer period.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the RBI yield-cap risk and whether the MFI yield of about 25% is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the regulator's interest-rate focus should be read in the context of financial inclusion, doorstep delivery, elevated credit cost and cost of funds, and risk-based pricing. It did not say how it sees future caps and said there is no question of a one-off yield cut.

capex_capacity: 392 new branches added in FY26; field presence in over 1 lakh villages and 550-plus districts; 2,015 branches and 577 districts as of the call, 34 lakh customers, 18,265 employees.
Presence in over 64% of India's pin codes; technology and AI used across underwriting, portfolio monitoring and risk assessment.
Liquidity of INR2,092 crores and undrawn sanctions of INR2,235 crores; ALM positive across all buckets; FY26 borrowings raised INR10,826 crores; 75 active lenders.
SGAL: SEBI licence received for INR200 crore Category II AIF; progressing toward first close with strong soft commitments; MOU with SBI for co-investment.

STL: first two clients acquired within two months of incorporation; strategic stake in QTrino (IIT Patna incubated, post-quantum cryptography) acquired January 2026; representative offices in Toronto and Dubai.
Management said standalone AUM growth of 15-20% in FY27 rests on branch infrastructure and ALM, and said it is growing into existing infrastructure rather than growing blindly.
demand_pricing: Sector: CRIF High Mark data cited by management shows MFI originations up 25.8% QoQ to INR77,555 crores in Q3 FY26; average ticket size up 18% YoY; sector PAR 1-180 days at 4.7% in January 2026.

Standalone disbursements FY26 INR11,202 crores; Q4 disbursements up 43% (per closing remarks); sourcing-to-disbursement ratio 39%; NATCAT insurance covered INR5,800 crores of disbursement since September 2025.

Pricing: average incremental MFI yield about 25% (management confirmed analyst's 25-26% reading as broadly correct); housing finance average yield about 15.5-16%; SFL green loans priced close to MFI yield.
Diversification: non-MFI share 17% of consolidated AUM today, target 30% by 2030. SFL AUM INR1,054 crores (+92.5% YoY); SHFL AUM INR1,267 crores.

Collections: Q4 overall collection efficiency just over 97%; X-bucket collection efficiency 99.9% in Q4 and said to be holding in April without giving a figure; management said no geopolitical stress seen in any state.
Cost of funds: marginal cost of borrowing 10.82%, down 43 bps; management said cost of funds should stay stable or fall as repo rates decline.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Credit cost guided down to 3-3.5% in FY27 from 3.8% in FY26 (Q4 at 2.5% standalone), and marginal cost of borrowing fell 43 bps to 10.82%, but consolidated NIM is guided flat at 12-13% and FY26 NIM was 13.23%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 392 branches added in FY26 to 2,015 today; FY27 standalone AUM growth of 15-20% is said to rest on existing branch infrastructure, with no forward branch count given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone AUM guided +15-20% to INR14,800-15,100 crores from INR12,853 crores; Q4 disbursements up 43% and undrawn sanctions INR2,235 crores support it, while consolidated growth is estimated at 25-30%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex plan discussed; growth is said to come from existing branches and ALM, and the only new capital item is the INR200 crore SGAL AIF, which is a fund, not productive capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said ROA should improve on FY26's 2.6% and that >3% is 'positive' but not guided; Q4 ROA was 4.71%, though it is partly credit-cost driven and FY27 guidance is only 15-20% AUM growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 collection efficiency was just over 97% overall versus 99.9% X-bucket, April was not quantified, and the Q4 PAT jump relies on credit cost falling to 2.5% against a 3-3.5% FY27 target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SGAL Category II AIF (INR200 crore) is in progress toward first close with soft commitments; SFL green loans are being disbursed (INR255 crores across 34 loans) and non-MFI share is targeted at 30% by 2030 from 17% today.

rows.label: RBI yield-cap risk on MFI pricing
rows.why: Incremental MFI yield is about 25%, management gave no view on future caps and said there is no question of a one-off yield cut, so a regulatory cut to yields is a live risk.

rows.label: Subsidiary ramp-up: SFL and SHFL growth
rows.why: SFL AUM INR1,054 crores (+92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%) and SHFL AUM INR1,267 crores (3-year CAGR 36%) keep the non-MFI mix rising toward the 30% by 2030 target from 17%.

rows.label: Treasury and FX gain sustainability
rows.why: Of the INR144 crore consolidated derecognition gain, INR92 crores is an FX effect offset by finance cost, and management said treasury income is incidental and reverses over time, so reported PAT may fall back.

539404|2026-06.headline: Satin Q1 FY27 standalone PAT up 182% YoY to INR120 crore after absorbing a INR36 crore management overlay; reported ROA 3.55%.
539404|2026-06.overview: Satin reported its 20th consecutive profitable quarter and its strongest Q1 in eight years, with consolidated AUM of INR15,935 crore (up 27% YoY, 5% QoQ) and record Q1 disbursements. Standalone NIM rose to 14.36% from 13.16% and cost-to-income improved to 44.49%. Management chose to absorb a INR36 crore management overlay, which lowered reported ROA to 3.55% (4.34% adjusted) and ROE to 15.10% (18.46% adjusted). Guidance for FY27 was kept at 20-25% consolidated AUM growth, 3-3.5% credit cost and 3.5-4% reported ROA, with a review at the half year.

financial_highlights.change: from 13.16% YoY; DA income INR94 crore in Q1 vs ~INR140 crore in Q4

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,360 crore, up 134% YoY and 29% QoQ across 121 branches in 14 states; CRAR 27.1%.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance (SHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,263 crore, up 31% YoY; CRAR 59.8% across 57 branches in 22 states.

segments.name: Green finance book
segments.commentary: Reached INR624 crore; INR294 crore disbursed across 50 loans in Q1; ~45% of sustainable and emerging businesses portfolio in clean mobility and renewables.

segments.name: Satin Technologies / QTrino Labs
segments.commentary: First paying HRMS customers in Q1; QTrino Labs reached first customer revenue milestone. Core banking platform in customer UAT, go-live targeted Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives
segments.commentary: Progressing toward first close of Category 2 AIF, with first deployment expected in the coming quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated AUM growth of 20-25% in FY27, implying INR18,200-18,900 crore by March 2027.
Standalone reported credit cost of 3-3.5% for FY27, inclusive of any buffer built.
Standalone reported ROA of 3.5-4% for FY27; management expects QoQ ROA improvement from the 3.3% consolidated level.
NIM expected to stay in a 14.35-14.50% steady-state range.
Guidance to be reviewed at the half year depending on monsoon; long-term target INR32,000 crore consolidated AUM by 2030 with 30% from non-MFI.
Non-MFI share of consolidated AUM at 19% vs 14% a year ago; target 30% by 2030.
capex_capacity: Added 41 standalone branches in Q1; total 2,041 branches, 34 lakh clients, 3.9 lakh centres, 18,518 employees.
Commenced operations in Kerala in June 2026, adding to Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
392 branches added in FY26 are seasoning; operating expense ratio improved to 6.33% from 6.98% in Q4.
AUM per loan officer up 29% YoY.
Breakeven rule of thumb for a new branch: about 1,000 customers, typically reached in about 9 months.
INR100 crore promoter infusion approved by shareholders at about a 17% premium to the minimum issue price, to fund subsidiary growth.
demand_pricing: Q1 is seasonally the softest quarter; management called Q1 disbursements the highest first-quarter disbursements in company history.

Assam floods hit 3 districts (Jorhat, Sivasagar, Charaideo): about 44,000 borrowers and INR149.83 crore outstanding affected, of which INR96.95 crore is covered by nat-cat insurance. Management says Assam ex-those districts is 100% on target.
Bank share of outstanding MFI loans fell to 26.4% from 32.6% a year ago; NBFC-MFI share rose to 43.7% from 38.9%.
Marginal cost of borrowing down 37 bps YoY to 10.52%; 77 active lenders; top 10 lenders are 52% of borrowing; INR2,000 crore direct assignment sanction from a public sector bank.

539450|2026-06.headline: S H Kelkar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore, with EBITDA up 21% to Rs 89 crore and margin at 13.4%.
539450|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore and EBITDA rose 21% to Rs 89 crore, with margin expanding to 13.4% from 12.6%. Flavours was the standout, at Rs 112 crore, which management says includes about Rs 15 crore of one-off pre-ordering and stock build; the normalised run-rate is about Rs 95-96 crore. Global Ingredients was softer on supply gaps, and Fragrances India was flat as the company exited low-margin business and repriced clients. Net debt rose Rs 65 crore to Rs 852 crore on inventory build and capex, and a Rs 30 crore insurance exceptional item was booked.

financial_highlights.change: Supported by product mix and raw material planning
Normalised about Rs 95-96 crore excluding about Rs 15 crore pre-ordering
Expected to rise to Rs 38-39 crore per quarter after Vanvate capitalisation

segments.name: Flavours
segments.commentary: Strong broad-based growth; Rs 112 crore in Q1 versus a normalised Rs 95-96 crore, with about Rs 15 crore attributed to pre-ordering and extra channel stock. Management expects Q2 to be above Rs 95-96 crore but not above Rs 112 crore.

segments.name: Fragrances (Europe and international)
segments.commentary: Healthy growth led by Europe and select international markets. Europe plant operational since May; European capex completed. Segment margins are weighed down by higher R&D and global CDC opex.

segments.name: Fragrances India
segments.commentary: Flat YoY, against a strong Q1 FY26 base. Company exited low-margin business and held back shipments until price corrections were agreed; about 95% of clients accepted price increases.

segments.name: Global Ingredients
segments.commentary: Softer quarter on lower demand in select export markets and supply gaps from raw-material constraints; management expects recovery in H2.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit revenue growth and improved margins for full FY27, but would not give a precise full-year margin range beyond the next 2-3 months.
If double-digit growth holds, EBITDA in absolute terms should be similar to Q1 levels; margin could vary about 1% either way.
Raw material costs said to be fixed for about 6 months via stock in hand and contracts; about 45 days extra inventory built to pass on future cost shocks.
Net debt expected broadly flat at June level through Q2 (may rise slightly in September), then fall about Rs 25 crore per quarter from Q3.
Remaining India capex about Rs 100 crore in total (Rs 25 crore in Q1 done, Rs 25 crore in Q2 on Vanvate, about Rs 50 crore for the three India plants); Vanvate factory commissioning in Q3.
Target ETR below 30%, from 31.5-32% currently.
Long-term targets: ROCE above 15% in 3-5 years and 20% long term; European business ROCE 17-18% over the long run.
US revenue expected at about USD 1.5-2 million for FY27; UK business needs 12-15 months before material revenue.
capex_capacity: Europe capex of about Rs 25 crore in Q1 completed; Almere factory operational since May 2026 and a large R&D centre in Germany added.
India: Vanvate factory to be commissioned in Q3 FY27; bulk of India investment capex expected by end of Q2.
Vashivali plant upgrade: last Rs 25 crore may be spent in Q4 FY27 or deferred to Q1 FY28, depending on demand.
Extra R&D spend of about USD 3 million a year in Europe.
Quarterly depreciation about Rs 35 crore, rising to Rs 38-39 crore after Vanvate capitalisation.
demand_pricing: Price corrections passed to about 95%+ of clients after raw-material cost inflation linked to West Asia geopolitics; clients reluctant to accept were not supplied until negotiations concluded.
Flavours pre-ordering of 1-2 to 3 weeks was driven by long lead and shipping times; July momentum reported as steady.
Global Ingredients supply curtailed due to raw-material uncertainty; backward integration and China de-risking steps said to be in place.
Unilever and global accounts: ongoing project flow but no large new breakthroughs; Unilever's own pricing pressures and weak India launches noted.
Management cites a US plus UK fragrance market of about USD 10 billion, roughly 4-5x India's fragrance market, with about USD 100 million addressable in the near term.
Around 10-11% of revenue comes from products launched in the last 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year Flavours budget and how much did FX add to revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Flavours was Rs 112 crore versus a normalised Rs 95-96 crore, with about Rs 15 crore pulled forward. Like-for-like growth was about 9%, and FX added about 5 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Is flat India Fragrance a high-base effect, and what is the trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 was strong. The company deliberately exited low-margin business, held back shipments during price negotiations, and says it now services almost all clients after building inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be guided for FY27, and is the Q1 gross margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise full-year range was given. Management says Q1 is a normal quarter, not exceptional, so EBITDA should be similar in absolute terms if double-digit growth continues, with margin varying about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the factory timelines, debt path and tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Vanvate commissions in Q3. Debt stays near June levels, then falls about Rs 25 crore a quarter from Q3. ETR is 31.5-32% now, targeted below 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Europe ramp-up and return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Germany is expected to break even in FY27 or FY28, the US a year later, and the UK a year after that. Long-term European ROCE is 17-18%, and group ROCE above 15% in 3-5 years, rising to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance claim status and how is depreciation trending?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 30 crore was received in Q1, with Rs 50-60 crore still pending and full settlement expected in FY27. Depreciation is about Rs 35 crore a quarter, rising to Rs 38-39 crore after Vanvate.

risks_watch: Flavours Q1 (Rs 112 crore) includes about Rs 15 crore of pre-ordering and extra channel stock that management says will not recur every quarter; Q2 is guided above Rs 95-96 crore but not above Rs 112 crore

Raw material cost visibility of about 6 months from July, backed by stock in hand, contracts and about 45 days of extra inventory; cost shocks beyond that could hit gross margin if prices cannot be passed on
Global Ingredients softness from supply gaps and lower export demand; recovery is expected only in H2 FY27
Fragrances India flat YoY after deliberate exit from low-margin business and shipment holds; watch whether volumes recover as price increases settle

key_quotes: So, we have prepared in a manner that we have 6 months visibility on the inventory and our contracts or pricing to the client.
But for the full year, we are not confident to predict beyond 2, 3 months' time.
This is the baseline normal quarter.
We do not expect Rs. 112 plus growth in the quarter 2. That is not our expectation.
539450|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious and guarded on the outlook: management calls Q1 a normal quarter but declines to give a full-year margin range beyond 2-3 months, citing geopolitical volatility, energy and freight costs. Confident on near-term execution points such as raw material cover, Europe plant commissioning and supply continuity for existing clients.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 13.4% from 12.6% (about 80 bps), but Q1 included about Rs 15 crore of Flavours pre-ordering, and management gave no precise full-year margin range; margin could vary about 1% either way with EBITDA similar to Q1 (~Rs 89 crore).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Vanvate factory in India is guided for commissioning in Q3 FY27 with about Rs 25 crore capex in Q2, and Almere (Europe) went live in May 2026; depreciation rises from about Rs 35 crore to Rs 38-39 crore per quarter after Vanvate.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterates double-digit FY27 revenue growth (Q1 +14% reported, ~9% like-for-like, FX ~5 pts), with Flavours normalised at Rs 95-96 crore and Q2 guided above that, and Global Ingredients expected to recover in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Remaining India capex is about Rs 100 crore (Rs 25 crore done in Q1, Rs 25 crore Q2, about Rs 50 crore for three plants) with Vashivali's last Rs 25 crore possibly deferred to Q1 FY28; no new capex plan or utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is guarded, declining a full-year margin range beyond 2-3 months and citing geopolitical, energy and freight volatility, while Q1 was flattered by about Rs 15 crore of pre-ordering.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 Flavours is guided above Rs 95-96 crore but not above Rs 112 crore, Global Ingredients is supply-constrained until H2, and raw-material cover is only about 6 months, so a cost shock beyond that could hit gross margin.

rows.label: Net debt reduction from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Net debt of Rs 852 crore is guided flat through Q2, then to fall about Rs 25 crore per quarter from Q3; Rs 50-60 crore of insurance claim is still pending.

rows.label: Effective tax rate reduction to below 30%
rows.why: ETR is 31.5-32% in Q1 against a stated target below 30%, but no timing or driver for the cut was given.

rows.label: Europe breakeven ramp (Germany, US, UK)
rows.when: Germany FY27 or FY28; US a year later; UK a year after that
rows.why: Almere is operational since May 2026 and European capex is complete, with US revenue guided at about USD 1.5-2 million for FY27 and UK needing 12-15 months before material revenue; European losses persist until breakeven.

tone.note: Management was confident on raw-material cover, Europe commissioning and client supply continuity, but cautious on full-year margins, Global Ingredients and geopolitical cost risk; analysts pushed on the Flavours pre-ordering one-off, the margin outlook and the debt path.

539450|2026-09.headline: S H Kelkar H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% to Rs.1,299 crore and EBITDA 33% to Rs.168 crore, with margin at 13%.
539450|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations grew 15% YoY to Rs.636 crore, and H1 revenue reached Rs.1,299 crore (up 14%). H1 EBITDA rose 33% to Rs.168 crore, margin about 13%, with gross margins broadly stable despite raw material volatility. Flavour revenue grew 47% in H1 to Rs.184 crore, though management called part of Q1 a one-off inventory build by customers. Net debt stood at Rs.911 crore at September 30, 2026, which management expects to be the peak for the year as inventory is reduced.

segments.name: Fragrance
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.1,088 crore, up 11.9% YoY; management cites about 14% underlying growth excluding roughly Rs.50 crore of low-margin business hived off in Q4 FY26. Domestic growth about 9% (roughly 5% price, 4% volume).

segments.name: Flavour
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.184 crore, up 47% YoY; Q2 revenue about Rs.72 crore versus a Q1 that was higher. Management sees Rs.90 crore per quarter as the run rate and about 20% sustainable growth.

segments.name: Overseas CDCs (Germany, UK, US)
segments.commentary: First sales achieved in all three markets; revenue is small and management says it will take 12-18 months to become meaningful. Around Rs.80 crore of spend in these centres is not yet generating meaningful revenue.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 12-13% per year on a continuing basis over the next 2-3 years, with EBITDA growth of 13-14% per year.
Gross margin expected in the 43% range; upside of about 0.5% if raw material and geopolitical conditions ease.
EBITDA margin of 15%+ targeted within 12-18 months at steady-state inflation, or about two years if inflation persists; 13% described as the lower end of sustainable.
Interest cost expected at Rs.16-17 crore per quarter in H2 FY27; D&A expected at Rs.145-150 crore annualised after new facility capitalisation.
Net debt expected to fall from September 2026 peak by March 2027; insurance claim settlement expected by March 2027.
Remaining FY27 capex about Rs.30-35 crore; FY28 capex about Rs.75-80 crore including spillover, with maintenance capex about Rs.15 crore.
capex_capacity: Europe capex almost complete; Europe factory operational since May 2026 and fully operational in Q2.
India Fragrance factory renewal expected to be completed and put to use in Q4 FY27; transition from Mulund follows in FY28.
Second factory (Vanavate or Vashivali) expected to be put to use in Q4 FY28, concluding the large expansion.
Jakarta (Southeast Asia) factory in full operation since September 2025, improving lead times to clients.
Overseas development centres in Germany, Manchester (UK) and US are fully staffed and in use; no further CDC investment planned.
demand_pricing: Domestic Fragrance growth split roughly 5% price and 4% volume; large clients are growing faster than smaller clients, which management calls transient.
Excluding about Rs.25 crore of intentionally exited low-margin categories, like-for-like growth is about 12%.
Management expects a stabilisation in raw material prices and strong H2 demand, but flagged the Middle East situation as the biggest risk.
Flavour growth in Q1 was partly a one-off as customers built inventory due to freight and logistics disruption; management expects about 20% sustainable growth.
More than 5,000 clients served globally; no specific RFQs cited. Europe and US smaller-brand and mid-size opportunities are being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fragrance growth split between volume and value in domestic market?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 5% from price and 4% from volume in the domestic Fragrance business, which grew about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: When will inventory unwind and working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory reduction started in October 2026; management does not expect a sharp total inventory fall but expects lower inventory intensity as sales grow over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable interest and depreciation run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest about Rs.16-17 crore per quarter in H2 FY27; D&A about Rs.145-150 crore annualised, with European acquisition amortisation reducing from 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Flavour Q2 run rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 at about Rs.72 crore was below the normal run rate and Rs.90 crore per quarter is the right run rate; Q1 was above it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROCE below 12% since 2019?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mature India businesses earn about 20% ROCE; overseas investment, the 2024 expansion and fire-related domestic capex weigh on the figure. Rs.80 crore of CDC spend is not yet earning returns.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone margin low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operations moved to subsidiaries KFG and KFL after the fire, so standalone margins are not representative and should recover once operations move back next year.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict, raw material inflation and availability, and geopolitical outcomes after the US midterm elections.
Net debt of Rs.911 crore at September 2026 and working capital tied up in high inventory; delivery on the March 2027 reduction target.
Flavour growth lumpiness from customer order timing and inventory destocking after Q1 one-off demand.
Overseas CDCs take 12-18 months to become meaningful; ROCE remains below 12% in the near term.
Execution of Fragrance factory renewal (Q4 FY27) and second factory (Q4 FY28) with capex spillover into FY28.
539450|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and margin recovery, but cautious on near-term inflation and geopolitics; management repeatedly declined to extrapolate the 40%+ Flavour growth and reset the base to about 20%.
key_quotes: We expect September debt level to represent a peak for the year with the reduction anticipated by March 2027 as we optimize inventory levels.
So, we expect 14% on a 12% revenue growth, 13% to 14% EBITDA growth year-on-year in the next 2-3 years.

It will take a good three to four years before we are breakeven in those markets by themselves and then another further three to four years as we continue to grow to generate meaningful returns on this investment.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Europe factory is already operational (fully in Q2 FY27), India Fragrance factory renewal is due Q4 FY27 and the second factory (Vanavate or Vashivali) is due Q4 FY28, though the second factory timing sits beyond the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance is 12-13% continuing revenue growth per year, with domestic Fragrance volume at about 4% and Flavour run rate seen at Rs.90 crore per quarter with about 20% sustainable growth, but no firm RFQs or order book were cited.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Remaining FY27 capex is only about Rs.30-35 crore and FY28 capex of about Rs.75-80 crore is already planned, with CDC investment finished and no further CDC investment planned; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.why: Management could benefit if raw material and geopolitical conditions ease, which would add about 0.5% to the 43% gross margin, but the guide is held rather than raised.

rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed in the call.

rows.label: Net debt peak and inventory unwind
rows.why: Net debt of Rs.911 crore at September 30, 2026 is expected to be the peak, with inventory reduction starting October 2026 and insurance claim settlement expected by March 2027.

rows.why: Operations moved to subsidiaries KFG and KFL after the fire, so standalone margins are not representative and are expected to recover once operations move back, with Mulund transition in FY28.

539523|2026-03.headline: Alkem Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14.6% YoY to INR36,033 million and FY26 EBITDA crossed INR3,000 crore, with management guiding FY27 margins to 20-21%.
539523|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR36,033 million (+14.6% YoY), with India sales up 8.8% to INR23,245 million and international sales up 25.4% to INR12,223 million. Q4 EBITDA was INR5,174 million at a 14.4% margin, and FY26 EBITDA grew 32.2% YoY per management, with a 20.4% full-year margin. Q4 net profit was INR2,365 million after exceptional items of INR602.7 million (labour code gratuity/leave liability) and INR747 million (real estate impairment). Management flagged rising logistics, API and packaging costs from geopolitical disruption, and announced that CEO Dr. Vikas Gupta is leaving; a new CEO search is underway.

financial_highlights.change: Margin up from 12.4% in Q4 FY25 (as stated)

financial_highlights.value: INR3,052 million per slide (management also said crossed INR3,000 crore); margin 20.4%
financial_highlights.change: Margin up from 19.4% in FY25; EBITDA +19.6% YoY (stated), +32.2% (stated for Q4 context)

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 India sales grew 8.8% YoY to INR23,245 million; management said branded generics grew close to 10%. IQVIA shows Q4 growth of 11.1% vs IPM ~10%, with chronic +16.1% vs IPM 13.6% and acute +10% vs IPM 7.7%.

segments.name: International (US and ROW)
segments.commentary: Q4 international sales rose 25.4% YoY to INR12,223 million; FY26 international sales were INR4,610 million (+22.5%). Management did not split US and ROW figures for the quarter.

segments.name: Trade generics
segments.commentary: FY26 trade generics growth was about 4.3% on an annualised basis after the carve-out into a separate entity; management is prioritising margin over top-line.

segments.name: Enzene (CDMO/biologics)
segments.commentary: Enzene India is at a high-teens EBITDA margin; Enzene US is loss-making during ramp-up and the group is not expected to be EBITDA positive this year. US CDMO revenue was under INR100 crore last year.

segments.name: Medtech (Occlutech)
segments.commentary: Medtech contributes less than 1% of revenue today. Occlutech acquisition expected to close in 45-60 days.

guidance_outlook: India: grow 100-150 bps above the market; with the market growing ~9-10%, management called double-digit growth the target.
US (dollar terms): high single-digit growth on pharma, plus forex gain and new launches; Tolvaptan launch expected around Sep/Oct 2026 with limited competition.
ROW: higher-teens growth assumed for FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin: 20-21% range (like-to-like), subject to geopolitical and cost clarity; management said it will know more by H2 or Q3.
R&D spend expected at 4-5% of revenue annually; Q4 runs higher (6-6.5%) because of filing cycle.
Other expenses expected to rise 7-8% in FY27, excluding the Occlutech acquisition.
Tax rate guided down to 27-29% from FY27 after moving to the new tax regime from April 2026 (previously 35-38%).
Dividend: 25-30% of PAT currently; management does not foresee a major cut in absolute dividend, so the payout ratio will rise as PAT rises.
capex_capacity: Enzene US biologics plant recently commissioned; ramp-up ongoing, no clear evidence yet of onetime asset turnover from US in-sourcing trend.
No further acquisitions planned for at least 12 months; Occlutech integration into Alkem MedTech expected to take about 12 months after closing.
Denosumab (Prolia/Xgeva) biosimilar under US FDA review; US launch not expected this year, possibly out-licensed.
Semaglutide: injectable approved and launched in India in March 2026; oral tablet in clinical trials; US filing planned in about 1.5 years.
demand_pricing: Q4 chronic branded generic growth 16.1% vs IPM 13.6%; outperformed in 6 key therapies: GI, vitamins and minerals, pain, antidiabetic, respiratory and dermatology.
Chronic is about 22% of India branded generics, up roughly 1 percentage point a year over 3-4 years.
Semaglutide launched day 1 in March 2026; about 11% unit market share in the latest IQVIA report.
Anti-infective market (oral liquids and injectables) remains muted; management said Alkem's acute growth is still high single-digit.
Domestic field force around 14,500 MRs at group level; attrition 18-19%.
Geopolitical environment has raised logistics, API and packaging costs; management hedges 80% of forex exposure and buys API and packaging inventory on price dips.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for India growth and the margin path given cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: India is targeted at 100-150 bps above the market; FY26 margin of 20.4% is the baseline and FY27 is seen at 20-21%, with 100 bps annual expansion now a moving target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Occlutech deal timing and the impact on numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Deal expected to close in 45-60 days; if it closes, Q2 FY27 would carry a full quarter impact. Medtech is under 1% of revenue today.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Denosumab biosimilar timeline in the US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: US approval is possibly by Q1 CY27 subject to inspection; no launch this year. Europe has one partner for the Prolia biosimilar; the Xgeva version has no partner yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CEO succession and CXO plan?
qa_highlights.answer: A new CEO will be hired from top global candidates, taking a few months. Non-pharma group businesses (Occlutech, Enzene) report to other promoters or the MD.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Tolvaptan launch and expected contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch expected around September or October 2026 as a limited-player launch, so contribution comes in H2 FY27; base US business faces value erosion.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for dividend and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend is 25-30% of PAT; absolute payout is expected to be maintained, so the payout percentage will rise after the tax reset. No acquisitions for 12 months.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (API, packaging, logistics) from geopolitical disruption; management will not quantify Q1 FY27 impact.
Management transition: Dr. Vikas Gupta departing; CEO search in progress and may take a few months.
Denosumab US approval and Europe partnering timing; Tolvaptan launch in Sep/Oct 2026.
Trade generics receivables risk and weak growth in FY26 (about 4.3%).

539524|2026-03.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16.6% to Rs 703 crore; FY27 guided to early-to-mid-teens growth and 27-28% margins.

FY26 revenue grew 12.2% to Rs 2,763 crore with a 27.2% EBITDA margin, and the Board approved a final dividend of Rs 4 per share. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to early-to-mid-teens and margins to 27-28%, while stepping up spending on labs, infrastructure and A&P.

Combined insurance and clinic losses narrowed to about INR22 crore from about INR33 crore last quarter. The UK business showed a revenue dip QoQ and no margin benefit yet from cost synergies, while Cayman insurance losses fell to $1.1 million from $3.7 million.

qa_highlights.question: When will insurance losses/combined ratio improve and will the company give up on insurance?

qa_highlights.question: Why is India IP footfall flat at about 60,000 for several quarters?

qa_highlights.question: Is UK going as planned and what is the path to revenue recovery?

539607|2026-03.headline: Blue Cloud guides FY27 revenue of Rs 3,000 crore on a confirmed order book of about Rs 1,100 crore; Q4 margin rose to 17% from 12%.
539607|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 top line landed in line with plan, and Q4 gross margin expansion (reported margin up from 12% to 17% quarter on quarter, per an analyst) was attributed to productised SaaS and subscription revenue after about two and a half years of R&D. Management reiterated the Rs 3,000 crore FY27 revenue guidance and about 30% growth thereafter, but the call gave no quarterly split and the gap between the confirmed order book and guidance was left to organic and inorganic pipeline. Working capital was a visible weak spot: receivables spiked at 31 March 2026 and the current ratio was estimated by an analyst at about 1, which management expects to ease from the next quarter. The AIS Anywhere business is being moved from customised delivery to a SaaS model, which management said may reduce near-term revenue volume.

qa_highlights.question: Is the top-line growth guidance of 40-50% still valid?

qa_highlights.question: Why has order inflow been slower than on-ground wind activity?

qa_highlights.question: Current IPP portfolio and expansion plans?

539686|2026-09.headline: K.P. Energy Q2 FY27 total income rose about 78% YoY to Rs 540 crore, but margin compressed to about 12% and management guides it to persist for 2-4 quarters.
539686|2026-09.overview: Consolidated total income for Q2 FY27 was about Rs 540 crore versus Rs 303 crore in Q2 FY26, with development (EPC) revenue at about Rs 527 crore. Profit after tax was Rs 26.92 crore, up slightly from Rs 26.08 crore in Q1 FY27, but H1 PAT fell to Rs 53.22 crore from Rs 61.37 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to labour cost and idling, right-of-way delays, crane availability, and raw material costs, and said margins would stay at current levels for 2 to 4 quarters. The order book stood at about 1.64 GW worth about Rs 1,940 crore as on 30 September 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited labour volatility and idling, ROW delays across multiple locations, crane availability and raw material costs; no quantified cost split was given.

539725|2026-09.headline: Gokul Agro Q2 FY27 revenue up 13% to INR7,481 crore; EBITDA up 41% to INR276 crore with margin at 3.68%.
539725|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 13% YoY to INR7,481 crore, with EBITDA including other income up 41% to INR276 crore and margin up about 74 bps to 3.68%. PAT rose 40% to INR150 crore, and H1 PAT grew 54% to INR274 crore on 10% revenue growth. Management attributed the growth mainly to better price realisations, with no volume growth expected this year as capacity is fully utilised. A 24 September 2026 change in edible oil import duties deferred trade purchases in September, lifting closing inventory, which management called a timing effect. This was the company's first earnings call, held to start a regular investor engagement.

segments.name: Edible oils
segments.commentary: About 85% of H1 FY27 consolidated volume; palm and soybean are the largest categories, with sunflower, mustard, groundnut, cottonseed, rice bran and vanaspati also sold.

segments.name: Biodiesel
segments.commentary: 300 TPD Gandhidham plant fully operational in Q1 FY27 and ISCC certified; revenue INR237 crore in Q2 and INR596 crore in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Castor derivatives
segments.commentary: Castor oil plus 12-HSA, hydrogenated castor oil and ricinoleic acid; no separate financials disclosed.

segments.name: Specialty fats
segments.commentary: Richfield, Pride, Biscopride, Chocosil and Rich Chef; described as a smaller share of volumes, with no figures given.

segments.name: Channel mix (H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: B2B 79%, exports 13% (33 countries), B2C 8% of channel revenue, up from about 5-6% in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 10% expected next year, then 10% to 15% per year thereafter, at current commodity prices.
EBITDA margin expected to stay in a 3.5% to 4% range, with absolute EBITDA growing accordingly.
Capacity additions across four plants, about 8 lakh tonnes per annum, operational only by October 2027.
B2C marketing spend earmarked at under INR25 crore, to be spent gradually; B2C margins expected to be broadly in line with consolidated, with no large near-term expansion.
Next earnings calls to follow half-year and full-year results.
capex_capacity: Existing capacity: Gandhidham about 3,400 TPD refining, 3,200 TPD seed crushing and 300 TPD biodiesel; Krishnapatnam about 1,400 TPD refining; Haldia about 1,350 TPD refining; Mangalore facility (capacity not stated).
Capacity expansion of about 8 lakh tonnes per annum across the four manufacturing locations, with full operation expected by October 2027.
15 MW captive solar plant commissioned in Gujarat in Q1 FY27; further 4 MW Andhra Pradesh, 4 MW Karnataka and 10 MW Gujarat planned.
Oil palm: about 550 hectares completed in FY25-26, with 900 hectares under development for completion in FY27; current output about 1,000 tonnes per annum, under 1% of requirement.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the 13% Q2 revenue growth mainly to better price realisations; commodity prices rose 15% to 20%, and realisations track market prices.
Edible oil import duties revised effective 24 September 2026; trade deferred purchases in September, raising closing inventory. Management views this as temporary, with channel activity normalising.
Hedging: inventory largely sold through back-to-back physical forwards or hedged on CBOT and Malaysian exchanges; import payments hedged via forwards; open inventory held at 10% to 15%.

About 80% of raw material is imported. Stock-in-trade purchases rose to INR2,000 crore in Q2 from INR491 crore in Q1; management said trading sales are usually 10% to 20% of volume and under 15% in H1.
Distribution spans more than 650 dealers and distributors across 28 states and UTs, with a new Jammu and Kashmir depot and Vitalife push in Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat and Karnataka.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue growth came from volume, price and new businesses such as biodiesel?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was driven mainly by better price realisations. Volume growth is not expected this year because capacity is fully utilised; new capex is underway.

qa_highlights.question: Is the roughly 3.5% margin sustainable, or does it include inventory or forex gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable, citing branding, value-added mix, better utilisation, smarter sourcing and cost control, with no mention of inventory or forex gains.

qa_highlights.question: How is the business insulated from edible oil price and forex volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is back-to-back sold or hedged, import payments are forward-hedged, and open inventory is held at 10% to 15%. No derivatives are used for forex.

qa_highlights.question: What volume and EBITDA growth is expected over the next three years from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 10% next year and 10% to 15% annually after that, with EBITDA margin at 3.5% to 4%; capacity arrives by October 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are per-tonne realisations and EBITDA by product, and what are B2C margins and spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Product-wise realisations and EBITDA per tonne were not disclosed. B2C margins are roughly in line with consolidated 3.5%, with marketing spend under INR25 crore and FY26 spend not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did stock-in-trade purchases rise to INR2,000 crore in Q2, and what is the scale of palm plantation backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports are about 80% of raw material, with surplus vessel quantities sold outright; trading sales are typically under 15%. Palm output is about 1,000 tonnes per annum, under 1% of requirement, with benefits 3 to 4 years away.

539730|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR213 crore (up 27.27% YoY), EBITDA INR29.13 crore (up 67.05%, margin 13.67%, +326 bps) and net profit INR11.07 crore (up 56.47%). Management guided to 25-30% top-line growth for FY27 and said margins will keep rising for about 8 quarters before a spike. Working capital and finance cost were the main investor concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant onboarding traction on PayCentral and whether MDR is an opportunity or a threat given a 8-10% share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PayCentral is early, with the Indian protocol working well and international growth faster. It said MDR is positive but not finalised, and the company sees no consolidation threat on the acquiring side.

qa_highlights.question: Why EBITDA rose while net revenue fell, and should investors focus on net or gross revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investors should focus on net revenue, and the EBITDA increase came from lower expenses. The CFO said EBITDA rose 41% YoY and margin moved from 47% to 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EPS guidance flat when PAT margin is about 57%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will protect core earnings and reinvest incremental accruals into AI, transaction intelligence and new revenue streams. It said the 2027–2029 ambition is a strong earnings base plus a large AI-led business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI infrastructure plan and the expected returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management ruled out large data-centre capex. It is focused on transaction intelligence scores, financial behaviour graphs and SLM application layers, which it said LLMs cannot replicate because they lack the data.

qa_highlights.question: Top-5 client concentration and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the strategy is to go horizontal with a larger merchant base, and that international focus is on larger clients. It did not give a top-5 revenue share.

539807|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 71% to INR5,560 crores, but Q2 PAT grew only 6% to INR72 crores as net take rate fell about 4% QoQ to 5.06 bps.

539871|2026-03.headline: Thyrocare FY26 consolidated revenue rose 21% to INR829 crore and Q4 PAT rose 128% to INR48.7 crore; management guides mid-to-high teens growth in FY27.

Partnership growth slowed to 23% in Q4 from 32% for the year, which management attributed to a one-off INR4 crore Kumbh-camp base effect and insurance pricing normalisation. Management said test volumes were boosted by biochemistry price cuts in the quarter, and it is launching specialty (allergy, genomics) and an allied consumables brand.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 900 franchisee addition sustainable and what is the Q1 PAT for radiology?
qa_highlights.answer: Adds reflect the enlarged sales team and branded stores; radiology Q1 PAT was about INR1.72 crores, with about INR6 crores expected for FY27.

risks_watch: Franchisee churn: management said not all 900 Q1 additions may remain by year-end, and the Q2 base is high (Q2 FY26 revenue about INR200 crores).

Parent-level debt: API Group debt reduced to about INR1,050 crores from INR1,700 crores; promoter holding is pledged. IPO or reverse merger is not planned and is at least 12 months away, per management.
Specialty execution risk: the segment is at a nascent stage, prescription-driven, and not yet scaled. Management has not set doctor coverage targets.
Aarogyam growth (21%) trails non-Aarogyam tests, so mix shift could dilute per-test realisation.
Consumables announcement expected by September 2026; details unknown.
Radiology divestment: no buyer identified; contribution is small (about INR6 crores PAT expected for FY27).
539871|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operations and growth, with pathology up 26%, franchisees at a record and margins expanding. Cautious and evasive on forward guidance: management declined to revise franchisee or growth guidance until H1, and gave no specialty targets or dividend guidance.
key_quotes: I'm proud to say that after a strong growth of 20% in FY26, in Q1 FY27, our pathology business has grown even faster at 26%.
So, it's too early for me to revise guidance. I will still hold to the mid to high teens guidance at this point in time.
I think API will consider an IPO when it is profitable ex-Thyrocare, as well as debt free.
Test number is like-for-like and all numbers in the book are like to like.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin expanded more than 290 bps to 74.1% and EBITDA margin reached 32.2% on better negotiations, 28% task volume growth and operating efficiency, though specialty margins are guided broadly in line with current EBITDA margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three new labs opened in Q1 (Muzaffarpur, Kurnool, Prayagraj) on a 43-lab India network, and specialty capex is largely done in Mumbai and Delhi, but no further lab or capacity additions beyond these were quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pathology grew about 26% YoY with task volume up 28%, franchisees at about 11,700 after 900 Q1 adds, and franchisee growth guided at mid-to-high teens for FY27, though Q2 faces a high base (about INR200 crores) and churn risk.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said significant specialty capex is not expected next year beyond expansion capex if volumes exceed plan, and no new large capex was announced against INR250+ crores already invested.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held mid-to-high teens franchisee growth and declined to revise guidance until H1, with no upgrade signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 franchisee adds of about 900 may not all persist given churn risk, Q3 adds are nil, and Q2 revenue base is high at about INR200 crores.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Specialty diagnostics commercially went live in Q1 FY27 with allergy (Phadia) and genomics, over 20 specialised tests added, and a Thyrocare-branded consumables announcement is expected by September 2026.

rows.label: Specialty diagnostics ramp (allergy and genomics)
rows.why: Specialty is under 1% of about 5.5 crore tests today, with a 15-20% portfolio ambition in 3-5 years, but no doctor coverage target is set and execution is nascent.

rows.label: Radiology (nuclear) divestment
rows.why: Management is pursuing a sale of the nuclear business against about INR140 crores invested, with Q1 radiology PAT of about INR1.72 crores and about INR6 crores guided for FY27, but no buyer is identified yet.

rows.label: API Group parent debt reduction
rows.why: Parent debt has fallen to about INR1,050 crores from INR1,700 crores, though promoter holding is pledged and IPO or reverse merger is at least 12 months away.

tone.note: Management was confident on pathology growth (26%), record franchisees and margin expansion, but cautious on forward guidance, declining to revise franchisee or growth guidance until H1 and giving no specialty targets or dividend guidance; analysts pressed on the sustainability of the 900 franchisee
